chapters.title: Chapter 4348 WONDER IV
paragraphs: The effect was immediate and magisterial!

Across the Early Veiled Shore, every being who had been meditating, who had been arduously working to forge their own Mana Glyphs through effort and concentration and time, suddenly felt their existence buzz with unfamiliar sensation.
Power.
Not a trickle. Not a stream. A fucking ocean of it, flooding into them from sources they couldn't identify, filling reservoirs they hadn't known they possessed.
HUUM!

The Emperor Penguin, who had been struggling to maintain three Mana Glyphs simultaneously, suddenly felt the burden vanish. Its reserves exploded outward, allowing it to forge a fourth, then a fifth, then a sixth with speed that should have been impossible.

Kazuhiko, momentarily holding Erikson's slipper with practiced ease, gasped as energy cascaded through him in waves that never ended. He began layering Mana Glyphs with complexity he'd only theorized about before, each one snapping into place with perfection that came from unlimited resources!

Adelaide, her snow-blue hair now radiating auroras of pure power, laughed with delight as she felt limitations she'd always accepted as fundamental simply... cease to exist. She could create. She could destroy. She could reshape and rebuild without ever worrying about running dry!
Across the Shore, similar reactions rippled through Noah's people.
Those who had been taking careful, measured steps in their cultivation suddenly found themselves sprinting.
Those who had accepted their limitations as permanent learned that their Master had decided otherwise!
For the first time, Noah's people got to experience a semblance of what he always felt.
That infinite wellspring of power that never ran dry, never diminished, never left him wanting!
And even this semblance...this fraction of what Noah himself possessed, was far too grand for words.
Many processed it with shock.
Others simply sat in stunned silence, trying to process the magnitude of the gift they'd been given.
A few, like the Emperor Penguin, immediately began pushing their new limits with enthusiasm that bordered on reckless!
"RAA!"
Noah watched it all with satisfaction.
This...giving power to those who followed him, elevating his people beyond their limitations...was this what building a Civilization meant?
Not conquest. Not domination.
Uplift!
He watched the wonder unfold with majesty before he sighed.
Because he wasn't done yet. Not even close.
"RUINEDEN," he called out again, his voice carrying renewed purpose. "Activate Parallel Processing Architectures. I want to run multiple probability streams simultaneously."
RUIN/EDEN's form brightened with something that might have been excitement.

"Yes, Master. This will require more resources. Parallel Processing at the level you're requesting, running complete phantom processes that explore different choices and feed results back to you, requires 10 Mana Glyphs of the Cheating Architect operating in perfect synchronization."
More prompts cascaded across Noah's vision.
|PARALLEL PROCESSING ARCHITECTURES - INITIALIZATION|
|Designating 10 Mana Glyphs for probability stream management|
|Remaining Available Glyphs: 63 (78 total minus 5 for Existence Code Injection minus 10 for Parallel Processing)|
|Note: Each active probability stream consumes substantial resources. Recommend limiting simultaneous streams to 3-5 for optimal stability.|
"I want to see three scenarios," Noah commanded, his tone carrying calculation that suggested he'd already been considering these options.

"First: What happens if I send a body across to the other side of The Veil. Second: What happens if I pursue other Doorways to THE Loom. Third: What happens if I wait for Justiciars to appear and follow Schrodinger's plan to track them back to their source."
RUINEDEN nodded, her expression growing more serious as she processed the request.
"Running probability calculations now," she said. "Be advised: These scenarios involve entities and forces far beyond current power scales. The outcomes may be... concerning."
HUUM!

Three illusory diagrams materialized in the air before Noah, each one showing a different branching path of possibility. They were ghostly, semi-transparent, depicting futures that hadn't happened yet but could depending on his choices.
The first diagram pulsed with crimson light, and RUINEDEN's voice took on grim tones as she detailed what it showed.
"Scenario One: Crossing to the other side of The Veil."
The diagram showed Noah's form stepping through that barrier between The Living and The Dead, passing from one fundamental state of existence to another.
And immediately, catastrophically, things went wrong.

"The moment you cross," RUINEDEN explained, her voice clinical despite the horror of what she was describing, "THE Dead Order senses your presence. Not just senses, she knows. Instantly and completely. Your existence becomes visible to her with perfect clarity because you've entered her domain, where her authority is absolute despite her limitations."
The diagram showed a massive figure...feminine, impossibly powerful, radiating authority that made THE Living Order look like a candle before a star...focusing attention on Noah's infinitesimal form.

"THE Dead Order, even in her current limited state, possesses power that operates on the next Scale of Existence," RUIN/EDEN continued. "She forcefully controls all aspects of your being. Your resistance is irrelevant. Your power is insufficient. Your Principles are bypassed because she operates on a level where your defenses don't exist yet."
The diagram shifted, showing Noah's Early Veiled Shore being pulled across The Veil through connections he couldn't sever.

"She uses you as an anchor to drag The Infiniverse to the other side of The Veil," RUINEDEN said, her tone carrying something that might have been concern. "The entire Early Veiled Shore, all beings within it, everything you've built...all of it crosses to where The Dead dwell."
The next part of the diagram made Noah's expression harden.

"Once she has The Infiniverse on her side, she immediately locates THE Living Order, Sigrid, and captures her. The fusion of THE Living and THE Dead Order begins immediately. The two halves of a fundamental force reunite, and in doing so, erase the limitations that kept THE Dead Order bound."
WAA!
The diagram showed Sigrid screaming as she was absorbed into that impossibly vast presence, two aspects of Order merging into something that transcended both.
"The unified Order entity gains the ability to cross The Veil freely," RUIN/EDEN continued. "She is no longer bound to either side. She is Order Absolute, operating without restriction."
But the horror didn't stop there.

"The unified Order then locates and devours Khor," RUINEDEN said, the diagram showing The First Hunger being consumed despite her power and mystery. "She strips away Khor's secrets, her knowledge, her connection to the higher Scale of Existence. All of it becomes fuel for Order's expansion."
The diagram shifted again, showing THE Dead- no, the Unified Order...examining the workings of The Infiniverse with interest.

"She discovers your Way of the Mana Architect," RUINEDEN said quietly. "She understands what makes you unique. And instead of eliminating you as a threat... she repurposes you. You become a battery for her new Civilization. Your Infinite Mana, your Perpetual Harvest, your Cheating Architect...all of it locked into service of Order Absolute, generating power for her purposes while you exist as a conscious prisoner unable to act, unable to resist, unable to do anything except provide energy for eternity."
The diagram faded, leaving only the implications hanging in the air like smoke after an explosion!

chapters.title: Chapter 4349: ERROR I
paragraphs: Noah’s expression had grown heavy, his eyes carrying darkness that suggested he was imagining exactly what that existence would feel like.
Conscious. Aware. Powerful. And completely, utterly helpless as his own strength was used to fuel purposes he didn’t choose.
It was a fate worse than death because death would at least be final.
His internal weavings ran in circles of calculation and fury.
So that’s what happens if he crossed The Veil prematurely!
THE Dead Order just... wins. Immediately and completely.
No fight or negotiation.
The thought was sobering.
He’d faced dangers before. He’d battled beings whose power exceeded his. He’d survived situations that should have been fatal through combination of luck, skill, and absurd cheating.
But this?
This was encountering a being who operated on a Scale of Existence where his tricks didn’t matter, where his power was irrelevant, where resistance itself was a concept that didn’t apply.
Noah took a breath, then spoke with calm.
“Show me the other scenarios.”
RUINEDEN nodded, and the second diagram pulsed with different energy...less immediately catastrophic but carrying its own breed of horror.
“Scenario Two: Pursuing other Doorways to THE Loom.”
The diagram showed Noah moving through the Transcendent Folds, seeking those mysterious passages that supposedly led to THE Loom where answers and power awaited.

“Result: Nearly all Doorways you encounter are collapsed,” RUINEDEN reported, her tone carrying clinical assessment. “The collapse isn’t natural...they’ve been deliberately sealed. And attached to the walls near each collapsed Doorway, you find Inevitabilities fused to the structure like living locks.”
The diagram showed grotesque images of Inevitabilities merged with reality itself, their forms twisted and repurposed into security systems.
“Similar to the exterior wall where you encountered the Lodestone attached,” RUINEDEN continued. “These Inevitabilities have been sucked in entirely.”
The diagram shifted, showing Noah moving from one collapsed Doorway to another, finding the same result repeatedly.

“However,” RUINEDEN added, and the diagram brightened slightly, “probability calculations suggest that some Doorways may still exist in uncollapsed states. The locations are unknown. The number is uncertain. But statistical analysis indicates they haven’t all been sealed.”
She paused.
“Finding them would require extensive searching across multiple Folds. This path is possible but inefficient path.”
Noah nodded slowly, processing that information. So THE Loom was being actively defended, sealed off, made inaccessible after his actions woth the Lodestone.
Which meant it was probably worth reaching.
“And the third scenario?”
The final diagram pulsed with colors that suggested imminent violence and complicated planning.
“Scenario Three: Waiting for another Justiciar and following Schrodinger’s plan.”
The diagram showed the Transcendent Quantum Folds, and within them, the emergence of another of those terrifying Living Existential Armors....a Justiciar performing its ritual of collapse.

“Probability calculations indicate high likelihood of Justiciar manifestation in the Transcendent Quantum Folds within the next few hours,” RUINEDEN reported. “If you, Schrodinger, and Leonore Rureaux interrupt its ritual, attempting to capture or interrogate it...”
The diagram showed Leonore Rureaux engaging the Justiciar, her power overwhelming it.

“...A dozen more Justiciars manifest immediately,” RUINEDEN continued, her tone darkening. “They arrive in response to the first one’s distress signal. When they assess the situation and determine they cannot win against your combined forces...”
The diagram showed all thirteen Justiciars simultaneously detonating, their forms erupting in explosions of anti-existence that would collapse the entire region.
“...They self-destruct,” RUINEDEN finished. “Complete existential annihilation. No bodies to examine. No trail to follow. Just devastation and lost opportunity.”
Noah’s eyes narrowed. “And if we don’t interrupt?”

“If you allow the Justiciar to complete its ritual,” RUINEDEN said, and the diagram shifted to show a different outcome, “it collapses the entire region of Transcendent Quantum Folds as intended. Countless Sextillions of Fold Dwellers and Living Existences perish. An entire section of existence becomes carved in white fires of purity. More fear spreads.”
The diagram showed the Justiciar completing its work, then departing.

“After completing the collapse, the Justiciar returns to wherever it came from,” RUINEDEN continued. “If you follow it without engaging, maintaining concealment and distance, probability suggests you could track it back to its source.”
She paused, her expression growing grave.

None of them were good.
None of them were safe.
None of them promised outcomes he could accept!

It wasn’t a pleasant smile. It wasn’t the kind of expression that suggested he’d found a solution everyone would be happy with.
It was the smile of someone who had just decided that none of the options presented were acceptable, so he would create his own option instead.

His eyes blazed brighter.
“But I have the Cheating Architect. I have Perpetual Harvest. I have access to the Earliest Folds and knowledge of how existence was structured before it learned to defend itself.”
He gestured broadly, encompassing all the possibilities that existed beyond the three scenarios.
“So instead of choosing between bad options, I’m going to create a fourth option.”

The future was uncertain.
The dangers were real and immediate.
But he had never been particularly concerned with doing things the expected way.
Why start now?
A few possibilities bloomed in his mind as he moved on!

RUIN/EDEN’s holographic form brightened immediately.

|Entry #2: Principle of Absolute Consumption (Source: Commander Tatiana)|
|Classification: Harvesting/Predation Type|
|Core Function: Converts all defeated entities into pure fuel for exponential power growth|
|Decompilation Status: 73% Complete|

|Notes: Architecture is surprisingly elegant despite its brutality. The conversion efficiency scales based on the victim’s final emotional state- fear and despair provide higher yields. Fascinating and horrifying in equal measure.|
The interface shifted again, highlighting another entry.
|Entry #3: Principle of Endless Hunger (Source: Prime Dead Early Creature - Valerius the Insatiable)|
|Classification: Consumption/Amplification Type|
|Core Function: Transforms metabolic processes into existential expansion- literally grows stronger through eating|
|Decompilation Status: 81% Complete|

|Notes: Less sophisticated than Tatiana’s approach but more stable. This Principle doesn’t cannibalize the user’s sanity as payment for power. Trade-off is lower peak efficiency but sustainable operation. Practical. Trying to be an Inevitability?|
Another entry bloomed with crimson-gold light.
|Entry #4: Principle of Dominion Through Death (Source: Prime Dead Early Creature - Moros the Inevitable End)|
|Classification: Authority/Subjugation Type|
|Core Function: Establishes hierarchical control over anything that has experienced death or near-death|
|Decompilation Status: 67% Complete|
RUINEDEN’s expression grew more analytical.
The interface expanded further, revealing more entries.
|Entry #5: Principle of Exponential Decay (Source: Prime Dead Early Creature - Nyx the Withering)|
|Classification: Entropy/Time Manipulation Type|
|Core Function: Accelerates aging and degradation of targeted entities and concepts|
|Decompilation Status: 79% Complete|
|Entry #6: Principle of Parasitic Unity (Source: Prime Dead Early Creature - Typhon the Many-Formed)|
|Classification: Symbiosis/Absorption Type|

|Decompilation Status: 71% Complete|

paragraphs: As he looked at them, the interface shifted dramatically, the entries suddenly blazing with verdant-gold light that made the previous ones look dim by comparison.
|Entry #7-15: Principle Collection (Source: Elyndra Viltharion, Scion of the First Harvest)|
|Classification: Agricultural/Growth/Authority Types|
|WARNING: Extreme Complexity Detected|

“And now we get to the really impressive acquisition,” RUINEDEN said, her voice carrying notes of genuine excitement mixed with professional frustration. “The nine Principles operating in harmony within The First Farmer’s daughter.”
She gestured, and the interface zoomed in on those entries, revealing complexity that made the previous ones look like children’s toys.
|Principle of Eternal Growth|
|Decompilation Status: 23% Complete|
|Estimated Time to Full Analysis: ???|
|Principle of Cyclical Harvest|
|Decompilation Status: 31% Complete|
|Estimated Time to Full Analysis: ???|
|Principle of Fertile Abundance|
|Decompilation Status: 28% Complete|
|Estimated Time to Full Analysis:???|
The list continued, each one showing frustratingly low completion percentages.

“Elyndra’s Principles aren’t just powerful individually- they’re architected to function as a unified system. Each one supports and amplifies the others. It is...genuinely brilliant. It should be the handiwork of The First Farmer.”

She pulled up a diagram showing how the nine Principles interconnected, creating a web of mutual support that resembled less a collection of separate abilities and more a single organism with nine major organs.

“The problem,” RUINEDEN continued, “is that decompiling them requires understanding not just each Principle individually, but also how they interface with each other. It’s like trying to understand a symphony by analyzing each instrument separately...you miss the composition that makes the whole greater than the sum of parts.”
Her expression grew more determined.

“I’m working on it, Master. The Cheating Architect is throwing substantial processing power at breaking down these architectures. But this isn’t something I can rush without risking corruption of the final product. Unless you can...get close and personal with the Daughter of The First Farmer. When these are ready for you to download...” she smiled, “...you’ll be able to either augment your current Principles with their capabilities or combine them to create new Agent Architects that operate under The Cheating Architect.”
HUUM!
Noah nodded slowly.
The Repository was working as intended!
It was patient power accumulation. Not immediate, but inevitable.

The Cheating Architect was essentially telling him that every being he met, every Principle he observed, would eventually become part of his arsenal. Not through theft or consumption, but through analysis and replication.
“Keep working on them,” he said finally, his tone carrying approval.
Noah’s attention shifted, moving to the next capability he wanted to test.
“What about Debug Mode?” he asked, his voice carrying curiosity. “Have we encountered any errors in existence that we can exploit?”
RUINEDEN’s expression brightened once more.

“Debug Mode is... interesting,” she said carefully. “It requires existence to malfunction in detectable ways before we can exploit those malfunctions. So far, we haven’t observed any significant errors in the fabric of reality around us.”
She paused.

“The Dead are functioning as intended- horrifyingly, but without technical errors. The Living Existences we’ve encountered operate within normal parameters. Even the chaos of the Wandering Territories isn’t actually erroneous...it’s just chaotic by design.”
Her expression grew more thoughtful.
“The Living or Dead Existential Armors might potentially be a source of exploitable errors,” she continued, her tone speculative.
She made a note in the air, her gestures creating persistent text that hung like promises.
“I’ll monitor for anomalies and alert you immediately if anything significant appears,” she said. “Debug Mode is incredibly powerful when applicable, but it requires the right circumstances.”

“However,” she said, drawing out the word with emphasis that made it clear something important was coming, “there is one possible error I’ve detected. Actually, it’s less ‘possible’ and more ‘definitely present and significantly impacting your development.'”
Noah’s eyes sharpened. “Where?”
RUINEDEN’s smile took on ironic qualities.
“Within your own existence, Master. Which is actually perfect timing, because I can better explain it if we jump onto the feature of the Development Console as well. Shall we?”
Noah felt his interest spike. An error in his own existence?
“Utilize the feature of Development Console,” he commanded.
WAA!
The response was spectacular.
The space around Noah transformed. The golden sands beneath his feet shifted, becoming a platform of blue-gold energy that pulsed with analytical authority.
RUINEDEN’s holographic form expanded, becoming more detailed, more present, as if she was drawing additional processing power from the activated Console.
“Development Console is now active,” she announced, her voice carrying satisfaction at finally being able to demonstrate this capability properly. “Accessing your existential parameters now.”
An illusory diagram materialized in the air before Noah...a perfect three-dimensional representation of himself, every detail rendered with impossible precision.
It wasn’t just his physical form.

The diagram showed layers upon layers of existential architecture...his Mana Glyphs arranged in geometric perfection, his Principles glowing like internal suns, his Early Veiled Shore existing as a pocket dimension attached to his core being, his consciousness branching across multiple bodies simultaneously.
It was beautiful!
Text began appearing around the diagram, displaying his current parameters with clinical precision.
|DEVELOPMENT CONSOLE - EXISTENTIAL PARAMETERS|
|NAME: Noah Osmont|
|CLASSIFICATION: The Early Creature (Authenticity: 127% - Exceeds baseline parameters)|
|COMPLEXITY: (3.89 Quintillion)|
|PURITY: (3.89 Quintillion)|
|ACTIVE MANA GLYPHS OF THE CHEATING ARCHITECT: 78 Total|
|—Dedicated to Existence Code Injection: 5|
|—Dedicated to Parallel Processing: 10|
|—Available for General Use: 63|
|—Per-Glyph Contribution: 10 Quadrillion Complexity, 10 Quadrillion Purity|
|PRINCIPLES:|
|—Perpetual Harvest (Maturity: Complete)|
|—Cheating Architect (Maturity: Complete)|
|—Additional Principle Signatures Detected: [DATA INTEGRATING]|
|EARLY VEILED SHORE STATUS: Operational, Expanding|
Countless details filled up the screen!
Noah studied the readout calmly.
The numbers were impressive...nearly 4 Quintillion in both major parameters, with substantial additional power from the Mana Glyphs.
He’d come a long way from the Fold Dweller who had started this journey in the Nullvein Gravewake Folds fighting Little Bobby within a Wheel of Existence just...oh, was it days ago?
“Hmm...” He wanted to be content at such an accomplishment, but there was still much to be done!
And RUINEDEN continued.
“Now, let’s look at the more interesting architectural components,” she said, and the diagram zoomed inward, focusing on specific areas of Noah’s existence.
The view shifted to show structures that resembled impossible castles made of compressed authority and crystallized will.
|RESPLENDENT CITADELS OF THE MANA ARCHITECT|
|Current Stage: Fourth (Advancing toward Fifth)|
|Function: Foundational architecture supporting Way of Existence|
|Status: Shining brightly as beacons of cultivated power|
|Note: Advancement to Fifth Stage progressing naturally through accumulated effort and understanding|
“Your Citadels are advancing beautifully, not much can be said about them currently.” RUINEDEN observed.
The diagram shifted again, this time focusing on something that made Noah’s attention sharpen immediately.
His Heart.

Not a mere physical heart...that mundane organ that pumped blood through flesh. This was his Heart of an Early Creature, the core component that defined what he was becoming, the architectural centerpiece that separated genuine Early Creatures from beings merely pretending at that scale of power!
The diagram showed it in exquisite detail.
Four components were complete, each one blazing with different aspects of authority:
|HEART OF AN EARLY CREATURE - CURRENT STATUS|
|Component 1: Ventryalis - The Primal Root Atrium of Echoes (COMPLETE)|
|Component 2: Oruvian Shardveil - The Arterial Convergence Core (COMPLETE)|
|Component 3: Myokelum Primus - The Living Pump of Trembling Flow (COMPLETE)|
|Component 4: Ascendran Nodule - The Living Principle of Complexity (COMPLETE)|
And forming now, blazing with light that suggested imminent completion:
|Component 5: Seraphilic Veinlace - The Living Principle of Purity (FORMING - 34% Complete)|
But there was a sixth component, one that should have been forming but wasn’t. A ghostly outline in the diagram, present but inactive, waiting for conditions that hadn’t been met yet!
|Component 6: Incarnaut Sanctis - The Early Chamber of Blood (DORMANT - 0% Complete - ERROR DETECTED)|
RUINEDEN’s expression grew serious as she gestured to highlight that sixth component.
“This is where we have a problem,” she said.
“Actually, calling it a ‘problem’ is underselling it. This is a fundamental architectural error in your development that’s limiting your progression in ways you haven’t noticed yet.”
WAA!
6/6 Keep the Magic Castles and Golden Tickets coming! Next chapter Titles: Early Creature Genesis! I-II, IMMACULATE I-III

And forming now, blazing with light that suggested imminent completion:

A ghostly outline in the diagram, present but inactive, waiting for conditions that hadn’t been met yet!

RUINEDEN’s expression grew serious as she gestured to highlight that sixth component.
“This is where we have a problem,” she said.
“Actually, calling it a ‘problem’ is underselling it.
This is a fundamental architectural error in your development that’s limiting your progression in ways you haven’t noticed yet.”

chapters.title: Chapter 4351: Early Creature Genesis! I
paragraphs: RUIN/EDEN pulled up additional data, showing how the Heart was supposed to function versus how it was currently operating.

“The Heart of an Early Creature is designed to form in stages,” she explained, her voice taking on lecturing qualities. “Each component builds upon the previous ones, creating a cascade of increasing complexity and power. Normally, this process is linear...you complete one part before the next begins forming.”
The diagram showed a timeline, each component lighting up in sequence.

“But here’s the issue,” RUINEDEN continued, her expression growing more animated as she warmed to her explanation. “You’re not a normal Early Creature. You’re more than genuine...your authenticity rating is 127% of baseline. You’ve integrated Principles that Early Creatures of your developmental stage shouldn’t possess. You’ve architected your existence using methodologies that didn’t exist in the Age of Early Creatures. In the Earliest Folds.”
She gestured broadly to encompass all of Noah’s impossible achievements.

“The normal parameters don’t apply to you anymore,” she said flatly. “The Age of Early Creatures, with its rules about sequential Heart formation, with its assumptions about cultivation speed and power ceilings...none of it fits your current reality. You’ve outgrown the template.”
Noah’s eyes narrowed as he processed that information.
The Heart was forming according to outdated rules!
Rules that were appropriate for Early Creatures developing naturally in their proper era!

“The specific error,” RUINEDEN continued, pulling up diagnostic text that highlighted the problem in sharp relief, “is that the Incarnaut Sanctis, the sixth and final component of your Heart, is locked in dormant state until the Seraphilic Veinlace completes. This is standard procedure for normal Early Creatures, because forming two Heart components simultaneously would strain their existential architecture beyond tolerance.”
She paused.

“But you’re not operating under normal strain tolerance, are you? Your Perpetual Harvest feeds you continuous power. Your Cheating Architect rewrites limitations as they appear. Your Resplendent Citadels and Mana Glyphs provide foundational support that most beings can’t imagine possessing. You could handle simultaneous formation without breaking. The system just doesn’t know that because it’s operating on assumptions that stopped being accurate about you several power scales ago.”
Noah felt understanding crystallize in his consciousness.
It was like discovering his computer had been artificially limiting its processing speed because some ancient setting assumed it was running on hardware from decades past!
The limitation wasn’t real...it was just a relic of outdated parameters that nobody had thought to update.
He reached inward with his consciousness, extending awareness toward his Heart with precision that came from intimate familiarity with his own existence.
And he felt it.
The Seraphilic Veinlace, forming with deliberate care, its structure already magnificent despite being only partially complete.
Veins of pure authority spreading through his existential architecture like roots seeking nourishment, like branches reaching toward light.
And beyond it, waiting in dormancy, the Incarnaut Sanctis.
The Early Chamber of Blood.

Even in its dormant state, Noah could sense its potential. This wasn’t just another component...this was the culmination, the final piece that would complete the Heart and elevate him to a level of Early Creature unlike any other.

But it was locked. Waiting. Unnecessary limitation imposed by rules that had stopped applying to him the moment he’d started accumulating Principles and Glyphs at rates that existence itself found offensive.
Well.
That was an error!
And Debug Mode existed specifically to exploit errors.
Noah’s expression shifted.
“Use Debug Mode,” he commanded, his voice carrying tyrannical certainty. “Rectify the error. I want both the Seraphilic Veinlace and Incarnaut Sanctis forming simultaneously.”
RUINEDEN’s eyes lit up with brilliance!
“Yes, Master,” she said. “Initiating Debug Mode protocols.”
|DEBUG MODE ACTIVATED|
|Error Identified: Sequential Heart Formation Protocol limiting development below user capacity|
|Error Classification: LEGACY LIMITATION - Outdated parameter application|
|Recommended Fix: Override sequential protocols, enable parallel formation|
|Resource Requirement: 3 Mana Glyphs of the Cheating Architect|
Three of Noah’s available Glyphs suddenly blazed with intensity that transcended their normal operation.
They detached from his general existential architecture and repositioned themselves around the diagram of his Heart, forming a triangle of pure corrective authority.
|APPLYING FIX...|
|Overriding: Age of Early Creatures formation protocols|
|Rewriting: Heart development parameters|
|Enabling: Simultaneous multi-component formation|
|FIX SUCCESSFULLY APPLIED|

|Result: Incarnaut Sanctis - The Early Chamber of Blood will now begin forming simultaneously with Seraphilic Veinlace. Both components will progress in parallel, feeding into and supporting each other’s development.|
HUUM
Glory bloomed.
Noah’s Heart, that impossible organ...suddenly erupted with light that made nearby reality pulse!
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
It beat like a drum that had been waiting eons to finally be played at full volume.
Each pulse sent waves of power through Noah’s existence, through his Early Veiled Shore, through the connections that bound him to his people and his Way.
Noah closed his eyes, his consciousness diving inward to observe the change.
And there, in the spaces where his existence was most fundamental, he felt it.

The Seraphilic Veinlace, already forming, suddenly blazed brighter as if it had been given permission to stop holding back. Its structure accelerated, veins of purity spreading faster, reaching further, establishing connections that would carry refined power through every aspect of his being.
And beside it, awakening from dormancy like something vast opening ancient eyes, the Incarnaut Sanctis began to form.
The Early Chamber of Blood!

Its structure was magnificent even in nascent state...a space that would exist within yet beyond his physical form, a chamber where the fundamental essence of what he was could be distilled, refined, elevated to heights that normal biology couldn’t contain.
They formed together now, in parallel, in harmony, each one supporting the other’s development through connections that were being architected in real-time.
It was beautiful in ways that transcended aesthetic appreciation!
This was his existence becoming more itself, more complete, more capable of containing the power he was accumulating at rates that defied reasonable cultivation speeds.
RUIN/EDEN’s voice cut through his internal observation, carrying information that made the moment even more significant.
|The Principle of Perpetual Harvest is responding to Heart formation|
|Labor’s Paradise Protocol Activated|
|Classification: Effort supercharge detected. The formation of Heart components is being recognized as tremendous Labor worthy of maximum amplification.|
Her holographic form displayed new data with visible excitement.

The diagram showed streams of verdant-gold light flowing from across Noah’s domain, from his people who were forging their Glyphs, from the Existential Taxation he’d implemented, from every source of accumulated Harvest.
Effort.
Glorious, magisterial effort!
All of it redirecting, funneling, pouring into the forming Seraphilic Veinlace and Incarnaut Sanctis like tributaries feeding into mighty rivers.

“The formation speed is being exponentially accelerated,” RUINEDEN continued, her voice carrying notes of calculation happening at speeds that blurred into single statements. “What should have taken days for each component to complete individually... you’re going to finish both in a fraction of that time.”
Noah opened his eyes, satisfaction blooming in his chest!

His Heart was completing itself properly now. Not limited by outdated rules, not held back by assumptions that had stopped applying to him, not forced to follow a path meant for beings who couldn’t handle what he could handle.
It was forming according to what he actually was rather than what some ancient protocol thought he should be!
It was perfect.
But as he observed the forming components with senses that could perceive their developing structure in exquisite detail, an idea crystallized in his consciousness.
An idea bloomed.
He looked at the Seraphilic Veinlace, the Living Principle of Purity, watching as its veins of authority spread through his existence like sacred circulatory systems.

And he looked at the Incarnaut Sanctis, the Early Chamber of Blood, observing as its chamber-structure began taking shape, creating space that would exist as both inside and outside him simultaneously.
They were forming separately. Parallel, yes, but distinct. Two components that would be part of a unified whole but which remained architecturally independent.
But what if they weren’t?

What if, instead of two separate components that merely coexisted, they were integrated? What if the veins of the Seraphilic Veinlace didn’t just exist near the Incarnaut Sanctis, but led directly into it?
What if the Chamber wasn’t just a space within his existence, but the culmination point where all the purified essence from the Veinlace flowed and concentrated and achieved transcendence?

chapters.title: Chapter 4352: Early Creature Genesis! II
paragraphs: The architectural beauty of it made him smile.
"RUIN/EDEN," he called out!
"Yes, Master?"
Noah’s smile deepened, taking on tyrannical qualities.
"Combine the aspects and potential boons of the two forming segments of the Heart," he commanded, each word deliberate and weighted with will that could reshape existence.
"The aorta of the Seraphilic Veinlace will lead directly into the Incarnaut Sanctis. They won’t just form simultaneously...they’ll form as unified architecture. One system, not two components."
RUIN/EDEN nodded silently!
"Yes, Master. The Cheating Architect exists specifically to rewrite architectural rules that claim to be absolute. And if we use enough Mana Glyphs to support the integration..."
Her voice took on calculating qualities.
"It would require 7 Mana Glyphs of the Cheating Architect operating continuously to manage the integration, and..."
Her smile grew wider.

"The resulting Heart component wouldn’t be two pieces working together. It would be a single unified system that combines the functions of both into something that transcends either. You’d be creating a Heart architecture that no Early Creature in history has ever possessed. Not even THE Creature. This...is your own."
HUUM!
Noah’s expression remained calm.
"Do it."
|EXISTENTIAL ARCHITECTURE INTEGRATION INITIATED|
|Resource Allocation: 7 Mana Glyphs of the Cheating Architect|
|Task: Forcible integration of Seraphilic Veinlace and Incarnaut Sanctis mid-formation|
|Warning: This will fundamentally alter standard Heart architecture|
|Proceeding with tyrannical confidence...|
The seven Glyphs blazed with authority that made space around Noah pulse with recognition of power being exercised.
They positioned themselves around the forming Heart components, creating a heptagon of pure will that would force integration that existence insisted was impossible.
And slowly, with precision that suggested the Cheating Architect knew exactly what it was doing despite the impossibility of the task, the two forming components began to merge.
Not absorbing into each other. Not consuming one another.
Integrating.

The veins of the Seraphilic Veinlace extended, reaching toward the forming Chamber of the Incarnaut Sanctis. Where they touched the Chamber’s structure, they didn’t stop...they continued inward, becoming part of the Chamber itself, establishing connections that would allow purified essence to flow directly from one component into the other.
The Chamber accepted these connections, its architecture adapting to incorporate them as if it had been designed this way from the beginning.
Walls that had been forming independently suddenly sprouted internal structures...channels, conduits, networks that would receive and concentrate the essence the Veinlace delivered.
It was like watching two incomplete puzzles realize they were actually parts of the same image, their pieces fitting together with satisfying precision.
|WARNING: Existential strain detected. Compensating with Mana Glyph authority.|
|INTEGRATION STATUS: 100%|
|INTEGRATION SUCCESSFUL|

|Result: Seraphilic Veinlace and Incarnaut Sanctis now form unified system. The Veinlace purifies essence and channels it directly into the Chamber, where it concentrates and achieves transcendent states. This is no longer two components.|
RUINEDEN’s holographic form was practically glowing with satisfaction at successful completion of something that should have been impossible.
|Due to the integration, because the Chamber is now directly connected to the Veinlace’s purification processes... the Incarnaut Sanctis can be manifested outwardly even before completion.|
Noah’s attention sharpened immediately.
"Explain."
RUINEDEN gestured, and the diagram shifted to show the Early Veiled Shore, with a new illusory structure pulsing on its golden sands.

"The Early Chamber of Blood can exist partially within you and partially as external space," she explained. "Normally, it wouldn’t be accessible until the entire Heart completed formation. But because you’ve integrated it with the Veinlace, because it’s now receiving continuous flow of purified essence from an active component... it can be established in your Shore right now."
Her expression grew more animated.

"You can create the physical manifestation of the Incarnaut Sanctis in your Early Veiled Shore," she said, each word carrying weight of significant revelation. "And once established, entities can enter it. Not just to visit, but to undergo transformation."
She pulled up specifications that made Noah’s eyes pulse with glorious tyranny!
|INCARNAUT SANCTIS - EXTERNAL MANIFESTATION CAPABILITIES|
|Function: Early Creature Genesis|

|Process: Entities who enter the Chamber undergo fundamental existential restructuring. Their potential is awakened and elevated, their architecture rebuilt according to Mana-based templates, their very nature transformed into new types of Mana-Based Early Creatures. Currently a maximum of 9 slots are possible.|
|Warning: This process is irreversible. Entities who undergo Genesis will emerge fundamentally changed. Their power will increase dramatically|
|Recommendation: Select candidates carefully. This could be deemed...The Glorious Evolution.|
HUUM!
The Glorious Evolution!
Noah stood in silence for a long moment.
He could froge new Early Creatures.

Not through consumption or transformation of existing ones, but through actual genesis...taking beings of sufficient potential and elevating them to a tier of existence that current reality insisted was closed, finished, ended with the Earliest Folds!
Nine.
Nine beings could enter his Heart’s external manifestation and emerge as something existence hadn’t seen in eons!
The implications were heavy.
The possibilities were endless.
In his Civilization, he would not be the only Early Creature!
The temptation to immediately start selecting candidates made his thoughts race!
"Establish the Chamber," he commanded, his voice carrying tyrannical certainty. "Manifest the Incarnaut Sanctis in my Early Veiled Shore. I want to see... what genesis looks like."
RUINEDEN bowed.
"It will be my pleasure, Master."
On the golden sands of the Early Veiled Shore, reality began to pulse with recognition of something new and impossible taking shape.
The Chamber was coming.
And with it, the genesis of new Early Creatures would begin!
The Incarnaut Sanctis was taking shape!
It was magnificent.
It was terrifying.
It was...
...going to have to wait.
Because in the distant Wandering Territories, his other body was experiencing something that demanded immediate attention.
Noah’s consciousness shifted focus, gazing toward that distant point where he’d been following Elyndra Viltharion through forests that existed in states of perpetual becoming.
They had arrived.
The Inner Garden Sanctum.

The transition had been subtle but absolute...one moment they’d been flying through the Forest of Perpetual Seasons, surrounded by trees that rearranged themselves and time that flowed in contradictory directions, and the next, they’d crossed some invisible threshold that marked the boundary between protective chaos and cultivated order.
The Inner Sanctum spread out before them in glory that defied casual observation.
It was...vast.
Vast in ways that transcended normal spatial measurements!
The Sanctum existed as its own pocket of reality, a space that had been carved from the Wandering Territories and shaped according to principles of growth and cultivation.
Noah’s enhanced perception swept across the landscape, cataloging details with speed.
Fields.

Endless fields, each one the size of Minor Folds, stretching toward horizons. But these weren’t fields growing normal crops...these were cultivation plots for concepts themselves, for Seeds of Principles that were being nurtured toward maturity!

The Inner Sanctum spread out before them in glory that defied casual observation.
It was...vast.
Vast in ways that transcended normal spatial measurements!
The Sanctum existed as its own pocket of reality, a space that had been carved from the Wandering Territories and shaped according to principles of growth and cultivation.
Noah’s enhanced perception swept across the landscape, cataloging details with speed.
Fields.
Endless fields, each one the size of Minor Folds, stretching toward horizons.
But these weren’t fields growing normal crops...these were cultivation plots for concepts themselves, for Seeds of Principles that were being nurtured toward maturity!

chapters.title: Chapter 4353 The First Farmer! I
paragraphs: In one field, Noah saw rows of plants that looked like crystallized time, each one representing a different temporal concept being grown from seed to full expression.
Elsewhere, massive trees grew downward from invisible ceilings, their roots reaching toward sky while their branches burrowed into earth, defying orientation itself.
Elsewhere, Fields cultivating...Everythings that looked like waves of stellar brilliance!
Between them, rivers of liquid authority flowed!
And tending these impossible fields were Fold Dwellers and Living Existences whose power made Noah's earlier assessments of strength seem quaint.
His eyes tracked across them to see names and measurements floating above their heads like status displays.
Mateus of the Golden Harvest
Complexity: 1.2 Quadrillion
Purity: 1.1 Quadrillion
Approximately 1 Quadrillion. A being whose power exceeded most
Dukes!
And nearby, tending to a field of what looked like solidified destiny:
Thera, Keeper of the Eternal Bloom
Complexity: 127 Quadrillion
Purity: 119 Quadrillion
Over 100 Quadrillion. A single entity whose casual existence generated more power than some entire Folds could muster.
His gaze continued scanning, finding more beings scattered across
the fields like farmers tending crops that could reshape reality.
1.5 Quintillion.
3 Quintillion.
4 Quintillion!
And continuing on...
Ancient Torvan, the First Tiller
Six Quintillion.
SIX.
Noah's expression remained calm, but these were wonders he was seeing!
This place wasn't merely a sanctuary!

The beings working these fields could each individually destroy current-era Folds without particular effort. Together, they represented power that could challenge... well, many things that claimed to be unchallengeable.
And they were growing Principles like crops.
Master, I'm recording everything. Every cultivation technique these beings are using, every field arrangement, every Seed type being nurtured...all of it is being cataloged for analysis.
Her holographic form appeared briefly in his peripheral vision, visible only to him.
This data alone is worth the entire journey.
Noah gave the mental equivalent of a nod, his attention still tracking across the impossible landscape.
The fields stretched endlessly...or at least, they stretched far enough
that weaker perceptions couldn't find their boundaries.

This space alone was equivalent to an entire Transcendent Fold, a pocket dimension that had been carved from the Wandering Territories and shaped into paradise for beings who understood growth as fundamental authority.
Elyndra led them forward.
As they passed through the fields, the native beings, those impossibly powerful Fold Dwellers and Living Existences who had found sanctuary here, turned to acknowledge her presence.
Not with fear. Not with submission.
With respect that transcended hierarchy.
They bowed their heads slightly, their expressions carrying genuine warmth mixed with reverence.
She smiled back at each one, her gestures conveying familiarity that suggested she knew them all personally, had probably worked these fields beside them at various points.
It was the kind of relationship that only developed through shared labor toward common purpose.

They continued deeper into the Sanctum, passing fields that grew increasingly complex in their cultivation...Seeds of higher-order Principles that pulsed with authority approaching what Tatiana had possesed.
And then, in the distance, Noah saw it.
A single cultivation plot surrounded by golden radiance that made everything else in the Sanctum look dim by comparison.

At its center stood a figure, backlit by that impossible light, making clear identification difficult. But even from this distance, Noah could sense something about the presence...weight that suggested accumulated wisdom, authority that had been refined through eons, power that...
...that felt wrong, somehow. Not threatening, but diminished. Like observing a star that should have blazed with fury but instead
flickered with uncertainty.
Elyndra slowed as they approached the radiant field's edge, her expression shifting into something more serious.

She turned to face Noah and his assembled companions...Sigrid standing close to him, Khor floating nearby with mysterious smile, Moiraine maintaining position with paradoxical authority humming, the Emperor Penguin and others forming constellation of power around their focal point.
"From here on out," Elyndra said, her voice carrying finality that suggested this wasn't negotiable, "I have to take him forward to meet
my Father alone."
Her blue eyes found Noah's, holding his gaze with intensity that searched for objections.
Noah analyzed the situationand smiled.
His gaze shifted to Khor, who stood beside Sigrid with that expression suggesting she found all of this entertaining.
His people were powerful in their own right- Sigrid now possessed 1.9 Quintillion in power, and Khor...could stomp anyone should anything drastic happen!
They could handle themselves.
And honestly, if The First Farmer wanted to try something hostile,
Noah possessed enough means to turn everything upside down.

He smiled calmly, his expression carrying confidence. "Walk around the Sanctuary of The First Farmer," he said to his companions, "Pluck anything you're allowed to pluck. Learn what you can learn. I'll be fine."
They all nodded at his words.
Elyndra's smile widened, genuine pleasure flickering across her
features.
"They'll be perfectly safe," she assured them, then turned back toward
Noah. "Shall we?"
Without waiting for further response, she moved forward, floating toward that golden-radiant field with grace.
Noah followed, his form rising to match her elevation.
As they flew deeper into the radiant space, separating from the

others, Elyndra turned her head slightly toward him. Her expression had shifted into something more direct, more openly curious, as if the presence of others had been restraining her natural tendencies toward straightforwardness.
"You know," she said, "out of all existences I've encountered, and I've
encountered many across these eons, you are the second person apart from my Father who has such a smell of growth and harvest."
She studied him with intensity that felt invasive without quite crossing into offense.
"Just what Principle did you nurture?" she asked, the question delivered with bluntness.
"Because that scent... it's not just similar to Father's work. It's almost
identical, but different."
Noah's expression remained calm.
She knew the answer to her own question, and yet she was here
playing around!
"Perpetual Harvest," he said simply, offering truth without elaboration.
"A Principle of continuous accumulation and exponential return on
effort invested."
Elyndra's eyes widened fractionally!
"Perpetual Harvest," she repeated softly, as if tasting the words.
"Father...called it his greatest failure, the Seed that refused to bloom
no matter what techniques he applied. And you... you actually succeeded in nurturing it?"
Her gaze intensified, searching his features for deception or exaggeration and apparently finding none.
"How did you manage what Father couldn't?"
Noah's smile deepened slightly.
"Different soil," he replied cryptically. "Different methods. Different understanding of what the Seed actually needed to grow. Even failure
is effort. Even with a failure, there is Harvest."
HUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4354 The First Farmer! II
paragraphs: It was answer that provided information while revealing nothing, the verbal equivalent of showing someone a closed door and describing its surface without opening it.
Elyndra stared at him for a long moment, her expression suggesting she was deciding whether to push for more details or accept the deflection gracefully.
Finally, she laughed with genuine amusement.
"You're infuriating to interrogate," she observed, "Every answer creates more questions. I can see why Father wanted to meet you personally."
They descended together, approaching the figure at the center of the golden-radiant field.
Noah's analytical capabilities were already activating, his enhanced perception beginning to break down and catalog what he was about to encounter.
The First Farmer.
The entity who had gazed upon THE Living Spirit...and likely other THE Living Existences!
The being who had created sanctuary in the Wandering Territories when nowhere else would accept Fold Dwellers.
The cultivator who had planted Seeds of Civilization and nurtured concepts into Principles.
Noah had high expectations!

This being was potentially one of the solutions to The Fallout...a force that could stand against The Dead, a mind that understood existence's architecture at levels that current-era beings had forgotten, a power that had survived when so many others had collapsed.
He had been active in the same time as Khor in the Earliest Folds.
He had met THE Living Existences personally.
Surely, such a being would radiate authority that made normal measurement meaningless. Surely, his power would exceed simple quantification. Surely...

Noah's eyes began to glow with blue light as his analytical capabilities fully engaged, breaking down the figure before him with precision that could measure power down to individual units of Complexity and Purity.
Beside him, Elyndra's voice rang out with genuine respect and affection.
"Father," she called out warmly. "I've brought the guest you've been expecting."
The figure turned.
And Noah's eyes widened as his analytical vision completed its assessment.
"What the fuck?"
The curse escaped before he could stop it, shock overriding his normal composure.
Because the figure who turned to face them was...
The First Farmer.

Noah recognized the features from their brief meeting in the Earliest Folds...the same bone structure, the same general appearance, the same fundamental presence that suggested agricultural authority refined through impossible time.
But everything else was wrong.
The being who stood before them now was old.
Not elderly. Not aged with dignity.
Old in ways that suggested imminent collapse.

His skin hung loose on bones that seemed too fragile to support even his minimal weight. His hair, which had been vibrant in the Earliest Folds, now appeared thin and colorless, each strand looking ready to fall out from sheer exhaustion.
His eyes, which had held depths of wisdom and determination, now carried shadows that spoke of pain and weariness that transcended normal suffering.
He was adorned in a green-gold robe that looked too heavy for his frame, the fabric somehow emphasizing his frailty rather than
concealing it.
And worst of all, he leaned heavily on a walking stick...not as affectation or symbol, but as genuine necessity.
His hands trembled where they gripped the wood, his entire posture suggesting that without that support, he would simply collapse.
Noah's analytical vision completed its assessment, and text appeared above the First Farmer's head with information that made his
expression sour dramatically.
Viltharion, The First Farmer
The One Who Gazed Upon THE Living Existences
The Cultivator of Sanctuary
Complexity: 0.000001 Quintillion
Purity: 0.000001 Quintillion
Quintillion.
The measurement was technically correct...he was following a Way
that operated on that Scale of Existence.
But those decimals...
0.000001 Quintillion was... 1 Trillion.
One trillion in both Complexity and Purity.
That was a tenth the power of a measly Duke!
That was less than many Living Existences possessed. That was... pathetic, for someone who should have been a cornerstone of
resistance against The Fallout!
Noah's expression rapidly soured, his mind racing through
implications.
This was the strength of the powerful First Farmer?
This diminished, frail, barely-functional being was supposed to be a core force for survival and prevention of The Fallout?
What the fuck happened?!
His thoughts were heavy enough that some of them clearly showed
on his face, because the First Farmer actually laughed...a wheezing, painful sound that suggested even amusement cost him dearly.
"I will have to apologize for disappointing you," the First Farmer said, his voice carrying kindness despite the weakness.
"I imagine you had certain... expectations about what you would find here. About who I would be. About what kind of help I could provide."

He moved slowly, painfully, each step requiring visible effort as he approached them with the walking stick bearing most of his weight. "But despite my current... diminished state," he continued, "I do remember you. Countless eons ago, I gave you a discarded Seed. My first failure. The concept I could never make bloom no matter what
techniques I employed.
HUUM!
He stopped a few feet from Noah, studying him with intensity that
made the moment feel significant.
"And eons later..." the First Farmer's voice grew softer, almost wondering, "...is that really what I sense in you? Did you allow
Perpetual Harvest to bloom?"
The first thing he asked about was Perpetual Harvest.
The Principle that Noah had built significant portions of his existence
around, that fed his continuous growth, that made effort compound into exponential returns.
The Failed Seed that had become one of the cornerstones of his Way.
Noah looked toward this grand being calmly, his expression giving
nothing away.
But before he could formulate answer, RUINEDEN's voice emerged in his consciousness.

Master, I'm detecting significant anomalies in this situation. Her holographic form appeared in his peripheral vision, visible only to him, her expression carrying concern mixed with rapid calculation. The First Farmer's current state doesn't match historical records or reasonable power scaling. A being who created this entire Sanctuary, who cultivated entities to Quintillion-level power, who stood alongside beings like Khor in the Earliest Folds...such an entity
shouldn't be reduced to mere trillions through normal cultivation decline. She pulled up data, showing comparisons and projections.
This level of diminishment suggests targeted assault. Not just defeat,
but fundamental destruction of power base. Similar to what happened to Khor when THE Living Paradox collapsed her existence, except... this seems even more complete. More thorough.
Her expression grew grimmer.
We hadn't accounted for it in our calculations, Master, but I'm now
considering: If THE Living Paradox targeted Khor, if other THE Living Existences were actively eliminating potential threats before The
Fallout... how many other powerful beings from the Earliest Folds suffered similar fates?
She gestured, creating illusory diagrams showing possible scenarios.
The First Farmer may have been on someone's radar.
Her voice took on darker tones.
We came here hoping for solutions, for powerful allies, for knowledge
that could help prevent The Fallout. Instead, we're finding evidence that those who might have helped were systematically eliminated
long before the current crisis began.
Noah's eyes pulsed as it felt like existence was getting tighter!
Like a huge net was closing in!
There would be no grand help from the First Farmer. No cavalry
arriving to save the day. No ancient power revealing itself at the critical moment to shift the balance.
As always, he would have to come up with solutions alone.

But this trip shouldn't be for naught. He could at least gather information, understand how things had deteriorated to this point, learn what had happened to bring a being of such magnitude down to pathetic weakness.
Noah sighed, the sound carrying weight of disappointment mingled
with resignation.
Finally, he nodded, raising his hand in gesture that felt both casual and ceremonial.
And from his palm, light began to emerge.
Not just any light...this was the pristine radiance of Perpetual Harvest
itself, green-gold brilliance that sang of continuous growth and
exponential accumulation, of effort compounding into power that could reshape existence through sheer persistence.
It blazed between them like proof of impossible achievement, like vindication of potential that others had dismissed as failure. The First Farmer trembled at its sight.
His entire frail form shook with emotion, his eyes widening with
wonder mixed with something that might have been joy or might have been grief or might have been both simultaneously!
He looked like a man dying of thirst who had just been shown water...
someone who had wanted to see this one thing more than anything else in existence, and now, finally, impossibly, he was witnessing it.
"It's real," he whispered, his voice breaking with emotion. "It actually bloomed. My greatest failure... became someone else's success. The Seed I discarded... found soil that could nourish it."
Oh!
His legs gave out.
Elyndra moved immediately, her grace transforming into urgency as
she caught her father before he could collapse entirely.

chapters.title: Chapter 4355 The First Farmer! III
paragraphs: She helped him sit on the brown-gold sand at the edge of the cultivation field, her movements carrying practiced ease that suggested this wasn't the first time she'd performed this action.
She waved her hands, and mats materialized from nowhere...simple, elegant things woven from what looked like compressed concepts of rest and stability.
One mat settled beneath her father. Another positioned itself beside him for her to sit upon. A third appeared near Noah, positioned at comfortable conversational distance.
"Please, sit," Elyndra said, her voice carrying gentle insistence.
"Father tires easily these days, and this conversation... this is important to him."
Noah complied, his form settling onto the mat with movements that suggested he was humoring her request rather than following orders.
The three of them sat there on the edge of that golden-radiant field, forming triangle of conversation.
The First Farmer laughed then...not the pained wheeze from before, but something closer to genuine joy, though it still carried notes of exhaustion that suggested even happiness cost him dearly.

"Countless eons ago," he began, "when I was still cultivating in the Earliest Folds, when I still possessed power that could reshape territories and nurture concepts into Principles... THE Creature visited my gardens."
Noah's attention sharpened immediately.
THE Creature.
The being whose authority seemed to permeate everything related to
Early Creatures. The mysterious presence that even THE Living Existences seemed to reference with particular weight.

"He was masked as a Fold Dweller," The First Farmer continued, his eyes growing distant with memory. "But I knew what he was. You cannot hide that kind of presence, that level of fundamental authority. It radiates from every action, every gesture, every casual observation."

He paused, his hands trembling slightly where they rested on his lap. "He examined my cultivation plots with interest that felt... proprietary. And when he came to the Failed Seed...the one that would eventually become your Perpetual Harvest, he held it and stated what a shame it was that such a seed would never bloom! That...even a Leader of a Civilization would have benefited tremendously from it!"
HUUM!
Noah felt his existence buzz.
THE Creature had held the Failed Seed of Perpetual Harvest and said such things?!
RUINEDEN's voice emerged in his consciousness at such a time. Even though we already knew of its importance, we may need to designate Perpetual Harvest with multiple additional levels of importance.]
Noah's expression remained calm.
The First Farmer continued speaking.
"But that was then," he said, his voice growing heavier. "When I still had power. When I still stood a chance. When I was on the cusp of attaining..."
He paused, his eyes flashing with emotion that mixed pain and obsession in equal measure.
The word dropped into the space between them.
THE.
Not just power. Not just advancement. Not cultivation to higher levels or accumulation of greater Complexity and Purity.
THE!
The distinction that separated beings who merely possessed power from entities who defined existence's fundamental parameters.
"I was close," The First Farmer continued, his voice carrying notes of obsession that had survived despite everything else being stripped
away.

"So close that I could taste it. My cultivation had reached heights that current-era beings can't conceive of. My understanding of growth and harvest and nurturing had become so refined that I was beginning to perceive the underlying code that governs how Principles themselves develop."
His hands clenched into fists, trembling with emotion!

"I stood at the threshold," he said, his voice breaking. "One more step. One more breakthrough. One more refinement of My Way. My Civilization. And I would have achieved THE. I would have become THE First Farmer! I would have been able to stand alongside THE Living Existences not as lesser being seeking approval, but as equal force defining existence's nature."
He shook his head, pain flickering across his features.
"But THE Living Emotive appeared."
Elyndra, who had been sitting beautifully and calmly beside her
father, suddenly pulsed with contained rage so intense that space around her began crystallizing with frost.
The First Farmer's voice continued, each word heavy with trauma that
time hadn't healed.
"That psychopath appeared in this very Sanctuary. They came through the protective forests as if they weren't there, bypassed
every defense we'd cultivated, arrived here with smile that suggested
they found the entire situation amusing."
His eyes grew distant, reliving memory that clearly caused him.
anguish.
"And they...shattered my foundation."
WAA!
The words were delivered simply.
"Not killed me," The First Farmer clarified, his voice taking on bitter

tones. "That would have been mercy. Instead, they dismantled my cultivation base piece by piece, breaking down the architectural supports I'd spent eons constructing, collapsing the Principles I'd nurtured, destroying the accumulation of My Way and My Civilization that had brought me so close to THE."
He paused, his breathing becoming labored.

"They nearly destroyed all of my Civilization as well. The Fold Dwellers and Living Existences who had found sanctuary here, who had been cultivating under my guidance....they went through them like farmer culling diseased crops. Not out of necessity. Not out of strategic concern. Just because they could. Because their suffering amused them."
Elyndra's rage intensified, her form practically vibrating with contained violence that wanted expression but had nowhere to go.
"And when they were done," The First Farmer continued, "when they
had reduced me from the cusp of THE to barely functional weakness, when they had collapsed most of my Civilization and left survivors traumatized beyond normal healing...they explained why."
His voice took on mocking tones, clearly mimicking THE Living
Emotive's words.
"They said: "There are already enough existences with the distinction
of THE who will be left behind. We don't need another one. Your
ambition is noted and denied. Your potential is recognized and eliminated. Consider yourself fortunate that I'm leaving you alive to witness The Fallout from this diminished state."
The cruelty was breathtaking in its calculated precision.
Not just defeating a rival. Not just eliminating a threat. But specifically

leaving the First Farmer alive and aware, forced to experience the helplessness of having once been powerful enough to stand alongside THE Living Existences, only to watch everything collapse while possessing insufficient strength to intervene.
It was torture disguised as mercy, punishment that would last until
The Fallout finally ended his suffering!
"He didn't even bother to kill me," The First Farmer said, his voice
carrying bitterness that had festered through eons. "He stated that my fear and anguish from being so close to THE, from having it ripped
away, would be good sustenance for him for eons until I experienced The Fallout."
His expression shifted, carrying genuine confusion mixed with pain.
"To this day," he said, his voice growing quieter, "I cannot understand
why THE Living Emotive and others had the nature they did. It could not simply be from their Way, right? To act like that. To do all that. To
cause suffering not from necessity or strategy, but from... what, artistic satisfaction? Entertainment? Pure malice refined into fundamental authority?"
He shook his head, the gesture carrying defeat.
"It was just... ah-"
The First Farmer suddenly began coughing, his frail form convulsing
with spasms.
The coughing fit intensified, each hack sounding like it might be his
last, his entire being trembling with strain that exceeded his capacity
to endure.
Elyndra moved instinctively, her hand rising toward her father,
radiance gathering around her fingers as she prepared to channel lifeforce that could stabilize him, heal him, provide relief from suffering that clearly exceeded normal tolerance.
But then she stopped.
Her hand froze mid-motion, the gathered radiance dissipating as she
forcibly pulled back, her expression carrying anguish that suggested this internal conflict played out regularly.
She turned toward Noah, and in her eyes, he saw seriousness mixed
with contained rage and helplessness.
"Any lifeforce or authority of others," she said, "even for the sake of

healing, even with best intentions... is poisonous to him. The damage THE Living Emotive inflicted wasn't just physical or cultivation-based. It was existential. Father's being now rejects external assistance, treating it as contamination rather than aid."
Her hands clenched into fists.
"None of us can help him. I... cannot do anything." The helplessness in her voice was genuine!
The First Farmer continued his coughing fit, his existence seeming
weary and tired.
Noah watched this display with expression that grew increasingly grave.
So this was The First Farmer!
A broken man!
He had come here hoping to find powerful being who could stand
against The Fallout, who could provide knowledge or resources or strategic advantage.

Instead, he'd found victim of THE Living Existences' preemptive elimination of threats, someone who had been specifically targeted and broken because he'd gotten too close to achieving THE. He had gotten too close to the sun!
