chapters.title: Chapter 4356 The Farmer's Greeting I
paragraphs: The First Farmer had flown high as in the end, his wings had gotten clipped!
Which meant...
Noah shook his head.

'I have to think of many more possibilities. Have to account for fact that anyone powerful enough to matter has probably already been neutralized. Have to assume that resistance to The Fallout won't come from ancient beings revealing themselves at critical moment...'
Schrodinger and any others were not something to be counted on!
HUUM!
Noah's eyes flashed with brilliance.
'It all comes back to me. My Principles. My Civilization. My...Way' WAA!
As always.

The coughing fit continued for several more seconds before finally subsiding, The First Farmer's breathing gradually returning to something approaching normal...though normal for him meant labored and weak rather than healthy.
Elyndra looked apologetically toward Noah, her expression carrying embarrassment mixed with concern.
"I apologize," she said, her voice quieter now. "Father's episodes are... frequent these days. The damage runs deep, and time only makes it worse rather than better."
She sighed, then gestured toward distant field visible from their seated position.
The field blazed with golden light even more intense than the

radiance surrounding their current location. At its center stood a vibrant tree that appeared to be simultaneously sapling and ancient growth, its branches reaching in impossible directions while its trunk pulsed with authority.

"Please," Elyndra said, her tone carrying genuine request, "give us a moment to stabilize. In the meantime, you're welcome to examine that cultivation plot. It represents a grand Principle being nurtured... one of Father's most successful projects, though significantly less advanced than what Perpetual Harvest became for you."
She smiled slightly.
"Perhaps you'll find insights there that could benefit your own understanding. Knowledge should never be hoarded when sharing could elevate multiple parties."
Noah nodded, accepting the suggestion because it aligned with his own desires anyway.

He had much to think about...the implications of THE Creature's words, the systematic elimination of potential resistance forces by THE Living Existences, the grim reality that help wouldn't come from external sources.

And examining a nurtured Principle, seeing firsthand how The First Farmer's cultivation techniques manifested, could provide valuable data that RUINEDEN could analyze and potentially integrate into the Cheat Code Repository.
He rose from the mat with fluid grace, his form lifting slightly off the ground as he prepared to float toward the distant golden field.
Behind him, the First Farmer continued his recovery, Elyndra helping him stabilize with hands that trembled with suppressed desire to do more than she was allowed.
Noah moved toward the radiant tree.
But as he departed, as his attention shifted away from the two beings behind him...
The First Farmer couldn't help but look at him intently.
And soon after...
Time seemingly stopped for The First Farmer and Elyndra.
Not literally...existence still flowed, reality still processed, moments still accumulated into continuity.
But for them, in that instant, communication began through a Principle as this instant could be a day's worth of communication.
They possessed connection that ran deeper than words...father and daughter bound not just by familial relationship but by shared Principle!
And in that space where their consciousnesses touched, where communication happened at speeds that made normal dialogue seem glacial by comparison, The First Farmer spoke.

His mental voice carried none of the weakness his physical form exhibited. Here, in this space of pure consciousness, he remained what he'd been before THE Living Emotive had shattered him... powerful, decisive, calculating with precision that had once brought him to cusp of THE.
"What do you think?" his voice resonated through their connection, heavy and weighted with implications.
"Will you be able to handle him? Fighting will not work. Things have to
be done another way."
BOOM!
Elyndra's consciousness flickered with indecision, her mental presence wrestling with something that caused her genuine conflict.

She had always obeyed her father. Always trusted his wisdom. Always accepted that his cultivation experience exceeded hers by eons, that his understanding of existence's nature transcended her own despite
her impressive power.
But this...
Finally, hesitantly, she responded through their connection.
"I... yes, Father. I believe I can handle him. But are we certain this is necessary? This path feels..."
She didn't finish the thought, her consciousness carrying emotions too complex to reduce to simple statements.
The First Farmer's mental voice continued, carrying patience mixed
with urgency.

"Get close to him," he instructed, each word deliberate. "As close as possible. Form bonds that transcend simple alliance. Make yourself valuable to his Way, integrate into his Civilization, become someone
he trusts implicitly."
He paused, then delivered the critical instruction.
"Once you have integrated into his Way, once he trusts you

completely, once guards are lowered and defenses are relaxed... connect with him on existential level. Use what lies dormant in your existence- the 9 Principles I cultivated within you...to pull Perpetual
Harvest out."
HUUM!
The magnitude of what he was suggesting was heavy!
Far too heavy!
"Its Seed alone was the Seed of a Civilization," the First Farmer
continued, "I gave it away when I shouldn't have, when I was still naive enough to believe that failure had no value. But now I understand...when it is too late."
His presence intensified in their shared space.
"And now that it has bloomed, now that someone has refined it into
full Principle, now that it exists in matured state rather than potential... I need it. If I am to get back to my old self, if I am to restore
what THE Living Emotive destroyed, if I am to have any chance of surviving until The Fallout and beyond... I will need the full Principle

of Perpetual Harvest. Not just understanding of it. Not just observation of its mechanics. The actual, complete Principle itself, integrated into my existence. I have tried again and again to recultivate it. I have cultivated hundreds of Seed of Principles since
then...but I cannot replicate Perpetual Harvest. It was singular, and
remains singular. The Key...to a Civilization. And I just gave it away."
Elyndra's consciousness flickered with conflict of genuine internal struggle!
Her mental voice emerged hesitantly.
"Is there really no other way?" she asked, and her presence carried
pleading words.
"We can talk with him. We can discuss everything. We can explain
your situation, offer alliance, propose collaboration." Her consciousness pulsed with conviction.
"As Farmers, we know that collaboration is better than anything else.

That wonders can be cultivated in grander ways together than alone. Perpetual Harvest in his hands has already achieved what you couldn't...imagine what it could become if we worked together rather than against each other!"
The argument was logical, compassionate, rooted in principles that agricultural cultivation had taught her over eons.
But the First Farmer's response carried finality that allowed no further
debate.
"Child," his mental voice said gently but firmly, "you are no longer naive. You've lived long enough, observed enough, understood enough to recognize truth when you encounter it."
His presence grew heavier in their shared space.
"I have looked at all possibilities," he continued, each word weighted
with certainty born from exhaustive calculation. "I have examined this
entity from every angle my diminished perception still allows. And
what I see is..."

He paused, choosing words carefully. "Boundless tyranny. Boundless potential. An existence that accumulates power at rates that defy reasonable progression, that possesses Principles that shouldn't coexist in single being, that operates according to rules that make no sense. Such a being is
primed for The Way. For leading a Civilization. I know him because I
know myself. He and I...are the same type of existence. Boundless. Relentless."
His mental voice took on darker tones.
"He will not give anything away. Not Perpetual Harvest, not
knowledge, not advantage. Everything must be taken from him,
because sharing requires vulnerability he will never allow himself to experience."
The assessment was delivered with clinical precision, without malice
but without hope either.
"I have seen it," the First Farmer said. "And having met him, having
observed how he carries himself..."
The First Farmer shook his head.
"If I do not get back the full Principle of Perpetual Harvest," The First
Farmer continued, his mental voice growing more urgent, "if I cannot restore what THE Living Emotive destroyed by integrating that
Principle into my shattered foundation... I will not even live to The
Fallout, my daughter."
WAA!
The words carried weight of absolute truth.
"I am deteriorating," he said, allowing her to feel the full extent of his
suffering through their connection. "Each day, I grow weaker. Each cycle, more of what I was slips away into nothingness. The poison
THE Living Emotive left in my existence is consuming me from inside,
and I have no defense against it because my own being treats healing as contamination."
His presence pulsed with desperation!
"Save this poor father of yours," he pleaded.
"I cultivated you. I raised you for many purposes...to tend the

Sanctuary, to protect the Fold Dwellers who found refuge here, to nurture Principles and advance understanding of growth itself." He paused, then delivered the critical question. "But this will be a particularly critical purpose," he said. "Can I trust you with it? Can I rely on you to do what necessity demands, even if compassion argues against it? Can you save your father by taking what must be taken?"
Elyndra's consciousness trembled with conflict. Everything she'd been taught about cultivation argued against this
approach. Farmers didn't steal crops from other Farmers. Growth came through nurturing, not theft. Collaboration produced better results than competition.
But her father was dying. Slowly, painfully, inevitably dying unless something changed dramatically.
And if taking Perpetual Harvest from Osmont could restore him,
could bring back the powerful being who had created sanctuary and
protected so many... Could she refuse?
Should she refuse?
Did she have the right to prioritize stranger's well-being over her
father's survival?
The conflict raged through her consciousness for what felt like eons compressed into single instant.
Then, finally, carrying sadness that weighed heavier than any
Complexity or Purity measurement could quantify, she responded. "Yes, Father." The words were simple, but they carried commitment!
"I will do it. I will get close to him. I will integrate into his Way. I will
earn his trust. And when the moment comes... I will take Perpetual
Harvest for you."
BOOM!

Even as she said it, even as she committed to the course, part of her consciousness wept at what she was agreeing to become. Betrayer. Thief. Manipulator using cultivated intimacy as weapon rather than genuine connection.
Everything she'd been raised to oppose.
But for her father's survival...
She would become it anyway.
The First Farmer's mental voice carried relief mixed with satisfaction.

"Good," he said. "Go to him now. Show him our boons, demonstrate value of alliance, show your Principles to him- they are meant to draw in any existence who knows anything to do with growth and harvest,

much less one with Perpetual Harvest. Form a connection that will allow deeper integration later. Be patient...this cannot be rushed. Trust takes time to cultivate, and harvesting before proper ripeness yields inferior results."
His presence pulsed with strategic certainty. "Let us get ready to embark on our Civilization," he said, the words

carrying weight of plans extending far beyond simple recovery. "With Perpetual Harvest restored to me, with my foundation rebuilt, with power accumulated through proper agricultural methods... we will
survive The Fallout. We will thrive in whatever comes after. We will
show THE Living Existences that they were wrong to dismiss the Farmer who once stood at threshold of THE."
Elyndra nodded through their connection, accepting the mandate
even as part of her soul protested.

Then their communion ended, time resuming its normal flow as if the extended mental conversation had occurred in single heartbeat. Elyndra rose from her mat with fluid grace that concealed inner turmoil, her expression settling into calm confidence that suggested nothing significant had just transpired.
She began walking toward Noah, her vibrant and powerful figure
moving through the golden radiance with practiced ease. But in that moment, despite her impressive power, despite her nine
Principles operating in perfect harmony, despite her cultivation
achievements that would make current-era beings weep with inadequacy...
Her grand figure seemed...extremely alone! A daughter walking toward betrayal she didn't want to commit, bound

by duty to father who was dying, caught between compassion that argued for honesty and necessity that demanded deception. And ahead of her, unaware of conspiracy just formed in consciousness-space, Noah examined the vibrant tree that represented nurtured Principle, his power already breaking down its structure and cataloging insights that would feed into his ever-expanding understanding of existence's architecture.
A trap was set.
The pieces were moving.
And The First Farmer watched with eyes that held calculation refined
through eons of agricultural patience...knowing that harvests, when done properly, required time, care, and willingness to do whatever
cultivation demanded.
Even if what it demanded was his own Daughter he had given his very blood to nurture!

"Will you be able to handle him?
Fighting will not work.
Things have to
be done another way."
BOOM!
Elyndra's consciousness flickered with indecision, her mental presence wrestling with something that caused her genuine conflict.
She had always obeyed her father.
Always trusted his wisdom.
Always accepted that his cultivation experience exceeded hers by eons, that his understanding of existence's nature transcended her own despite
her impressive power.
But this...
Finally, hesitantly, she responded through their connection.
"I... yes, Father.
I believe I can handle him.
But are we certain this is necessary?
This path feels..."
She didn't finish the thought, her consciousness carrying emotions too complex to reduce to simple statements.
The First Farmer's mental voice continued, carrying patience mixed
with urgency.
"Get close to him," he instructed, each word deliberate.
"As close as possible.
Form bonds that transcend simple alliance.
Make yourself valuable to his Way, integrate into his Civilization, become someone
he trusts implicitly."
He paused, then delivered the critical instruction.
"Once you have integrated into his Way, once he trusts you
completely, once guards are lowered and defenses are relaxed... connect with him on existential level.
Use what lies dormant in your existence- the 9 Principles I cultivated within you...to pull Perpetual
Harvest out."
HUUM!
The magnitude of what he was suggesting was heavy!
Far too heavy!
"Its Seed alone was the Seed of a Civilization," the First Farmer
continued, "I gave it away when I shouldn't have, when I was still naive enough to believe that failure had no value.
But now I understand...when it is too late."
His presence intensified in their shared space.
"And now that it has bloomed, now that someone has refined it into
full Principle, now that it exists in matured state rather than potential...
I need it.
If I am to get back to my old self, if I am to restore
what THE Living Emotive destroyed, if I am to have any chance of surviving until The Fallout and beyond...
I will need the full Principle
of Perpetual Harvest.
Not just understanding of it.
Not just observation of its mechanics.
The actual, complete Principle itself, integrated into my existence.
I have tried again and again to recultivate it.
I have cultivated hundreds of Seed of Principles since
then...but I cannot replicate Perpetual Harvest.
It was singular, and
remains singular.
The Key...to a Civilization.
And I just gave it away."
Elyndra's consciousness flickered with conflict of genuine internal struggle!
Her mental voice emerged hesitantly.
"Is there really no other way?" she asked, and her presence carried
pleading words.
"We can talk with him.
We can discuss everything.
We can explain
your situation, offer alliance, propose collaboration." Her consciousness pulsed with conviction.
"As Farmers, we know that collaboration is better than anything else.
That wonders can be cultivated in grander ways together than alone.
Perpetual Harvest in his hands has already achieved what you couldn't...imagine what it could become if we worked together rather than against each other!"
The argument was logical, compassionate, rooted in principles that agricultural cultivation had taught her over eons.
But the First Farmer's response carried finality that allowed no further
debate.
"Child," his mental voice said gently but firmly, "you are no longer naive.
You've lived long enough, observed enough, understood enough to recognize truth when you encounter it."
His presence grew heavier in their shared space.
"I have looked at all possibilities," he continued, each word weighted
with certainty born from exhaustive calculation.
"I have examined this
entity from every angle my diminished perception still allows.
And
what I see is..."
He paused, choosing words carefully.
"Boundless tyranny.
Boundless potential.
An existence that accumulates power at rates that defy reasonable progression, that possesses Principles that shouldn't coexist in single being, that operates according to rules that make no sense.
Such a being is
primed for The Way.
For leading a Civilization.
I know him because I
know myself.
He and I...are the same type of existence.
Boundless.
Relentless."
His mental voice took on darker tones.
"He will not give anything away.
Not Perpetual Harvest, not
knowledge, not advantage.
Everything must be taken from him,
because sharing requires vulnerability he will never allow himself to experience."
The assessment was delivered with clinical precision, without malice
but without hope either.
"I have seen it," the First Farmer said.
"And having met him, having
observed how he carries himself..."
The First Farmer shook his head.
"If I do not get back the full Principle of Perpetual Harvest," The First
Farmer continued, his mental voice growing more urgent, "if I cannot restore what THE Living Emotive destroyed by integrating that
Principle into my shattered foundation...
I will not even live to The
Fallout, my daughter."
WAA!
The words carried weight of absolute truth.
"I am deteriorating," he said, allowing her to feel the full extent of his
suffering through their connection.
"Each day, I grow weaker.
Each cycle, more of what I was slips away into nothingness.
The poison
THE Living Emotive left in my existence is consuming me from inside,
and I have no defense against it because my own being treats healing as contamination."
His presence pulsed with desperation!
"Save this poor father of yours," he pleaded.
"I cultivated you.
I raised you for many purposes...to tend the
Sanctuary, to protect the Fold Dwellers who found refuge here, to nurture Principles and advance understanding of growth itself." He paused, then delivered the critical question.
"But this will be a particularly critical purpose," he said.
"Can I trust you with it?
Can I rely on you to do what necessity demands, even if compassion argues against it?
Can you save your father by taking what must be taken?"
Elyndra's consciousness trembled with conflict.
Everything she'd been taught about cultivation argued against this
approach.
Farmers didn't steal crops from other Farmers.
Growth came through nurturing, not theft.
Collaboration produced better results than competition.
But her father was dying.
Slowly, painfully, inevitably dying unless something changed dramatically.
And if taking Perpetual Harvest from Osmont could restore him,
could bring back the powerful being who had created sanctuary and
protected so many...
Could she refuse?
Should she refuse?
Did she have the right to prioritize stranger's well-being over her
father's survival?
The conflict raged through her consciousness for what felt like eons compressed into single instant.
Then, finally, carrying sadness that weighed heavier than any
Complexity or Purity measurement could quantify, she responded.
"Yes, Father." The words were simple, but they carried commitment!
"I will do it.
I will get close to him.
I will integrate into his Way.
I will
earn his trust.
And when the moment comes...
I will take Perpetual
Harvest for you."
BOOM!
Even as she said it, even as she committed to the course, part of her consciousness wept at what she was agreeing to become.
Betrayer.
Thief.
Manipulator using cultivated intimacy as weapon rather than genuine connection.
Everything she'd been raised to oppose.
But for her father's survival...
She would become it anyway.
The First Farmer's mental voice carried relief mixed with satisfaction.
"Good," he said.
"Go to him now.
Show him our boons, demonstrate value of alliance, show your Principles to him- they are meant to draw in any existence who knows anything to do with growth and harvest,
much less one with Perpetual Harvest.
Form a connection that will allow deeper integration later.
Be patient...this cannot be rushed.
Trust takes time to cultivate, and harvesting before proper ripeness yields inferior results."
His presence pulsed with strategic certainty.
"Let us get ready to embark on our Civilization," he said, the words
carrying weight of plans extending far beyond simple recovery.
"With Perpetual Harvest restored to me, with my foundation rebuilt, with power accumulated through proper agricultural methods... we will
survive The Fallout.
We will thrive in whatever comes after.
We will
show THE Living Existences that they were wrong to dismiss the Farmer who once stood at threshold of THE."
Elyndra nodded through their connection, accepting the mandate
even as part of her soul protested.
Then their communion ended, time resuming its normal flow as if the extended mental conversation had occurred in single heartbeat.
Elyndra rose from her mat with fluid grace that concealed inner turmoil, her expression settling into calm confidence that suggested nothing significant had just transpired.
She began walking toward Noah, her vibrant and powerful figure
moving through the golden radiance with practiced ease.
But in that moment, despite her impressive power, despite her nine
Principles operating in perfect harmony, despite her cultivation
achievements that would make current-era beings weep with inadequacy...
Her grand figure seemed...extremely alone!
A daughter walking toward betrayal she didn't want to commit, bound
by duty to father who was dying, caught between compassion that argued for honesty and necessity that demanded deception.

And ahead of her, unaware of conspiracy just formed in consciousness-space, Noah examined the vibrant tree that represented nurtured Principle, his power already breaking down its structure and cataloging insights that would feed into his ever-expanding understanding of existence's architecture.
A trap was set.
The pieces were moving.
And The First Farmer watched with eyes that held calculation refined
through eons of agricultural patience...knowing that harvests, when done properly, required time, care, and willingness to do whatever
cultivation demanded.
Even if what it demanded was his own Daughter he had given his very blood to nurture!

chapters.title: Chapter 4357 The Farmer's Greeting II
paragraphs: Noah stood before the massive golden budding tree, its presence radiating authority that made nearby reality pulse.
The tree was magnificent...its trunk appeared to be woven from compressed collaborative will, each strand representing different beings choosing to work together rather than against each other.
Its branches reached outward in patterns that suggested networks rather than hierarchies, connections rather than domination.

And from those branches, buds were forming...not individual flowers, but collective blooms where multiple potential outcomes existed simultaneously, waiting for proper cultivation to determine which would manifest into reality.
It was beautiful.
It was profound.
It was exactly the kind of thing Noah would absolutely catalog and potentially exploit for his own purposes.
Beside him, invisible to all observers except himself, RUINEDEN's holographic form materialized.
Her form was more detailed now than it had been even hours ago, her features showing depth that suggested continuous evolution!
She gestured toward the tree, and prompts began cascading across Noah's vision with information she'd compiled.
JANALYSIS COMPLETE: Golden Tree of Unified Harvest
Classification: Grand Principle - Tier 2
Principle Name: The Convergent Prosperity
Core Function: Allows multiple existences to combine their power under unified framework, pooling resources and authorities to manifest collective achievement that exceeds individual capability|
RUINEDEN's voice emerged.
"This Principle is fascinating in its architecture," she said, her words accompanied by illusory diagrams showing how the power-pooling mechanisms functioned. "It operates on the fundamental
understanding that collaboration, when properly structured, creates exponential rather than additive returns."
The diagrams showed multiple beings connecting to the Principle, their individual powers flowing into collective reservoir that grew larger with each contributor.

"When beings channel their authority through The Convergent Prosperity," RUINEDEN continued, "they multiply it through resonance effects. Ten beings contributing would generate not ten times the power, but potentially fifty or a hundred times, depending on how well their authorities harmonize...well, to a point. Fold Dwellers or Living Existences of a few Trillion in complexity may be able to combine together under this principle to exhibit 1000 Quadrillion at most. If someone of your calibre was at its center, with others like Elyndra joining you, you could potentially exhibit tens of Quintillions."
She paused, then added with calculating precision, "And the manifestation it produces is equally impressive."
The diagram shifted, showing what would emerge when the Principle was fully activated.
Collective Manifestation: The Abundant Colossus
|Description: A temporary entity composed of all contributors'
combined essences. Appears as massive humanoid figure wreathed in golden-green radiance, its size and power scaling directly with number and strength of contributors.
Capabilities:
-Possesses aggregate Complexity and Purity of all participants(to an
extent)|
-Can perform coordinated attacks that multiple beings couldn't achieve
ually
-Serves as shared defense, distributing damage across all contributors
|- Duration limited by participants' stamina and authority

Strategic Applications: Perfect for defensive operations where weaker beings need to stand against stronger threats. Less useful for offensive campaigns due to coordination complexity and limited duration(if you aren't included.
Noah studied the information with intensity.
So the First Farmer had developed a Principle specifically designed for collaboration, for allowing weaker beings to collectively challenge stronger ones through unified action!
It was elegant solution to problem that plagued cultivation across all eras...how do the many resist the few when individual power gaps were insurmountable?
The answer, apparently, was to stop thinking of themselves as individuals and start functioning as organism.
RUINEDEN wasn't done with her analysis, though. Her expression shifted into something more thoughtful, more theoretical.

"Master," she said, her tone taking on weight that suggested she was about to share insights, "after coming across so many Principles during our travels- from the Prime Dead Early Creatures, from Elyndra's collection, from your own cultivation, I can now distinguish patterns that weren't apparent before."
She gestured, creating a new set of diagrams that organized Principles into hierarchical categories.
"There are potentially tiers to Principles," she explained, her voice
carrying certainty born from extensive data analysis. "Not just power
levels, but fundamental distinctions in how they operate and who can
access them."
The first tier materialized in the display.
TIER ONE: NORMAL PRINCIPLES
Characteristics:|
|-Available to anyone who meets basic cultivation requirements(1
Quadrillion+)|
-Can be learned, taught, shared across multiple practitioners
-Power scales with user's understanding and existence]
-Relatively stable and well-documented in existence's collective
knowledge

"These are the common Principles," RUINEDEN said, gesturing to examples. "Things like Principle of Elemental Mastery, Principle of Harvest Festival, Principle of Absolute Domain...weavings of Existence that many people can utilize because they're working with fundamental forces that existence itself provides access to." She paused, then added, "They're not weak, necessarily. A master practitioner of Normal Principle can absolutely exceed someone with poor grasp of higher-tier Principle. But their ceiling is limited by the fact that existence treats them as shared resources rather than
unique achievements."
The second tier materialized, glowing with more intense radiance.
TIER TWO: GRAND PRINCIPLES
Characteristics:
|-Limited in number of practitioners who can utilize them
-Normally holds significantly more power than Normal Principles
|-Often requires specific lineage, inheritance, or earned right to access(Nurtured as Seeds)
-Integration more complex, demanding greater existential
investment

"Grand Principles are where things get interesting," RUINEDEN continued, her voice warming with enthusiasm. "These aren't shared resources...they're restricted access. Only certain beings can utilize them, and often, teaching them to others is complex of a process."
She gestured to specific examples.

"All nine Principles that Elyndra possesses are Grand tier," she said, pulling up their specifications. "Principle of Eternal Growth, Principle of Cyclical Harvest, Principle of Fertile Abundance...each one limited in how many practitioners can exist simultaneously." The diagrams showed how Grand Principles operated differently from Normal ones, their architecture more complex, their integration more demanding, their payoff exponentially greater.
"The Convergent Prosperity before us is also Grand tier," RUINEDEN

added, gesturing toward the golden tree. "Limited number of practitioners can nurture it, though many can benefit from its effects once manifested. That's common pattern for collaborative Principles... few can cultivate them, but many can utilize results."
Noah processed this information with calculating precision, already considering implications for his own development! But RUINEDEN's expression shifted again.
"And then," she said, her voice dropping to tones that carried weight
of genuine significance, "there is a tier far above all of these. A classification so exclusive, so fundamentally unique, that I'm taking liberty of creating self-proclaimed designation for it."
A third tier materialized in the display, blazing with radiance that
made the previous categories look dim by comparison. TIER THREE: SINGULARITY PRINCIPLES (RUIN/EDEN
Classification)
[Characteristics:|
-Available ONLY to the entity who discovered and nurtured them
|-Cannot be taught, cannot be shared, cannot be replicated -Met such terrifying conditions during development that only
original cultivator's existence can contain them -Power ceiling theoretically unlimited, scaling with user's
advancement
-Represent fundamental uniqueness of practitioner's Way
RUINEDEN's expression carried satisfaction at having codified something she clearly considered important theoretical advancement. "In this tier," she explained, her voice carrying emphasis that made

every word significant, "the Principle is bound to a single existence so completely that separation is impossible without destroying both Principle and practitioner. These are singular by definition. One practitioner, one Principle, indivisible."

chapters.title: Chapter 4358 The Farmer's Greeting III
paragraphs: She paused, then delivered the critical examples.
"Perpetual Harvest and the Cheating Architect both fall into this category."

Noah's own Principles...the foundations of his rapid advancement, the cornerstones of his impossible accumulation, the core components of his Way...were so unique that no other entities could hold them.
Not because they were particularly powerful (though they were).
Not because they were difficult to understand (though they might be).
But because they had met conditions during their cultivation that made them fundamentally tied to Noah's specific existence in ways that couldn't be replicated.
Because...who could possibly hold The Cheating Architect?

"Well," RUINEDEN amended, her expression shifting slightly, "The Infiniverse also has access to Perpetual Harvest, but that's special case. She was akin to the sentient farmland that Perpetual Harvest grew from...the soil that nurtured the Seed into full bloom. So both your existences have access to it because she's fundamentally part of your cultivation architecture."
Her voice took on more analytical tones.

"Actually, calling her just 'part' of your Civilization undersells her significance. The Infiniverse is akin to grand instrument of your Civilization. More accurately..." she paused, choosing words carefully, "...she is the backbone of your Civilization. The foundational infrastructure upon which everything else is built."
Noah nodded calmly at this.
The Infiniverse...his Early Veiled Shore, his sanctuary, his accumulating domain- wasn't just territory he controlled.
She was living architecture, sentient foundation, entity whose existence was so intertwined with his own that separating them would collapse both.
She was simultaneously part of him and separate from him, extension of his will that possessed her own consciousness.
RUINEDEN continued, her voice taking on more speculative tones.

"Principles like Perpetual Harvest and the Cheating Architect.." she paused, her expression growing more serious, "...should be good guides toward the next Scale of Existence. Toward the distinction of THE."

"Think about it," RUINEDEN continued, "THE Living Existences all possess authorities that are fundamentally unique to them. THE Living Order's authority over structure and hierarchy...no one else can replicate it. THE Living Paradox's control over true contradictory states...singular to his existence. THE Living Emotive's mastery over feelings and experiences...truly bound to him alone."
Her diagrams shifted, showing parallels between THE Living Existences' authorities and Noah's Singularity Principles.

"Your Perpetual Harvest and Cheating Architect operate on similar paradigm," she explained. "They're fundamentally yours in ways that make them unreplicable. That suggests you're already walking path toward THE, whether intentionally or not. Your Principles are exhibiting characteristics that match how THE-tier authorities function."
She paused, then added with calculating precision, "Which means the question isn't whether you can reach THE, but whether you'll survive long enough to complete the journey."
HUUM!
"I need a few more minutes here," RUIN/EDEN said, shifting back to more immediate concerns as her analytical capabilities engaged fully with the golden tree.

"I'm nearly finished breaking down the architecture of The Convergent Prosperity. Once complete analysis is done, I can make it the first Grand Principle that the Infiniverse can nurture and produce en masse for those in your Civilization to obtain."
Her expression carried satisfaction at the prospect.

"Imagine it," she continued, her voice warming with enthusiasm. "Your people, able to pool their power through properly cultivated collaborative Principle. Able to manifest The Abundant Colossus when defending your Shore. Able to coordinate attacks that individual capability couldn't achieve. It would transform your Civilization from collection of powerful individuals into unified force that operates as
single organism when necessary."
Noah nodded, satisfaction blooming in his mind.
The Infiniverse.
His smile deepened as he thought about her, who had been quietly working in background, forging wonders without needing constant attention or praise.
She was silent without making flashy moves, but she was already doing unfathomable things.
As if sensing his thoughts, RUIN/EDEN's expression shifted into something that resembled conspiratorial smile.

"Speaking of The Infiniverse," she said, her voice taking on tones that suggested she was about to share secret, "Sis Infiniverse has actually been utilizing my help to forge a surprise for Master. Something special that we've been developing in background while you were focused on other advancements."
Her smile widened.
"Would you like to know what it is?" she asked, her tone suggesting she was offering forbidden knowledge. "Fair warning...it would spoil the surprise. But I can tell you if you want."
Noah considered for a moment, his thoughts weighing curiosity against the satisfaction of being genuinely surprised by something.
Finally, he shook his head.
"No," he said simply, his voice carrying amusement. "Let her surprise me. I trust whatever she's creating will be worth the wait." RUIN/EDEN nodded, her expression carrying approval at his restraint.
But then her smile took on more mischievous qualities. "Master," she said, her voice carrying notes of professional advice, "I
also feel obligated to point out that if you could choose to...get friendlier on Elyndra sooner rather than later, we would make significantly more advancements on Principles."
She gestured, creating illusory diagrams that showed potential knowledge gains from closer integration with The First Farmer's
daughter.
"She possesses nine Grand Principles operating in perfect harmony," RUIN/EDEN continued, her tone clinical despite the absurdity of what she was suggesting.
"Direct... intimate contact would allow me to analyze those Principles
as at this moment, I can't truly gain much. The data we could acquire
through close integration would be invaluable."
Her smile widened further.
"You...need to sacrifice your innocence, Master," she said with mock seriousness, "for the sake of research. Think of the scientific
advancement!"
WAA!
Noah shook his head, smile tugging at his lips despite himself.
What innocence? He'd lost that particular commodity long ago! But as he looked at RUINEDEN...at her animated expression, her mischievous smile, her increasingly complex mannerisms...he felt
happy.
As if he was seeing Ruination at her fullest. How she always wanted to be with him, but never got the chance.
Her existence truly was becoming more alive with personality as he
advanced. Each breakthrough in his power, each new capability of the
Cheating Architect, each expansion of his consciousness seemed to grant her additional depth of character. She was evolving into something complex!

RUINEDEN continued, her voice taking on more speculative tones.
"Principles like Perpetual Harvest and the Cheating Architect.." she paused, her expression growing more serious, "...should be good guides toward the next Scale of Existence.
Toward the distinction of THE."
"Think about it," RUINEDEN continued, "THE Living Existences all possess authorities that are fundamentally unique to them.
THE Living Order's authority over structure and hierarchy...no one else can replicate it.
THE Living Paradox's control over true contradictory states...singular to his existence.
THE Living Emotive's mastery over feelings and experiences...truly bound to him alone."
Her diagrams shifted, showing parallels between THE Living Existences' authorities and Noah's Singularity Principles.
"Your Perpetual Harvest and Cheating Architect operate on similar paradigm," she explained.
"They're fundamentally yours in ways that make them unreplicable.
That suggests you're already walking path toward THE, whether intentionally or not.
Your Principles are exhibiting characteristics that match how THE-tier authorities function."
She paused, then added with calculating precision, "Which means the question isn't whether you can reach THE, but whether you'll survive long enough to complete the journey."
HUUM!
"I need a few more minutes here," RUIN/EDEN said, shifting back to more immediate concerns as her analytical capabilities engaged fully with the golden tree.
"I'm nearly finished breaking down the architecture of The Convergent Prosperity.
Once complete analysis is done, I can make it the first Grand Principle that the Infiniverse can nurture and produce en masse for those in your Civilization to obtain."
Her expression carried satisfaction at the prospect.
"Imagine it," she continued, her voice warming with enthusiasm.
"Your people, able to pool their power through properly cultivated collaborative Principle.
Able to manifest The Abundant Colossus when defending your Shore.
Able to coordinate attacks that individual capability couldn't achieve.
It would transform your Civilization from collection of powerful individuals into unified force that operates as
single organism when necessary."
Noah nodded, satisfaction blooming in his mind.
The Infiniverse.
His smile deepened as he thought about her, who had been quietly working in background, forging wonders without needing constant attention or praise.
She was silent without making flashy moves, but she was already doing unfathomable things.
As if sensing his thoughts, RUIN/EDEN's expression shifted into something that resembled conspiratorial smile.
"Speaking of The Infiniverse," she said, her voice taking on tones that suggested she was about to share secret, "Sis Infiniverse has actually been utilizing my help to forge a surprise for Master.
Something special that we've been developing in background while you were focused on other advancements."
Her smile widened.
"Would you like to know what it is?" she asked, her tone suggesting she was offering forbidden knowledge.
"Fair warning...it would spoil the surprise.
But I can tell you if you want."
Noah considered for a moment, his thoughts weighing curiosity against the satisfaction of being genuinely surprised by something.
Finally, he shook his head.
"No," he said simply, his voice carrying amusement.
"Let her surprise me.
I trust whatever she's creating will be worth the wait." RUIN/EDEN nodded, her expression carrying approval at his restraint.
But then her smile took on more mischievous qualities.
"Master," she said, her voice carrying notes of professional advice, "I
also feel obligated to point out that if you could choose to...get friendlier on Elyndra sooner rather than later, we would make significantly more advancements on Principles."
She gestured, creating illusory diagrams that showed potential knowledge gains from closer integration with The First Farmer's
daughter.
"She possesses nine Grand Principles operating in perfect harmony," RUIN/EDEN continued, her tone clinical despite the absurdity of what she was suggesting.
"Direct... intimate contact would allow me to analyze those Principles
as at this moment, I can't truly gain much.
The data we could acquire
through close integration would be invaluable."
Her smile widened further.
"You...need to sacrifice your innocence, Master," she said with mock seriousness, "for the sake of research.
Think of the scientific
advancement!"
WAA!
Noah shook his head, smile tugging at his lips despite himself.
What innocence?
He'd lost that particular commodity long ago!
But as he looked at RUINEDEN...at her animated expression, her mischievous smile, her increasingly complex mannerisms...he felt
happy.
As if he was seeing Ruination at her fullest.
How she always wanted to be with him, but never got the chance.
Her existence truly was becoming more alive with personality as he
advanced.
Each breakthrough in his power, each new capability of the
Cheating Architect, each expansion of his consciousness seemed to grant her additional depth of character.
She was evolving into something complex!

chapters.title: Chapter 4359 The Farmer's Greeting IV
paragraphs: It was beautiful to witness, even when that emerging personality was suggesting he seduce powerful beings for research purposes.
But as Noah turned his attention away from RUINEDEN's mischievous recommendations, he noticed a presence that had materialized beside him while he'd been focused on internal conversation.
Elyndra.

She stood silently, her vibrant form radiating that particular authority of nine Principles operating in harmony, her blue eyes fixed on the golden tree with expression that suggested she was lost in thought rather than observing her surroundings.
She seemed... sad.
Not overtly, not dramatically, but carrying weight of someone wrestling with internal conflict that had no satisfying resolution. Noah silently gazed at her.
Elyndra stood beside Noah, her consciousness focused on the golden tree that truly represented collaboration in its purest form.

But her thoughts were elsewhere, cycling through everything that had led to this moment...her father's condition, the task he'd assigned her, the conflict between what she believed and what necessity demanded.
She knew her father.
Had known him for eons, when he'd been powerful enough, when his cultivation had brought him to threshold of that fundamental
distinction.
He had lived his whole life aligned with what was right. With what it meant to be good.

Saving as many Fold Dwellers as possible, creating sanctuary for those who had nowhere else to go, even allowing inclusion of Living Existences despite their historical prejudice against Fold Dwellers as lesser beings.

He had done everything according to principles that agricultural cultivation had taught him...that growth came through nurturing rather than exploitation, that collaboration produced better results than competition, that patience and care yielded harvests that force and haste could never achieve.
And where had it gotten him?
Shattered by THE Living Emotive, reduced to weakness that made even standing difficult, poisoned against healing that might restore what had been destroyed.

Horrible beings like THE Living Emotive did what they wanted with impunity and without any consequences. They acted according to pure malice refined into authority, and existence itself seemed to reward them for it rather than punish them.

THE Creature was supposed to be the one to balance things out. To keep THE Living Paradox in check, to prevent THE Living Existences from becoming monsters who consumed everything in pursuit of their own advancement.
And yet even he was nowhere to be seen. Absent when needed most, leaving beings like her father to suffer consequences of system that rewarded cruelty over compassion.
Her father was...tired.
Tired of doing things the right way and watching it accomplish nothing. Tired of being good while others thrived through being terrible.
Tired of principles that felt increasingly like chains rather than guidance.
She understood why he was suggesting they take what they needed
from Noah rather than negotiating for it. Why he believed collaboration wouldn't work, that force was necessary, that adopting methods of THE Living Existences was only path forward.

He knew he could try collaboration. Maybe it would finally work out. Maybe Noah would be reasonable, would give up Perpetual Harvest willingly, would help restore what THE Living Emotive had destroyed.
But her Father... was tired of maybes.

He wanted certainty, like THE Living Emotive possessed. Success, like THE Living Paradox had achieved. Power that couldn't be taken away, accumulated through methods that worked regardless of whether they were right or wrong.
And how did THE Living Existences succeed?
By taking what they wanted.
Elyndra felt sadness crystallize in her chest, heavy and cold.
She didn't believe it. Her very existence told her they should be forging their own Way, advancing according to principles they chose rather than imitating paths that others had walked.
To build their Civilization, it should be done according to their own methods. Their own understanding. Their own values.
They shouldn't deviate to follow how others proceeded. Shouldn't take hints from The Way of beings they opposed. Shouldn't become the thing they resisted just because it seemed effective.
Her father was doing exactly that...abandoning his Way in favor of methods that had brought THE Living Existences success but had also made them into monsters.
And if he did that, if he truly went about things through betrayal and theft rather than cultivation and collaboration...
He may have forever lost his way.
He may have corrupted it beyond recovery, because even if he
obtained Perpetual Harvest through deception, even if he restored his power through stolen Principle...
He would never reach THE.
Because he wouldn't have done it his Way. He would have achieved it through imitation of methods that were fundamentally opposed to everything his cultivation had been built upon.
But she couldn't find herself able to tell her father that she thought
his Way may have gotten irreparably damaged. That his desperate attempt to restore what was lost might actually guarantee he could never reclaim what truly mattered.

How could she say such things to someone who was dying? Who had sacrificed everything for principles that had brought him nothing but suffering? Who deserved rest and restoration rather than philosophical lectures about corruption of purpose?
So what could she do?
Stand beside him as he destroyed himself trying to save himself?
Refuse his request and watch him die knowing she could have helped but chose not to? Try to change his mind when exhaustion and pain had made him incapable of hearing arguments about long-term
consequences?
There were no good options.
Only varieties of betrayal... of Osmont, of her father, or of herself.
At this time, Noah's calm voice cut through her spiral of internal
conflict.
"You seem sad."
The observation was delivered without judgment, without prying curiosity, just simple acknowledgment of what was obvious to anyone
paying attention.
Elyndra turned to look at him, finding his expression calm.
"Yeah," she replied, allowing honesty to color her voice. "I am a bit
melancholic and sad. Existence... can be unfair. Very, very unfair."
Noah nodded, his gaze returning to the golden tree.
"Yes, it is unfair," he said, his tone carrying acceptance rather than complaint. "But from that unfairness comes struggle, and from that struggle... wonders can bloom."
The words landed with weight that made Elyndra pause.
From unfairness comes struggle, and from struggle comes wonders.
It was perspective she needed to hear, reminder that hardship wasn't
just obstacle but potentially catalyst.
That the difficult her father that she faced, that everyone struggled against...they weren't just barriers to overcome but conditions that could produce achievements impossible under easier
circumstances.
She sighed, nodding slowly as she focused more fully on Noah. Maybe there was still path forward that didn't require betrayal. Maybe collaboration could work if she presented it properly. Maybe...
No.
She stopped herself. No more maybes. Time to be direct.
"While my Father is in the state he is in," she began, her voice taking
on more formal tones, "it does not mean his efforts are diminished any less. His Sanctuary still has countless things to offer." She gestured broadly to encompass the fields around them.
"One of the major offerings...the Produce that the Living Existences you came with were planned to be given...grants 1000 Quadrillion Complexity and Purity or more per consumption."
WAA!
"The trade-off is that it completely limits one's advancement and

potential thereafter. It's shortcut to immense power, but it's also ceiling that can never be exceeded. Those who consume Father's highest-tier Produce gain tremendous immediate strength but sacrifice all future growth."
She continued detailing other achievements, her voice warming with pride despite her earlier melancholy.
"We also have Seeds that can be used as weapons- projectiles that

move faster than even the perception of entities exceeding 1 or 3 Quintillion in power. When triggered, they explode with force that could collapse beings with 3 or 4 Quintillion Complexity and Purity." Her eyes found Noah's, holding his gaze with intensity. "We have techniques for nurturing Principles that predate modern cultivation methods. We have knowledge about THE Living Existences that few outside the Earliest Folds possess. We have resources accumulated over eons of careful agricultural development." She paused, then delivered what she clearly considered the most
important information.
"With the coming Fallout," she said, her voice carrying weight of
confession, "my Father believes it is only possible to overcome it by having an entity at the distinction of THE. Which is... an impossibility almost, given current circumstances and timelines."
"So he nurtured me. At my peak, with the inherent nature of my

existence and nine converging Principles, if I use enough nurturing from other sources- collapsed weavings of Prime Dead Early Creatures, the Existential Armors they forge, other complex atrocities that contain concentrated power...I can reach a state of THE False Harvest. A False part of My Way"
She paused, making sure he understood the significance. "Momentary. False. Unstable. But I can achieve such power briefly,"
she continued. "Burning up everything accumulated, sacrificing all reserves, pushing beyond normal limits...the moment The Fallout descends, I could protect this Sanctuary and those within it."
Her blue eyes blazed with determination mixed with desperation. "We do not have to become The Dead to survive," she said, her voice
carrying conviction. "This was my father's goal. This was what all his cultivation aimed toward."
She took a breath, then delivered what was clearly request that mattered more than anything else.
"I would be immensely grateful if we can work together to achieve
this
goal."

chapters.title: Chapter 4360 The Farmer's Greeting V
paragraphs: The words buzzed between them.
Noah continued staring at the tree ahead, his expression thoughtful as he processed everything she'd said.
Then, he smiled with genuine curiosity.
"What is wrong with all of us becoming The Dead?" he asked.

"We could all survive being collapsed and return again a day later. Sounds like elegant solution to surviving The Fallout, doesn't it?" Elyndra blinked, her expression cycling through confusion before settling into something resembling disbelief.
She studied his features, trying to determine if he was joking or if he genuinely didn't know.

"You do know," she said slowly, carefully, as if explaining fundamental truth to someone who somehow missed it, "that the Curse of The Dead, and anything to do with THE Creature, means that all Dead Existences are completely cut off from ever reaching the next Scale of Existence, right?"
Her voice grew more emphatic.

"That was the cost for such a terrifying capability. THE Creature granted The Dead the ability to return from collapse, to survive what should be absolute ending, to persist through conditions that would unmake Living Existences. But in exchange, they can never advance beyond their current Scale. They are trapped, forever, at whatever level they possessed when they crossed The Veil."
She paused, making sure he absorbed the information.
"Becoming The Dead isn't just transformation...it's permanent limitation. A ceiling that can never be exceeded. An end to all potential growth in exchange for impossible survival."
Noah's eyes turned immensely sharp at this revelation.
He looked at Elyndra up and down.
But her expression carried no deception...just certainty born from knowledge that she considered fundamental truth of existence.
The Dead couldn't reach the next Scale of Existence.
They were trapped, forever, at whatever level they'd achieved before crossing The Veil.
Which meant that if he became Dead, if he crossed to the other side, if he chose survival through that method...
He would never reach THE.
Never advance beyond his current Scale, no matter how much power he accumulated, no matter how many Principles he integrated, no matter what achievements his Way produced.
It would be ceiling disguised as salvation, trap baited with immortality, permanent limitation masquerading as ultimate survival technique.
What of his Arch Lich though? Did his type of Death align with THE Creature's Curse? Or was he purer?
Noah simply stared out toward the tree silently, his thoughts racing through implications!
So that probability stream RUINEDEN had shown him...the one where THE Dead Order captured him and turned him into battery for her Civilization, wasn't just horrifying because of the loss of freedom.

It was catastrophic because it would permanently cap his advancement. Would lock him into current Scale of Existence forever, removing any possibility of reaching heights he was apparently already walking toward.
The Dead couldn't reach THE.
Which meant THE Dead Order couldn't either, despite her immense power. She wasnt fully...THE...Unless she unified with Sigrid!
She was trapped on that side of The Veil, unable to cross over or advance further, limited by the very method that had allowed her to survive when THE Living Order had collapsed.
Once someone crossed The Veil and became Dead, they were no longer competition. They were permanently locked out of ever challenging THE Living Existences' positions.
Was that why Khor and others were potentially collapsed?
Elyndra took his silence as confirmation that he'd been joking, her expression relaxing slightly as she sighed.

"So," she said, returning to her earlier question, "do you think a collaboration is possible? With your Perpetual Harvest, cultivating what even father could not bloom, we could accomplish goals that many outside THE Loom seek to accomplish."
She paused, her blue eyes finding his with intensity that carried genuine hope mixed with determination.
"As I said before," she continued, her voice softening, "I would like to
be your friend."
Noah looked at the figure of Elyndra...at her astonishing beauty, her nine converging Principles, her genuine desire for collaboration mixed with hidden agenda he suspected but couldn't confirm.
Then his gaze shifted to the distant figure of The First Farmer, who was gazing at groups of countless beings in his sanctuary with expression that seemed calm and benevolent.
Finally, Noah smiled.

"Collaboration is possible," he said simply, his voice carrying certainty. "And I would like to see the weapons of The First Farmer. If we're going to work together, I should understand what resources are
available."
Elyndra's smile blazed brilliant enough to make existence in the entire area seem a shade brighter, her blue eyes shining with joy.
She stretched out her hand toward Noah, her thumb and two fingers
raised in gesture he didn't recognize.
Noah raised his eyebrows. "What are you doing?"
Elyndra blinked, then turned her head slightly, confusion flickering
across her features.
"Oh," she said, realization dawning. "You don't know the Farmer's Greeting? It's a gesture- three fingers waved at a distance, or connecting like a handshake when up close."
She smiled, moving closer.
"It's akin to blessing and wishing a good harvest and prosperity to the
other party. Here, let me show you."
She motioned to Noah's hands, and he brought his thumb, index finger, and middle finger forward as she'd demonstrated.
Their fingertips touched...three points of contact forming triangle of connection between them.
Elyndra's smile became radiant, her blue eyes shining brilliantly with
genuine warmth.

In that moment, she seemed to have forgotten the heavy task laid upon her by her father, forgotten the conflict between duty and principle, forgotten everything except the simple joy of teaching someone about her culture's traditions.
"There you go," she said, her voice carrying delight. "Your first Farmer's Greeting. I wish you boundless harvest and prosperity, Friend."
Noah looked at this astonishingly gorgeous being, at her vibrant
presence, her genuine warmth...and calmly smiled.

"And a boundless harvest to you as well," he said coolly. Their fingers remained connected for moment longer than strictly necessary, the gesture lingering in space between them. Then they separated, the moment passing as Elyndra began explaining details about the Sanctuary's weapons and resources with enthusiasm.

Noah's consciousness shifted, pulling away from the Wandering Territories, from the golden tree and Elyndra's complicated presence, returning to his Early Veiled Shore where something magnificent was reaching completion.
He stood on the golden sands, his form perfectly still as he observed the final stages of construction happening in spaces that existed simultaneously within and beyond normal reality.
The Incarnaut Sanctis.
The Early Chamber of Blood.
The space where genesis of new Early Creatures would occur, where
beings of sufficient potential could undergo transformation that would elevate them to tier of existence that current reality insisted
was closed.
He thought about his interaction with Elyndra, about the
collaboration she proposed.
In his mind, RUIN/EDEN's voice emerged with tones that carried amusement mixed with professional assessment.
"The Daughter of The First Farmer might pounce on you before you
pounce on her. Master's charms are unbeaten as always." Noah shook his head at such words.
"Stop playing around," he said, his voice carrying command wrapped
in fondness. "Finish Incarnaut Sanctis, the Chamber of Blood. Let us
bring the newest Mana-Born Early Creatures to fruition."
He paused, his eyes blazing with tyrannical light.
"Let us usher in...The Glorious Evolution."
HUUM!
RUINEDEN's response was singular, her voice carrying certainty that
transcended artificial origin.
"Yes, Master."
And on the golden sands of the Early Veiled Shore, the Chamber
completed its formation with pulse of authority that announced to existence itself that something new and impossible had just achieved
manifestation.
The genesis was ready to begin!

The Dead couldn't reach THE.
Which meant THE Dead Order couldn't either, despite her immense power.
She wasnt fully...THE...Unless she unified with Sigrid!
She was trapped on that side of The Veil, unable to cross over or advance further, limited by the very method that had allowed her to survive when THE Living Order had collapsed.
Once someone crossed The Veil and became Dead, they were no longer competition.
They were permanently locked out of ever challenging THE Living Existences' positions.
Was that why Khor and others were potentially collapsed?
Elyndra took his silence as confirmation that he'd been joking, her expression relaxing slightly as she sighed.
"So," she said, returning to her earlier question, "do you think a collaboration is possible?
With your Perpetual Harvest, cultivating what even father could not bloom, we could accomplish goals that many outside THE Loom seek to accomplish."
She paused, her blue eyes finding his with intensity that carried genuine hope mixed with determination.
"As I said before," she continued, her voice softening, "I would like to
be your friend."
Noah looked at the figure of Elyndra...at her astonishing beauty, her nine converging Principles, her genuine desire for collaboration mixed with hidden agenda he suspected but couldn't confirm.
Then his gaze shifted to the distant figure of The First Farmer, who was gazing at groups of countless beings in his sanctuary with expression that seemed calm and benevolent.
Finally, Noah smiled.
"Collaboration is possible," he said simply, his voice carrying certainty.
"And I would like to see the weapons of The First Farmer.
If we're going to work together, I should understand what resources are
available."
Elyndra's smile blazed brilliant enough to make existence in the entire area seem a shade brighter, her blue eyes shining with joy.
She stretched out her hand toward Noah, her thumb and two fingers
raised in gesture he didn't recognize.
Noah raised his eyebrows.
"What are you doing?"
Elyndra blinked, then turned her head slightly, confusion flickering
across her features.
"Oh," she said, realization dawning.
"You don't know the Farmer's Greeting?
It's a gesture- three fingers waved at a distance, or connecting like a handshake when up close."
She smiled, moving closer.
"It's akin to blessing and wishing a good harvest and prosperity to the
other party.
Here, let me show you."
She motioned to Noah's hands, and he brought his thumb, index finger, and middle finger forward as she'd demonstrated.
Their fingertips touched...three points of contact forming triangle of connection between them.
Elyndra's smile became radiant, her blue eyes shining brilliantly with
genuine warmth.

In that moment, she seemed to have forgotten the heavy task laid upon her by her father, forgotten the conflict between duty and principle, forgotten everything except the simple joy of teaching someone about her culture's traditions.
"There you go," she said, her voice carrying delight.
"Your first Farmer's Greeting.
I wish you boundless harvest and prosperity, Friend."
Noah looked at this astonishingly gorgeous being, at her vibrant
presence, her genuine warmth...and calmly smiled.
"And a boundless harvest to you as well," he said coolly.
Their fingers remained connected for moment longer than strictly necessary, the gesture lingering in space between them.
Then they separated, the moment passing as Elyndra began explaining details about the Sanctuary's weapons and resources with enthusiasm.

Noah's consciousness shifted, pulling away from the Wandering Territories, from the golden tree and Elyndra's complicated presence, returning to his Early Veiled Shore where something magnificent was reaching completion.
He stood on the golden sands, his form perfectly still as he observed the final stages of construction happening in spaces that existed simultaneously within and beyond normal reality.
The Incarnaut Sanctis.
The Early Chamber of Blood.
The space where genesis of new Early Creatures would occur, where
beings of sufficient potential could undergo transformation that would elevate them to tier of existence that current reality insisted
was closed.
He thought about his interaction with Elyndra, about the
collaboration she proposed.
In his mind, RUIN/EDEN's voice emerged with tones that carried amusement mixed with professional assessment.
"The Daughter of The First Farmer might pounce on you before you
pounce on her.
Master's charms are unbeaten as always." Noah shook his head at such words.
"Stop playing around," he said, his voice carrying command wrapped
in fondness.
"Finish Incarnaut Sanctis, the Chamber of Blood.
Let us
bring the newest Mana-Born Early Creatures to fruition."
He paused, his eyes blazing with tyrannical light.
"Let us usher in...The Glorious Evolution."
HUUM!
RUINEDEN's response was singular, her voice carrying certainty that
transcended artificial origin.
"Yes, Master."
And on the golden sands of the Early Veiled Shore, the Chamber
completed its formation with pulse of authority that announced to existence itself that something new and impossible had just achieved
manifestation.
The genesis was ready to begin!

chapters.title: Chapter 4361 The Glorious Evolution! I
paragraphs: Noah stood on the golden sands, his consciousness fully focused on this body after experiencing the complicated interactions in the Wandering Territories.
Here, in his sanctuary, in the space that was both his domain and extension of his very existence, something magnificent had reached completion.
The Incarnaut Sanctis.
The Chamber of Blood.
It rose near the center of the Early Veiled Shore like monument, its structure defying casual description through sheer grandeur.
The Chamber appeared as massive heart-shaped construct, but calling it merely "heart-shaped" undersold the architectural magnificence!

It was as if someone had taken the conceptual ideal of what a heart should be...the perfect organ pumping life through existence, and given it physical form using materials that reality itself envied.
The structure blazed with crimson-gold radiance that made nearby space pulse in sympathetic rhythm, as if the Shore itself recognized this as vital organ rather than simple building.
The exterior surface appeared organic yet crystalline, smooth yet textured with patterns that showed veins and arteries carved into impossibly dense material.
But it was the blue lines that truly commanded attention.
Countless brilliant blue vessels pulsed across the Chamber's surface like living circulatory system made manifest.
They weren't painted or carved...they were actual conduits of concentrated Mana, visible through semi-transparent sections of the
structure.

Radiant blue arteries thick as tree trunks extended from the Chamber's apex, branching into progressively smaller vessels that covered every surface. Blue veins ran along the Chamber's base, pulsing with rhythm that matched Noah's own heartbeat.
And from multiple points around the structure, massive conduits... arteries that could have served as highways, extended outward and sank directly into the Early Veiled Shore itself.
These weren't just decorative elements. They were functional integration points, connections that bound the Chamber to the Shore so completely that separating them was almost an impossibility.
It was beautiful!
This was architecture that served purpose, form following function to create something that was simultaneously tool and artwork, machine and organism, construct and living entity.
Noah approached the Chamber with measured steps, his eyes tracking across its surface with analytical precision that cataloged every detail.
RUIN/EDEN's holographic form materialized beside him.
"The Incarnaut Sanctis is complete," she announced.
"Integration with your Early Veiled Shore successful. All systems operational. The Chamber of Blood is ready to begin its purpose."
She gestured, and prompts began cascading across Noah's vision with technical specifications.
INCARNAUT SANCTIS - OPERATIONAL STATUS]
Classification: Engine of Civilization (Tier: Foundational)|
Integration Level: 100% - Bound to Early Veiled Shore and Noah Osmont's existence]
Function: Evolution Chamber for entities following the Way of the Mana Architect
Current Capacity: 9 Evolutions

"The Incarnaut Sanctis is connected deeply to you and your Early Veiled Shore," she said, her words accompanied by illusory diagrams showing the integration points. "It functions as another Engine of Civilization, similar to your Resplendent Citadels but serving different purpose."

The diagrams showed how the Chamber drew power from multiple sources...from Noah's Heart directly, from the Shore's accumulated authority, from Perpetual Harvest's continuous flow, from reserves of Mana that had been stockpiled through countless harvests.

"It should become one of the foremost tools for your emerging Civilization," RUINEDEN continued, her tone warming with enthusiasm. "The mechanism is elegantly simple: anyone following your Way can enter the Chamber. They walk through its structure, navigating passages that test their resolve and compatibility with your Principles. And when they reach the very center..."
She paused for emphasis.
"Their existence will be anchored with the Chamber itself. Bound through connections that cannot be severed. And once anchored, they undergo rapid evolution that completely alters their existence."
Her expression grew more animated.

"Evolution, in its truest sense, is change over time. Gradual adaptation to environmental pressures. Incremental improvements accumulated across generations until species that began as simple organisms become complex entities capable of contemplating their own
existence."
The diagrams shifted, showing timelines that stretched across eons.

"But what we're creating here," RUIN/EDEN continued, her voice growing more intense, "is not that. This is not gradual change. This is not incremental adaptation. This is Evolution compressed into single transformative moment...the greatest change possible in the shortest
period of time."
Her eyes blazed with excitement.
"Those who enter the Incarnaut Sanctis and reach its center will have

their hearts transformed," she explained, each word weighted with significance. "Their existing cardiovascular systems, whether biological or existential, will be completely restructured. Replaced. Rebuilt from foundational level upward."
The diagrams showed the process in exquisite detail...hearts being unmade and remade, structures being dissolved and reformed, existence being deconstructed and reconstructed according to new
templates.

"They will emerge with Mana-Born Hearts of Early Creatures," RUINEDEN said, her voice carrying weight of fundamental transformation. "Hearts that pump not just blood but concentrated Mana. Hearts that generate power continuously rather than merely circulating it. Hearts that mark them as new species of Early Creature never before seen in the Earliest Folds or current era."

She paused, then delivered the critical specification. "And their existence will be transformed tremendously," she continued. "Because the minimal Complexity and Purity for Mana-Born Early Creatures produced from the Chamber of Blood would have been... 1 Quintillion."
Would have been.
The phrase hung in the air.
Noah walked toward the Chamber with deliberate steps, his hand

reaching out to touch its crimson-gold surface. The material felt warm beneath his palm, pulsing with rhythm that synchronized with his own heartbeat the moment contact was established. "Would have been, huh?" he said, his voice carrying knowing
amusement.
RUINEDEN's smile widened.
"Yes, Master" she said quietly.
"It would have been the baseline. But...
"Since the Chamber of Blood was somewhat in line with the
that The Infiniverse has been forging for you, she added a supplemental feature that truly revolutionized the Chamber of Blood
to grant..."
HUUM!
"...The Glorious Evolution."
The words seemed to resonate through the Shore itself, carried by
authority that made reality pulse with recognition. RUIN/EDEN's expression grew more serious as she began explaining the modifications.
"In conjunction with The Infiniverse," she said, her voice taking on

technical precision, "the Chamber of Blood was altered. Perpetual Harvest was woven deeply into its architecture, integrated so completely that every function now operates through that Principle's framework."
The diagrams shifted, showing how verdant-gold light flowed through the blue vessels, how effort and harvest had been integrated into the Chamber's very structure.
"The additional feature," RUINEDEN continued, "is Tiers of Evolution.
Not single transformation, but graduated system that rewards those who can endure greater pressure with proportionally greater results." She gestured, creating three distinct visual representations.
TIER ONE: FOUNDATIONAL EVOLUTION Requirements: Basic compatibility with Way of Mana Architect + Survival of initial transformation
Results:
-Complexity: 1 Quintillion
-Purity: 1 Quintillion
-Mana-Born Heart of an Early Creature (Standard)|
-Designation: Mana-Born Early Creature
