chapters.title: Chapter 4362 The Glorious Evolution! II
paragraphs: "The First Tier represents baseline achievement," RUINEDEN explained. "Those who enter the Chamber and survive the anchoring process will emerge with power that would make common Early Creature seem like children."
The second representation blazed brighter.
TIER TWO: ENHANCED EVOLUTION]
Requirements: Withstanding increased Mana Haki pressure + Demonstrating exceptional compatibility
Results:
-Complexity: 2 Quintillion
-Purity: 2 Quintillion
-Enhanced Mana-Born Heart of an Early Creature
-Designation: Advanced Mana-Born Early Creature
-Additional Capability: Direct Mana manipulation at scales that First Tier cannot achieve

"The Second Tier requires more," RUINEDEN continued. "Not just survival, but excellence. Not just endurance, but demonstration that the entity can bear weights that would crush weaker beings. Those who achieve this evolution emerge twice as powerful as First Tier, with capabilities that extend beyond simple power increase."
And finally, the third representation blazed with radiance that made the previous two look dim.
TIER THREE: THE GLORIOUS EVOLUTION
Requirements: Withstanding maximum Mana Haki pressure + Perfect compatibility with Way of Mana Architect + Existential resilience that transcends normal limits
Results:
-Complexity: 3 Quintillion
-Purity: 3 Quintillion
-Prime Mana-Born Heart of an Early Creature
-Designation: Prime Mana-Born Early Creature
-Additional Capabilities: Mana regeneration that approaches infinite, Authority over Mana itself within localized areas, Capability to grant temporary Mana augmentation to allies

Note: This tier represents peak achievement possible within current Chamber configuration. Those who emerge from Glorious Evolution are beings who could stand against Prime Dead Early Creatures and survive.
RUINEDEN's voice carried reverence as she explained the mechanism.

"When an entity steps into the Chamber," she said, "they will be anchored through those blue vessels you see extending throughout the structure. And once anchored, their existence will be forced to bear the Mana Haki of your... Infinite Mana."
Her expression grew more intense.

"Mana Haki is weight made manifest," she explained. "Not physical pressure, but existential weight...the crushing force of unlimited power pressing down on consciousness that has limits. It's like asking finite being to hold infinity in their hands without being crushed by the impossibility."
The diagrams showed entities being subjected to this pressure, their forms straining under burden that exceeded their capacity to comprehend.

"Depending on how much of this force they can bear," RUINEDEN continued, "depending on how long they can withstand pressure that increases exponentially with each moment, depending on whether their existence proves resilient enough to be augmented rather than
shattered... the entity will gain different tier of evolution."
She paused, making sure Noah understood the significance.
"The pressure is real. The danger is genuine. Those who cannot withstand even First Tier pressure will collapse, their existences unmade by weight they attempted to bear. But those who survive..."
Her smile widened.
"Those who survive will emerge as new species of Early Creature. Mana-Born. Forged in your Chamber. Carrying your authority. Walking your Way."
Noah's expression remained cool, but internally, satisfaction blazed!
This was his power.
This was what he could accomplish through combination of impossible Principles, reality-breaking cheat codes, and collaboration with entities who understood his vision.

He held the Incarnaut Sanctis...a Chamber that existed simultaneously within his Heart and manifested externally on his Shore. And ridiculously, with help from RUIN/EDEN and The Infiniverse, with Perpetual Harvest weaponizing effort into immediate reward...
He could now produce up to 9 Mana-Born Early Creatures.
Beings who could potentially possess power at 1, 2, or 3 Quintillion depending on their resilience and compatibility.
It was ridiculous.
It was broken.
It was his Civilization taking shape according to principles that current-era existence couldn't comprehend.
RUIN/EDEN's final words carried weight of profound
acknowledgment.
"This is the harvest and results of your effort, Master," she said.

"Everything you've accumulated, every Principle you've integrated, every impossible achievement you've accomplished...it all culminates in this capability. The power to elevate others not through slow cultivation but through transformative evolution that compresses eons into moments."
Noah smiled.
He looked around the Early Veiled Shore, his gaze tracking across the beings who had chosen to follow his Way or been bound to it through
various circumstances.
Sigrid was already a given...THE Living Order would undergo evolution, would emerge with power that matched her conceptual significance. She would be first, or among the first, because her role
was too critical to delay.
But who else?
The limit was 9 currently, though he knew that as he continued completing his Heart, as the Incarnaut Sanctis matured and integrated more deeply with his existence, that number would rise
steadily.
And when it came to effort, when it came to beings who had
demonstrated loyalty and capability...
Noah's eyes swept across the Shore, cataloging potential candidates
with calculating precision.
Henry, his Nepotism burning brightly.
Moiraine, whose paradoxical nature pulsed. The Emperor Penguin,
Malphas...
Even beings like the Arch Lich Ra'Zan, who commanded Death itself.

And bouncing in the distance, occasionally phasing through solid matter with cheerful disregard, a particularly enthusiastic Blue Slime. But as Noah's gaze swept across these potential candidates, it stopped on a figure that made him pause.
Titano.
The simple-minded giant stood near the edge of one of the Sacred
Water pools, his massive form somehow managing to project contentment despite his size.
He was looking around with expression of pure, uncomplicated happiness...just enjoying being surrounded by unique beings in a space that welcomed him.
No schemes. No hidden agendas. No complex motivations. Just Titano, happy to be here, grateful for inclusion, content with
simplicity.
Sometimes, the best candidates were the ones who didn't overthink
things.
"Titano!" Noah called out, his voice carrying across the Shore.
The simple-minded giant's head turned, his expression brightening immediately into sheepish smile.
He scratched his head, a gesture that suggested embarrassment at being singled out, then lumbered over with movements that somehow managed to be both massive and gentle.
"How can Titano help Brother?" he asked, his words carrying that particular simple-minded cadence.
Noah looked up at the giant and smiled.
"Go in there," he said, gesturing toward the Incarnaut Sanctis. "I want
to test something out. Your existence will undergo another change."
He paused, making sure Titano understood.
"If you can withstand the pressure inside as long as you can, you will
gain tremendous power. And if you gain power..." Titano's eyes lit up with understanding, his expression transforming into excitement that transcended his usual contentment.
"More power means more riches!" he declared, the logic absolutely
sound in his simple worldview.
Noah nodded, satisfaction warming him at the giant's enthusiasm.
"Yep. Go on."
Titano didn't hesitate. No questions about danger, no concerns about transformation, no complex analysis of risk versus reward.
Just immediate, trusting obedience based on belief that Brother
wouldn't lead him wrong.
The giant approached the Incarnaut Sanctis with steps that made the golden sands tremble, his massive form dwarfing the Chamber's entrance despite its substantial size.
But as he crossed the threshold, as he entered the space that existed
simultaneously in multiple dimensions, Titano's form seemed to shift, accommodating itself to interior that operated on different spatial principles than exterior suggested.
The entrance sealed behind him with pulse of crimson-gold light, and suddenly, every being on the Early Veiled Shore could sense what was happening inside!

to test something out.
Your existence will undergo another change."
He paused, making sure Titano understood.
"If you can withstand the pressure inside as long as you can, you will
gain tremendous power.
And if you gain power..." Titano's eyes lit up with understanding, his expression transforming into excitement that transcended his usual contentment.
"More power means more riches!" he declared, the logic absolutely
sound in his simple worldview.
Noah nodded, satisfaction warming him at the giant's enthusiasm.
"Yep.
Go on."
Titano didn't hesitate.
No questions about danger, no concerns about transformation, no complex analysis of risk versus reward.
Just immediate, trusting obedience based on belief that Brother
wouldn't lead him wrong.
The giant approached the Incarnaut Sanctis with steps that made the golden sands tremble, his massive form dwarfing the Chamber's entrance despite its substantial size.
But as he crossed the threshold, as he entered the space that existed
simultaneously in multiple dimensions, Titano's form seemed to shift, accommodating itself to interior that operated on different spatial principles than exterior suggested.
The entrance sealed behind him with pulse of crimson-gold light, and suddenly, every being on the Early Veiled Shore could sense what was happening inside!

chapters.title: Chapter 4363 The Glorious Evolution! III
paragraphs: Inside the Chamber of Blood, Titano stood in space that defied his understanding.

The interior was vast...impossibly vast, given exterior dimensions, and filled with those blue vessels he'd seen on the outside. But here, they weren't decorative. Here, they pulsed with purpose that made the air itself hum with potential.
Thousands of blue conduits surrounded him, each one thick as his arm, each one carrying concentrated Mana that made his skin tingle with proximity.
And then, without warning, they pulsed.
The vessels suddenly blazed brighter, their blue radiance intensifying until sharp needle-like ends emerged from their tips.
The needles shone with green-gold light...the unmistakable radiance of Perpetual Harvest integrated into every aspect of the Chamber's function.
They shot out.
Hundreds of them. Thousands of them. Mana-infused needles moving faster than Titano's enhanced perception could track, converging on him from every direction simultaneously.
SHINK! SHINK! SHINK!
The needles pierced his skin.
Titano's eyes widened with shock.
Something had pierced his skin.

His skin, which had been augmented by Lost Forgotten Principle to withstand attacks that could shatter Folds. His skin, which had never been broken by anything in his memory. His skin, which was supposed to be his ultimate defense.
And these needles just... went through it. Like it was nothing!
He tried to move, to pull away, to resist...but the needles were already anchored. Already connected. Already beginning their work.
His entire body was elevated into the air of the Chamber of Blood, suspended by thousands of conduits that had pierced through his defenses as if they weren't there.
RUINEDEN's voice echoed through Noah's consciousness, providing real-time analysis.
EVOLUTION PROCESS INITIATED
Subject: Titano
Current Status: Anchored]
Mana Infusion: Beginning
"The process has started," RUINEDEN stated, her tone carrying clinical precision mixed with evident excitement. "Immense
concentrations of pure Mana are being poured directly into the very core of Titano's existence."
The diagrams showed Mana flooding into Titano's being, not just filling reserves but transforming the container itself.

"Perpetual Harvest is nurturing every aspect of the transformation," she continued. "Every moment of endurance is being harvested and converted into additional augmentation. Every second he withstands the pressure is effort that compounds into greater results."
Her voice took on more serious tones.
"And alongside all of it, the weight of Mana Haki is beginning to be imposed."
Inside the Chamber, Titano felt it.
Weight.

This was weight of infinity trying to fit into finite space. This was the crushing burden of unlimited power pressing down on consciousness that had limits. This was Mana Haki...the existential pressure of Noah's Infinite Mana made manifest as test of worthiness.
Titano roared.
Not from pain, though pain was certainly present. Not from fear, because Titano didn't really understand fear in complex ways.

He roared because that's what you did when something heavy was pressing down on you...you pushed back with everything you had. His simple mind didn't complicate the situation with analysis of whether he could withstand this pressure or how long he could endure or what the strategic implications of failure would be.
He just... endured.
Moment after moment. Second after second. Breath after agonizing breath.
The weight increased. The pressure intensified. The Mana flooding into his existence grew thicker, more concentrated, more potent until it felt like liquid metal being poured directly into his soul.
But Titano withstood it!
HUUM!
Through sheer, stubborn, simple-minded refusal to give up because Brother had asked him to do this, and Titano didn't fail Brother.
The pressure continued building. The weight continued increasing. And Titano continued enduring, his consciousness narrowing to single point of determination...withstand, withstand, withstand!
And then, suddenly, something changed.
His forehead began to glow.
Blue light emerged from his skin, concentrating at the center of his brow with intensity that made the Chamber's own radiance seem dim.
The light coalesced, taking shape, forming symbol that pulsed with authority that transcended normal measurement.
An infinity symbol.
Brilliant blue. Perfect in its execution. Marking him as something new, something that hadn't existed before this moment.
THRESHOLD ACHIEVED
Subject has withstood sufficient Mana Haki pressure to qualify for Second Tier Evolution, and cannot proceed further.]
Initiating Enhanced Transformation Protocol
WAA!
Blinding blue light exploded outward from Titano's form, flooding the
interior of the Chamber with radiance so intense it leaked through the structure's walls and blazed across the entire Early Veiled Shore.
Every being on the Shore felt it...that pulse of transformation completing, of evolution achieving success, of new species of Early Creature coming into existence!
RUINEDEN's voice buzzed.
EVOLUTION COMPLETE Subject: Titano
Final Classification: Advanced Mana-Born Early Creature
Tier Achieved: Second - Enhanced Evolution]
Current Statistics:
-Complexity: 2,000,000,000,000,000,000 (2 Quintillion)|
-Heart Type: Enhanced Mana-Born Heart of an Early Creature
Additional Capabilities Granted:
-Direct Mana Manipulation (Advanced Tier)|
-Mana Reinforcement (Can augment physical capabilities beyond
baseline through active Mana circulation)|
-Mana Sense -Authority Integration: Lost Forgotten Principle has been preserved,
is being analyzed and enhanced through transformation "This," RUINEDEN said, "is the first Early Creature created after you,
Master. A new species never before seen in the Earliest Folds. A Mana-Born entity whose existence proves that your Way can produce wonders that traditional cultivation never imagined."
The blue light began to fade, and the vessels binding Titano retracted their needle-like ends with synchronized precision.
The giant descended slowly, his form touching the Chamber's floor
with gentleness that belied his mass.
For a moment, he stood there, processing transformation that had reshaped his existence from foundation upward.
Then he moved toward the exit, each step measured and controlled
in ways that suggested he was still adjusting to capabilities that
exceeded his previous limits.
The Chamber's entrance opened, and Titano emerged.
Noah stood waiting, his expression calm.
Because the being who walked out of the Incarnaut Sanctis was...
magnificent.
Titano had always been large, but now his form seemed refined by transformation. He appeared as golden giant...not just golden-skinned, but radiating golden light that suggested internal
power made visible.

His entire body was inscribed with brilliant blue and white lines that pulsed in rhythm with his heartbeat, patterns that weren't tattoos but actual manifestations of Mana circulating through enhanced
physiology.
His head was bald, and at the center of his forehead, shining with
authority that made reality pulse, was that brilliant blue infinity symbol...mark of his achievement, badge of his new status, proof that he had withstood weight of infinity and emerged stronger!
He came to stand before Noah, his movements controlled despite
obvious eagerness to share his experience.
"Brother," Titano said, his eyes shining with wonder, "Titano feels...
big! Free! Titano feels... magisterial!"
HUUM!
Magisterial.
The word resonated nearby!
Noah smiled.
"Yes," he said, "Magisterial indeed."

chapters.title: Chapter 4364 The Glorious Evolution! IV
paragraphs: This was his Civilization!
This was what he could accomplish when given tools and time and collaboration with entities who understood his vision.

If he had enough time, he did not doubt being able to produce entities with Quintillions of power in size. He could forge complex structure of beings who walked on a glorious Way of Existence, who stood together not through domination but through genuine advancement.
This would be the prime solution for The Fallout. Him attaining THE distinction by elevating his power and his Way, forming Civilization that could not be wiped out even by THE Loom itself!
He simply needed time.
After Titano, there would be others.
Noah's eyes flashed as he looked toward thr others he'd already identified.
As he contemplated these possibilities...
HUUM!
He felt tremor across the Early Veiled Shore.
Not danger. Not threat. But recognition...of completion, of achievement, of something significant reaching fruition.
He felt Perpetual Harvest pulse with fervor, the Principle becoming even more solid in his existence, its integration deepening!
And deep within The Infiniverse itself, he felt something calling out to him.
Something that buzzed with anticipation. Something that wanted to be discovered!
Something that The Infiniverse had been building while he focused on other advancement.
The surprise.
RUINEDEN's voice emerged.

"It seems the surprise of Sis Infiniverse is ready," she said, her voice warm with anticipation. "Master should be able to sense it freely. Let me know who else you would like to undergo The Glorious Evolution in the Chamber of Blood...I will take care of arrangements and ensure optimal conditions for their transformations."
She paused, then added with conspiratorial excitement.
"While you check out... the surprise."
The surprise!
Noah smiled, satisfaction deepening as he felt the shocking brilliance of Perpetual Harvest that The Infiniverse could also utilize.
It seemed she had done something particularly shocking indeed.
His body on the Early Veiled Shore flickered, existence reorganizing itself as he moved instantaneously to appear in another section deep within The Infiniverse.
Inside The Frequency of Apocalypse.
Noah materialized in region of endings.

Swirling obsidian brilliance filled the space around him, seas of dark radiance that carried concepts of ending rather than beginning. Entropy given form. Apocalypse made manifest. Cataclysm waiting to be unleashed.

This was where The Infiniverse stored and refined weavings related to conclusion rather than continuation...concepts that most beings avoided because proximity alone could collapse weaker existences. But at the center of these seas of terminal authority, of The End...
Noah saw a world.
A blue planet.

It floated in the darkness like jewel suspended in void, surrounded by seas of blue Mana that flowed around it like protective atmosphere. And beyond that, green-gold seas of Perpetual Harvest swirled.
The planet's continents and structure looked oddly familiar... eerily so, actually. The shapes, the proportions, the arrangements...
It resembled his home. The blue planet he'd been born on, that had been transformed long ago.
But beside the planet, drawing his attention with presence that commanded focus, stood The Infiniverse herself.
Her humanoid form was adorned in bejeweled green-gold dress that seemed to be woven from Perpetual Harvest made fabric, each gem pulsing with concentrated authority.
Her eyes shone with beams of green-gold light that suggested she was channeling power continuously rather than simply observing.
She bowed toward Noah with grace.
"Master," she said, "I have successfully weaponized Effort."
She had weaponized Effort?
He smiled, floating toward her.
RUINEDEN's illusory form appeared beside them, completing the trio.
The Infiniverse continued.
"I weaponized Perpetual Harvest," she explained. "Created system capable of granting you feedback of immediate harvest proportionate to effort you invest. Formed in the outline of your home..."
She gestured downward toward the blue planet.
"Below us is...The Cultivation Citadel of The Early Creature, Osmont."
HUUM!
The name alone carried weight! Heavy weight!

"Let me explain," The Infiniverse continued, "The Cultivation Citadel focuses multiple sources of existential weight...your Infinite Mana, my own authority as extension of your Early Veiled Shore, your Principles, and all other accumulated weavings of existence."
RUINEDEN picked up the explanation, her holographic form displaying technical diagrams.
"All of this weight," she said, "will be multiplied with effort through Perpetual Harvest's framework. And all of it will be imposed on you constantly when you cultivate within this space."
The diagrams showed how the system functioned...layers upon layers of pressure being applied simultaneously, each one compounding the others to create burden that would crush normal beings instantly!

"The mechanism creates stressors on your very existence," The Infiniverse continued. "Constant, unrelenting pressure that forces your being to adapt or collapse. But because Perpetual Harvest is woven into every aspect, every moment you withstand this pressure is effort that immediately harvests reward."
"Current calculations suggest a potential gain of approximately 5 Quintillion Complexity and Purity per day at maximum output."
BOOM!
What?
What?!
"If you have body cultivating within the Citadel constantly, enduring
full weight of imposed pressure without rest..."
She paused, making sure he understood the magnitude.
"You could gain 5 Quintillion per day."
The Infiniverse smiled as she pointed to the blue planet.
"The Citadel multiplies weight of existence you must withstand," she

explained. "Not just doubling or tripling...exponentially multiplying. Your Infinite Mana becomes crushing burden rather than resource. Your strength and weight are effectively turned against you. My authority becomes pressure that pins you down. Your Principles become weights attached to your consciousness."
Her voice grew more intense.
"The more multiplied weight you withstand, the more your Existence

is compressed. Compressed existence struggles under burden that exceeds its capacity. But overcoming this struggle....enduring when everything screams to give up, persisting when collapse seems inevitable, continues to grant harvests of Complexity and Purity."
RUINEDEN added final technical details. She pulled up calculations showing different pressure levels and their effects.
"Level One imposes weight equivalent to bearing your own power

twice over. Level Ten multiplies it a hundred times. Level Fifty..." she paused, "...would make you feel like you're trying to hold your entire Civilization on your shoulders while standing at bottom of ocean made from compressed concepts."
The Infiniverse's final words carried both pride and concern.

"I built this for Master," she said, her voice softening. "Others may perish the moment they enter here. A minimum of 10 Quintillion would be required for anyone who is not you to ensure they survive even lowest pressure settings."
She gestured toward the blue planet below.

"But for you, Master, this is training ground that will accelerate your advancement toward THE. This is where effort becomes harvest in most direct way possible. This is weapon I forged from your own Principle...Perpetual Harvest turned against yourself in most productive way imaginable. A methodology for the survival of The Fallout."

Noah stared at the Cultivation Citadel, at the blue planet that resembled his long-lost home, at the construction that would allow him to gain 5 Quintillion per day if he could endure its full weight.
And slowly, inevitably, his tyrannical smile widened as he patted the head of The Infiniverse!
This was his way of Existence.
These were his tools.
And with them, he would reach heights that others insisted were
impossible.
It was time to begin... The Glorious Evolution indeed, this time, with
his own advancement!
His overall people and Civilization had to be strong, but he...had to
also lead by example.
He had to undergo levels of advancement that made everyone look
upto him...and aspire for unfathomably more!
"Let's see..."
He began to float towards the blue planet, his gaze briefly glancing off
to side as he watched something distant- far outside The Infiniverse. In the region of molten crimson blue mana that used to be regions of
Collapse, he sensed the figures of Schrodinger and Leonore Rureaux approaching once more with a sense of caution.
Uniquely enough, there were currently three Schrodingers- a Living Paradox, a Living Concept, and a Living Elemental! Noah shook his head while gazing at this scene as undoubtedly, they
were here to confirm how things had ended and pursue their own solution for The Fallout.
The following of a Justiciar to their base.
But as Noah had seen with The First Farmer, the only effort to be
reliant on was himself!
Whatever others were trying to do would merely be possibilities. Side missions.
He was the solution.
"As Anaximander said...one may simply have to become the storm!"
HUUM!
His eyes were bright as he turned away from the distant scene of
Schrodingers and went into the blue planet to experience...the weaponization of effort and harvest!

But as Noah had seen with The First Farmer, the only effort to be
reliant on was himself!
Whatever others were trying to do would merely be possibilities.
Side missions.
He was the solution.
"As Anaximander said...one may simply have to become the storm!"
HUUM!
His eyes were bright as he turned away from the distant scene of
Schrodingers and went into the blue planet to experience...the weaponization of effort and harvest!

chapters.title: Chapter 4365 The Glorious Evolution! V
paragraphs: The moment Noah's body crossed through the shimmering barrier surrounding the blue planet, the Cultivation Citadel of The Early
Creature, something fundamental shifted in the relationship between his existence and reality itself.
It wasn't pain, exactly.
It was weight.
His own power, that infinite wellspring of Mana that had carried him through impossible situations, that had defied the natural order of existence time and time again...it turned against him!

Or rather, it didn't turn against him so much as it suddenly remembered that it was supposed to follow certain rules, certain laws, and those laws were now being enforced with prejudice that bordered on malicious.
The Infiniverse became an anchor dragging him down.
The Principle of Perpetual Harvest, still settling into the fundamental structure of his being, became chains wrapped around every particle of his existence.
His Infinite Mana...oh, his beautiful, impossible, reality-breaking Mana, became the very thing crushing him toward the planet's surface with acceleration that would have made gravity weep with envy!
Noah spun through the atmosphere, unable to control his descent, watching the blue sky blur into green as the landmass below rushed up to meet him with enthusiasm.
BOOM!
His body impacted the continent with force that should have shattered continents, but the ground here was different- woven from concepts of cultivation and growth that made it simultaneously
yielding and unyielding.
The crater that formed around his impact was perfectly circular, as if the very earth had been prepared for arrivals exactly like this.
Noah lay at the center of the crater for a moment, simply breathing. Each breath was work.
Each inhale required conscious effort, as if the air itself had weight, as if oxygen had decided it would only enter his lungs if he asked nicely and proved he deserved it.
He pushed himself up slowly, muscles straining against pressure that came from everywhere and nowhere simultaneously. His legs shook- actually shook, as he forced himself to stand.
When had his legs last shaken from effort? When had standing upright been anything other than automatic?
Around him, through the haze of effort, he could see rivers of green-gold light flowing through the air itself.
Perpetual Harvest was abundant here, saturating the atmosphere
with potential that should have made him stronger but somehow only made the weight heavier.
It was beautiful and terrible all at once!
Oh!
CULTIVATION CITADEL - LEVEL 1 PRESSURE ENGAGED
Environmental Analysis:|
- Current Pressure Multiplier: 2x baseline existence
- Effect: All physical actions require 2x normal effort
- Effect: All existential authority usage faces 2x resistance
-Warning: This is merely the first threshold
- Note: Adaptation is the goal, not survival
Movement Status: Severely Impaired
Mana Circulation: 1% efficiency
Physical Capability: Reduced to 0.01% normal capacity
Advisory: Even minor movements will be arduous at current
adaptation level. Once full acclimation is achieved, when this pressure feels identical to normal atmospheric conditions, higher pressure
levels may be imposed
Noah read the prompts with eyes that watered from the simple effort of focusing. His hand, which he raised to wipe his face, moved through the air like it was swimming through honey mixed with
regret.
"So this...is what weakness feels like," he murmured, his voice barely echoing despite the effort it took to speak.
He had never felt so powerful and so pathetic simultaneously. The contradiction was almost amusing.

Here he stood, an Early Creature with Quintillions of Complexity and Purity, bearer of Principles, master of Infinite Mana...and he could barely lift his own arms without his muscles screaming in protest.
It was perfect.
HARVEST NOTIFICATION
Minimal Effort Detected - Standing Upright: 12 seconds
Reward: +0.000001 Quintillion Complexity
Reward: +0.000001 Quintillion Purity
Note: Effort translates directly to harvest in this environment
Note: All actions, no matter how small, contribute to advancement
Note: The greater the pressure overcome, the greater the harvest reaped
Noah's eyes widened fractionally, and even that small expression of surprise required muscular effort that made his face ache.
Standing here, simply existing under this pressure, was advancing
him.
The weaponization of effort and harvest, indeed!
The illusory figure of RUIN/EDEN materialized beside him, her form
shimmering with blue-gold light.
"Master could attempt basic exercises to better adapt to the
pressure," she suggested.
"Push-ups, sit-ups, squats, running...all standard physical conditioning that will force your body to acclimate faster."
TRAINING RECOMMENDATIONS
Physical Exercise Options:|
- Push-ups: Force arm and core strength adaptation
- Sit-ups: Build existential endurance through repetitive motion
- Squats: Strengthen foundation and leg stability
- Running: Promote overall circulation and pressure integration
Additionally: Mana manipulation and Glyph utilization will face identical pressure applications. Conjuring even a simple fireball will require tremendous effort and controll
The struggle itself is the cultivation

Noah nodded slowly, the motion making his neck muscles burn. His existence pulsed with determination, and suddenly his upper body became bare, the simple act of dismissing his clothing taking more concentration than it should have.
His lower body was clad only in tight-fitting white-blue shorts that would have made Erikson proud, the kind of training wear that suggested serious intent without unnecessary embellishment.
His physique was on full display now...muscles that had been forged through impossible battles and cultivation that defied nature.
His torso was defined, and his abs formed ridges that could have been used as reference points for sculptors.
His shoulders and arms carried the kind of lean muscle mass that
came from actual functional strength rather than aesthetic vanity.
Under the pressure of the Cultivation Citadel, those muscles were visibly undulating, pulsing with power that was being forced to work
for every millimeter of movement.
It was glorious.
It was magisterial!
It was exactly what he needed.
Noah opened his mouth, speaking with tyrannical confidence that his
current state did nothing to diminish: "Let's have the pressure of the
fifth level." The silence that followed his declaration was profound. Even RUIN/EDEN seemed taken aback. The Infiniverse, that vast
consciousness that had been with him through so much, didn't
immediately argue or offer cautious counsel.
Instead, both replied in unison.
"Yes, Master. Be careful not to accidentally collapse the existence of
this body."
The air around Noah began to buzz.
No, that was too simple a description. The very fabric of existence
surrounding him began to press, as if reality itself was being compressed, condensed, refined into something denser and more terrible.
PRESSURE LEVEL INCREASED
WARNING: CULTIVATION CITADEL - LEVEL 5 PRESSURE ENGAGED
Environmental Analysis:
- Current Pressure Multiplier: 10x baseline existence
- Effect: All physical actions require 10x normal effort
- Effect: All existential authority usage faces 10x resistance
- Effect: Molecular cohesion of physical body under extreme stress
- Effect: Existential integrity challenged at fundamental level CRITICAL WARNING: This pressure level is designed for beings who have already adapted to Levels 1-4. Immediate imposition may result
in:|
- Physical collapse
- Existential fragmentation
- Consciousness dissolution
- Permanent structural damage to cultivation foundation
Recommendation: Return to Level 1 immediately Master's Response: [REJECTED]|
The prompts appeared and were immediately dismissed by Noah's
will. He wasn't interested in caution. He wasn't interested in the slow, methodical approach that everyone else would take.
He was interested in results!
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4366 The Glorious Evolution! VI
paragraphs: The pressure slammed down on him like the weight of multiple entire Folds condensed into a single point. Noah's knees buckled because the fundamental structure of his legs simply couldn't support the impossible weight anymore.
He crashed to his knees, the impact sending cracks through the ground beneath him despite its reinforced nature.
His body wanted to collapse further. His existence screamed at him to release the pressure, to accept defeat, to acknowledge that this was too much too fast!

Every particle of his being was being compressed, refined, tested against forces that would have unmade lesser existences entirely. His fingers, pressed against the ground, couldn't even twitch. The simple act of breathing became a battle requiring conscious effort and determination that bordered on the absurd.
It was impossible to stand.
It was impossible to move.
It was impossible to exist like this.
'Good', Noah thought through the pressure that threatened to crush his very consciousness.
'Impossible is my specialty!
HUUM!
His eyes flashed with tyrannical defiance, blazing with determination that pressure couldn't dim.
His mouth opened, and despite the tremendous effort required, despite the way his jaw muscles burned and his throat constricted, he bellowed!
"I! AM! NOAH! OSMONT!"
The words echoed across the Cultivation Citadel, carried by will more than sound.
His muscles undulated, pulsing with power that refused to accept limitation.
His Heart of an Early Creature blazed within his chest like a furnace that remembered it was supposed to burn through impossibilities.
His Citadels hummed like engines being pushed past their recommended limits.
Who was he?
He was someone who had faced down Early Creatures. Someone who had survived traversals to the Earliest Folds.
Someone who carried the weight of protecting his family, building his Civilization, defying the natural order of existence itself!
How could simple pressure make him kneel when he had so many other weights already bearing down on him?
'Rise', he commanded his body.
His muscles screamed in protest.
'RISE', he commanded his existence.
His bones creaked under impossible strain.
'RISE!' he commanded reality itself.
HUUM!
And slowly- painfully, gloriously, impossibly...he began to move!
His left hand lifted from the ground. Just an inch. Just a single inch, but it was progress measured against forces that said progress was impossible!
JEFFORT DETECTED
Current Action: Attempting to rise under 10x pressure
Assessment: Tyrannical]
Assessment: Foolish
Assessment: Magnificent
HARVEST ACCUMULATION ACCELERATING
His right hand followed, pushing against ground that felt like it was made of condensed concepts rather than simple matter.
+0.00001 Quintillion Complexity
+0.00001 Quintillion Purity
His back straightened fractionally, vertebrae stacking despite the weight trying to compress them into powder.
+0.00002 Quintillion Complexity|
+0.00002 Quintillion Purity
His legs began to unbend, muscles firing in sequences that required coordination his body barely possessed under this pressure.
+0.00005 Quintillion Complexity
+0.00005 Quintillion Purity
Sweat poured down his face, not from heat but from sheer effort. His
entire body was trembling, every muscle group engaged in the
impossible task of standing upright.
This was the weaponization of effort and harvest.
This was what it meant to turn suffering into strength, struggle into
advancement, impossibility into inevitability.
JADAPTATION BEGINNING|
Physical Structure: Reinforcing under pressure
Existential Framework: Condensing and strengthening
Mana Circulation: Pathways widening to accommodate resistance]
Principle Integration: Deepening under strain
The Early Creature, Osmont, demonstrates the fundamental truth of
cultivation:
That which does not kill you makes you stronger
That which should kill you makes you transcendent
That which transcends killing becomes the foundation of glory
Glory.
Oh, glory!
Noah's lips pulled back in a smile that was equal parts agony and
triumph.
"More," he whispered through gritted teeth.
HUUM!
"MORE." JEFFORT INCREASING
HARVEST ACCELERATING
+0.0001 Quintillion Complexity
+0.0001 Quintillion Purity
+0.0002 Quintillion Complexity
| +0.0002 Quintillion Purity]
+0.0005 Quintillion Complexity
| +0.0005 Quintillion Purity]
The numbers climbed steadily, each moment of strain translating
directly into advancement. This was different from the harvest of Inevitabilities or the cultivation from Sacred Herbs. This was pure, distilled growth born from refusing to accept limitation.
This was his Way.
He straightened fully now, standing upright under pressure that should have been impossible to bear. His body still trembled, still screamed in protest, but he was standing in the crater.
And if he could stand, he could move.
And if he could move, he could train.
And if he could train under this pressure...
The smile on his face widened as he contemplated what would
happen when he finally adapted to this level, when the impossible became merely difficult, when the difficult became routine.
Then he would increase the pressure again!
Meanwhile, in the Earliest Folds...
The glacial region had transformed into a sea of Mana so dense that it
had taken on physical properties. Blue-white waves of pure potential
lapped against crystalline shores that hadn't existed before Noah's declaration of his Way.

Noah's body, this iteration of him that existed eons in the past, stood at the center of this transformation, breathing out visible clouds of concentrated authority that dissipated into the surrounding atmosphere.
Two days.
He had been in the Earliest Folds for over two days now, which
translated to mere hours in his current era. This was the longest Temporal Traversal he had managed before being forced to leave by circumstance or discovery.
The possibilities were intoxicating.
The dangers were even more so!
His other counterpart, Ozymandias, was currently rampaging through
the endless forests of the First Folds, experiencing The Way of

Hunger with enthusiasm that bordered on gluttony. That body was devouring everything it could find...beasts, plants, even the conceptual essence of places themselves, growing stronger with each consumption.

If any of his bodies was going to be forced to leave the Earliest Folds early, it would be Ozymandias. The trail of devoured existence he was leaving behind was subtle but noticeable to anyone looking carefully
enough.
But here, in this glacial region transformed by his declaration of Mana's supremacy, Noah had time to think. Time to plan. Time to consider possibilities that existed when one had access to the past

itself. The most obvious application was spreading the Sparks of his Way of Mana throughout the Earliest Folds. He had them flowing freely across the Transcendent Folds of his current era, subtle seeds of his Way that let him grow his Civilization's influence without direct
intervention.
But doing that here, in the time before THE Loom, before the structures of power had fully crystallized...
"They would find me immediately, Noah thought, his analytical mind running through scenarios.
THE Living Paradox. THE Living Emotive.
From THE Dead Order, he had already seen how quickly such beings
could track him the moment he entered the other side of The Veil.
If he came under the direct scrutiny of any of THE Living Existences
in their prime, when they walked freely through the Earliest Folds without constraint...
All his plans would end before they truly began.
But the possibility of growing his Civilization from this point in time,
of nurturing something that could span eons, that could exist as a
force from the past to the present...
It was too tempting to dismiss entirely!

chapters.title: Chapter 4367 A Seed Civilization! I
paragraphs: RUIN/EDEN's illusory form appeared beside him, her voice carrying into his consciousness alongside detailed prompts:
EARLIEST FOLDS CIVILIZATION SEEDING

"Master, if marks of your Civilization begin to arise in the Earliest Folds, THE Living Existences and THE Creature and THE Weavers, all of whom already have established Civilizations, will sense it immediately," she explained, her tone clinical.
"The disruption would be obvious. The emergence of a new Way of Existence in an era when such things are being carefully monitored would draw attention you cannot afford."
Noah nodded slowly.
RUIN/EDEN continued, prompts flowing alongside her words
POTENTIAL SOLUTION - HIGH RISK:|

"You shouldn't do it at all," she stated flatly. "But if you must, the only potentially viable solution is to find a small, isolated group of existences. They cannot be Living Existences or Early Creatures, those are already connected to THE Living Existences through fundamental bonds that would expose any deviation in their cultivation."
RECOMMENDED TARGET: Fold Dwellers

"Fold Dwellers exist below the notice of the higher powers unless they do something noteworthy," RUIN/EDEN explained. "They are numerous enough that a small group disappearing wouldn't raise alarms. They are weak enough that their growth wouldn't register on the existential scales THE Living Existences monitor."
CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS:
"You would need to nurture this Civilization in absolute secret," she continued.
"Strict instructions must be given to those in this small group to isolate themselves completely. They cannot interact with others outside their group. Ever. Not once. Not for any reason."
"The moment they interact with outside forces, the moment their Way and power become exposed, they will all be killed," RUIN/EDEN stated with certainty.
"And the threads of their existence will lead back to you. THE Living Existences will trace the source. They will find you. And you will follow them into nonexistence."
The prompts were stark, allowing no room for misunderstanding: ISOLATION PROTOCOL REQUIREMENTS:|
- Zero external contact
- Hidden location unknown to all but Master
- Absolute obedience to cultivation restrictions
- No expansion beyond initial group size
- No demonstrations of power outside sealed territory
- Complete suppression of existential signatures
- Emergency dissolution protocols if discovery becomes imminent
Noah absorbed this information, his mind already working through the possibilities, the implications, the terrible potential and equally terrible risks.
"But if it works..." he murmured.
RUIN/EDEN's voice softened slightly, acknowledging the possibility even as she outlined its difficulty.

"If it works, Master, the applications are profound. A small group of Fold Dwellers, given access to your Way of the Mana Architect, isolated from external influence, allowed to cultivate in secret for
eons..."

"They would have time," RUIN/EDEN emphasized. "Eons of cultivation. Generations upon generations advancing along your Way without interference. If they procreate amongst themselves, if they maintain discipline, if they somehow avoid discovery..."

"Master could potentially foster a force of beings reaching Quintillions of Complexity and Purity," she stated. "Possibly higher, depending on how long they remain hidden and how effective they are. A secret army cultivating from the Earliest Folds to your current era, growing stronger with each passing age while the rest of existence remains ignorant of their presence."
Noah's eyes gleamed with tyrannical calculation.
"And they would only emerge at my signal...when I wish for it in the current era...." he said.

"Exactly," RUIN/EDEN confirmed. "You impose an absolute command: they remain in isolation until the Leader of their Civilization sends a specific signal. Something only you can generate from the current era."
Noah stood in his sea of Mana, surrounded by the cold beauty of the glacial region, and made a decision.
"Let's go find ourselves a group of Fold Dwellers," he said with glorious certainty!
Unknown location, First Folds...an insignificant tribe.
The tribal village was burning.

Not with actual fire...that would have been too merciful, too quick, too clean an end. Instead, it burned with the destruction that came from overwhelming existential authority applied by beings who viewed lesser creatures as entertainment rather than equals.
Dozens of Fold Dwellers knelt in the central square of their settlement, forced into positions of submission by pressure that made
standing impossible.
Their homes...structures woven from hardy wood and grown stone that had sheltered families for generations, lay in ruins around them.
At the center of this scene of cruelty stood an Early Creature, his massive form radiating power.
Ten Quadrillion Complexity and Purity, concentrated into a being who had decided that might made right and weakness made victims!
Before him, still defiant despite being forced to his knees, was the
Tribe Leader.
He was younger than one might expect for such a position...barely into what Fold Dwellers considered middle age.
His face was lean, intelligent, marked by the kind of weathering that came from hard decisions rather than simple aging.
His eyes burned with refusal despite the hopeless situation, suggesting either tremendous courage or tremendous stupidity.
His name was Kael, and he was about to die defending principles that
the Early Creature found amusing.
"Why all this mayhem and fear?" the Early Creature asked, his voice carrying false reasonableness that made the question somehow
worse.
"I just wish to lay with all the women in this tribe, and the rest of you
will survive."
He paused, letting the implications sink in while his power pressed
down harder, forcing several Fold Dwellers to press their bodies
against the ground.
"Is your dignity worth your lives?" he continued, "Come on, put your
dignity and pride down. Fold Dwellers like you never held high levels of such things anyway. You're insects pretending to be people. At least
insects know their place."

The faces of the female Fold Dwellers turned ashen. Some wept openly. Others stared at nothing, their minds already trying to distance themselves from what was about to happen. Kael spoke, his voice ragged but unbroken.
"Do all Early Creatures act like this?" he demanded, knowing the

answer but asking anyway. "What will THE Creature think about you if he knew of your actions? You talk of dignity, but is this the dignity of the Early Creatures? Is this what strength means to you?" The Early Creature's expression darkened instantly. The amusement vanished, replaced by genuine anger that suggested Kael had touched on something sensitive, some insecurity that even beings of tremendous power couldn't fully suppress.
"Sometimes," the Early Creature said coldly, "weak insects don't listen until one squashes one as an example."
He raised his massive leg, preparing to bring it down on Kael with
force that would do more than kill...it would erase, would unmake,
would serve as demonstration to all present that questioning one's betters led to nonexistence. The Fold Dwellers cried out.
Some in despair, some in rage. A few tried to rise, to fight, to do
something despite knowing it was futile.
The leg began to descend.
And then...
HUUM!
Reality froze.
A flash of blue brilliance descended from above like judgment made
manifest!

chapters.title: Chapter 4368 A Seed Civilization! II
paragraphs: In an instant, everything stopped, the Early Creature's leg mid-stomp, the tears on the Fold Dwellers' faces, even the air itself seemed to crystallize into stillness.

Noah appeared above the village, surrounded by waves of Mana. His eyes swept across the scene, taking in everything...the destroyed homes, the kneeling people, the Early Creature caught in mid-cruelty like an insect preserved in amber.
"This will do," he said simply, his voice carrying across the frozen moment.
His gaze turned to the Early Creature, this being of Ten Quadrillion Complexity and Purity who had thought his power made him untouchable.
Noah didn't attack. Didn't unleash some devastating technique. Didn't even really move beyond a casual gesture.
He simply exerted his Mana Haki...that aura of dominance born from Infinite Mana refined through impossible cultivation, and reality acknowledged which of them actually held authority here.
SQUELCH!
The Early Creature crumpled.
Not wounded. Not defeated. Not even killed in any conventional
sense.
He simply collapsed, his entire existence folding in on itself like paper being compressed by forces beyond its structural integrity.
Ten Quadrillion Complexity and Purity, reduced to nothing by a casual flex of will from someone who understood that numbers only mattered if reality agreed they mattered.
Noah floated down grandly, Mana swirling around him. The ice holding the Fold Dwellers melted as he approached, though they

remained kneeling...now from shock and awe rather than compulsion. He looked at them all, these people who had been moments from either death or fates worse than death, and his eyes found Kael...the defiant tribe leader whose pride had nearly gotten him killed.
When Noah spoke, his voice was light, almost conversational, but it carried across the village with clarity that suggested every syllable had been crafted specifically for this moment.

"Do you all wish to have true power?" he asked, the question hanging in the air like possibility given form. "Power that will make it so not even Early Creatures question your dignity or force you to kneel?"
His words descended on an oppressed people, on Fold Dwellers who had been told their entire lives that they were lesser, weaker, meant to serve or suffer at the whims of their betters.
Slowly, one by one, they rose from their kneeling positions.
They looked at him...this stranger surrounded by blue brilliance who had appeared from nowhere and unmade their tormentor with ease.
And in their eyes, Noah saw exactly what he needed to see. Not just gratitude.
Not just desperation.
But hunger.
The hunger for strength. For dignity. For the power to never kneel
again.
Perfect.
The silence that followed Noah's question hung in the air!

The Fold Dwellers looked at each other, then at the collapsed form of the Early Creature who had been tormenting them moments ago, then back at Noah...this stranger wreathed in blue brilliance who had appeared from nowhere and offered them impossible things.
Kael was the first to move.
He rose fully from his kneeling position, his legs still shaking slightly from the lingering effects of the pressure that had forced him down, but his eyes were clear. Sharp.
He approached Noah with careful steps, stopping at a respectful distance before bowing deeply- not the forced submission of moments ago, but genuine gratitude mixed with caution.
"Thank you," Kael said, his voice steady despite everything. "For saving
us. For stopping him. For... for seeing us as worth saving at all."
He straightened, and his expression shifted from gratitude to something harder...more analytical.
"But in all my life, I have learned one fundamental truth that transcends all others." His gaze met Noah's directly, unflinching. "Nothing is free. Not truly. Not ever."
The other Fold Dwellers watched their leader speak.
Kael continued, his voice gaining strength.
"We were just saved. Rescued from fates worse than death. And we are immensely, profoundly grateful for it." He paused, letting that gratitude register as genuine before adding the crucial caveat.
"But it was not free. Our salvation came with a cost...perhaps one we don't yet understand, but a cost nonetheless."
His hand gestured toward Noah, encompassing the power radiating
from him.

"And now, your words. This power you speak of. This strength that would allow us to stand against Early Creatures, to never kneel again, to claim dignity that's been denied us our entire existence..."
Kael's voice dropped, becoming more intense.
"It should also not be free. Because nothing of value ever is. And because it is not free, because there must be a cost, because someone
must pay..."
He stepped forward, placing his hand over his heart.
"If it is okay, let me be the one to bear all its cost for my people!"
The declaration rippled through the assembled Fold Dwellers. Several cried out in protest, but Kael raised his other hand to silence them
without looking away from Noah.
"I will bear the cost," he stated with finality.
"Whatever it is. Whatever you require. Payment in service, in loyalty,
in blood if necessary. Let it fall on me alone."
His voice carried a kind of desperate nobility!
"Give them the boons. Make them strong. Let them never kneel again. And I... I will pay whatever price that power demands."
The selflessness was so pure, so genuine!
Noah looked at Kael with eyes that had seen countless beings make
countless bargains, and a smile crossed his face.
"The only cost," Noah said, "is isolation of you and your people. And a pledge of fealty to me. That is all."
He let that sink in before continuing:
"I will not force you to do anything you do not want to do. I will not
command you to fight battles or sacrifice yourselves for causes you don't believe in. I will give this power freely."
His smile deepened slightly:
"But sometime in the future...eons later, I may call upon you. And
when I do, I will expect you to answer!"
The simplicity of the terms seemed to surprise Kael more than any elaborate contract would have. He turned to look at his people, at the faces marked by hope and defiance and desperate hunger for
something better.
The women who had been moments from violation. The men who had
been forced to kneel. The children who had watched their parents reduced to begging. The elderly who had lived too long under the cruelty of beings who viewed them as insects.
They all looked back at him with trust! Kael smiled sadly.
"The First Folds never gave us a warm welcome anyway," he said, his

voice mixing bitterness with liberation. "We can isolate ourselves from it. From all of it. If it means standing tall, if it means never kneeling again, if it means our children grow up knowing dignity..."
He turned back to Noah, and his voice rang with certainty. "We accept. Isolation. Fealty. Whatever future call you make. We
accept all of it."
Noah nodded, satisfaction gleaming in his eyes. His hands rose, and suddenly Mana surged from him like waves crashing against shores that had never known oceans.
The blue brilliance wrapped around the entire village...not just the
people but the structures, the ground they stood on, the very space they occupied.
Reality seemed to acknowledge that this section of the First Folds was being claimed, carved out, removed from the normal flow of
existence.
The Fold Dwellers gasped as they felt the sensation of being lifted, of
being isolated, of becoming separate from the larger fabric of reality around them.
Noah's right hand swept through the air with casual authority, and space itself tore.
It tore like fabric being ripped by forces that refused to accept its

integrity. The tear widened into a massive rift, and through it, the Fold Dwellers could see something that made their minds struggle to process...regions of Collapse, spaces where existence had failed, gaps between the structured reality they knew.
"The Wandering Territories," Noah said, as if that explained
everything.
TEMPORAL AND SPATIAL DISPLACEMENT INITIATED
Action: Removing isolated settlement from First Folds
Destination: Wandering Territories - Stable Collapse Regions Reasoning: Historical consistency suggests Wandering Territories remain unchanged through major timeline events]

chapters.title: Chapter 4369 A Seed Civilization! III
paragraphs: RUIN/EDEN's voice appeared in Noah's consciousness.

"Master, the Wandering Territories are the only regions we know remained relatively stable when the First Folds eventually split into all the Transcendent Folds and Minor Folds. They exist in the gaps, the spaces between structured existence."

"The First Farmer hid there for eons," RUIN/EDEN continued, her analysis flowing naturally. "He was eventually found and tracked down by THE Living Emotive, but his sanctuary itself was not hidden, and he brought in Living Existences which included Living Emotive- he was asking to be found."

"If we place this tribe deep enough in the Wandering Territories, establish proper isolation protocols, and ensure they follow instructions precisely... the probability of discovery drops to manageable levels. Not zero...never zero when dealing with THE Living Existences, but low enough to justify the risk."
Noah steered the bubble of blue Mana containing the village through the tear in space, guiding it into regions that existed between existence.
The Fold Dwellers watched in awe as structured reality gave way to something more fluid, more chaotic, more free.
Inside the protective bubble, Noah floated down to where Kael and the others had gathered. His hands moved with precise gestures, and suddenly dozens of Sparks materialized in the air before him.
Each Spark was a condensed node of pure blue Mana, pulsing with potential that made the air around them hum with recognition of power waiting to be claimed.
They matched exactly the number of Fold Dwellers present. His voice rang out grandly.
"Take the Sparks, and follow my Way. Be part of my... Civilization."

Kael stepped forward first- of course he did, the leader taking the first risk as leaders should. His hand reached out, trembling slightly from anticipation, and touched the Spark floating before him.
The moment contact was made, the Spark ignited.

Blue Mana surged through Kael's existence like rivers discovering they were meant to be oceans. His body lit up from within, transforming at a fundamental level as The Way of Mana integrated into his very being!
HUUM!

His eyes widened in shock and wonder as he felt something crystallizing within his existence...a Mana Locus, budding and growing, establishing itself as the foundation of power he had never imagined possible.

The other Fold Dwellers watched their leader transform, saw the power flowing through him, saw him stand taller and straighter as strength replaced the weakness that had defined their entire existence.
One by one, they stepped forward. One by one, they took their Sparks. One by one, they were remade!
CIVILIZATION SEEDING: INITIATED
Status: Unknown variables detected]
Assessment: Hidden in gaps between spaces of The Earliest Folds, an
isolated Civilization has begun formation
Participants: 47 Fold Dwellers (23 male, 19 female, 5 children)
Initial Complexity Average: 847,000 (Scrubs)|
Projected Growth Rate: Calculating...
WARNING: Results highly unpredictable
Note: Eons of isolated cultivation along Master's Way could produce... interesting outcomes
Note: Generational advancement patterns unclear
Note: Mutation possibilities due to Mana saturation over extended timeline cannot be calculated]
RUIN/EDEN's voice carried a mix of fascination and concern.
"Master, we're in completely uncharted territory here. Fostering a Civilization in the past to emerge in the present violates a great deal of things..."
Noah smiled as he watched the transformations, his gaze sweeping over each Fold Dweller as they were initiated into his Way.
When all had taken their Sparks, when all were standing with Mana flowing through them like lifeblood they'd been missing their entire lives, he spoke again.
"Your safety and mine is now in your hands."
He let that sink in.
"If you wish to survive and prosper, isolation is critical until I call upon you. Nobody will find you. Nobody will even know to look for you. You will live here in peace while following The Way."
His expression grew more serious.

"A tumultuous and chaotic time is coming in the First Folds. Wars between powers you cannot imagine. Conflicts that will reshape existence itself. You will be isolated from all of it. And you need to continue to be so."
The finality in his voice made it clear this wasn't suggestion but fundamental requirement.
"No contact with the outside. No exploration beyond your territory. No demonstrations of power where others might see. You exist in secret. You cultivate in silence. You prosper in isolation."
He paused, then added with emphasis that carried genuine warning.

"The moment you break isolation, the moment you interact with forces beyond your territory, the moment you reveal what you've become... that is the moment you all die. And I die with you, traced back through the connections between us."
Well...he had to scare them and himself a little. THE Living Existences were that terrifying after all!

Kael listened, his newly awakened Mana Locus pulsing within him as he processed these instructions. The other Fold Dwellers did the same, their faces showing understanding mixed with determination. Finally, Kael spoke, his voice pulsing with resonance now that Mana flowed through him.
"Sir... just who are you?"
It was the question they all wanted to ask. This being who had
appeared from nowhere, saved them from death or worse, offered them impossible power, and was now seeding them as a secret Civilization in the gaps between existence.
Who was he? What was he? Why was he doing this?
Noah's smile widened, and when he spoke, his words carried across
the bubble of Mana with the force of declaration.
"I will be your Ancestor. The Architect of Mana, Osmont."
BOOM!
The name resonated through existence itself!

Wandering Territories, his mind already working through everything that needed to be established, all the protocols that required implementation, every safeguard that could mean the difference between survival and discovery.

aster, I need to outlin some constraints. Chamber Blood cannot be forged here in The Earliest Folds. "However, you could infuse them directly with your blood and
concentrated Mana. Not enough to trigger immediate transformation, that would and may still create detectable signatures, but enough to alter their fundamental composition over time."

Way." "You also cannot leave permanent Mana structures that pulse with your signature," RUIN/EDEN added. "No towers, no grand constructions, nothing that broadcasts your presence across time. Everything must be subtle, integrated, hidden within the natural flow
of the Wandering Territories."

time to establish basic protocols and seed initial cultivation methods." Noah absorbed all these limitations with characteristic calm, his smile never wavering. If anything, the constraints made the challenge more
appealing.

He would give them everything they needed to survive. Everything

they needed to cultivate. Everything they needed to remain hidden while growing strong enough that when he finally called them forth... The smile on his face suggested he was very much looking forward to that moment!

chapters.title: Chapter 4370 Collaboration and Civilizations I
paragraphs: In existence, no thread stands alone.

The strongest fiber, woven in isolation, remains merely strong. But threads bound together, supporting and elevating each other, become something transcendent...fabric that can bear weights no individual strand could dream of holding!
Collaboration.
The simple act of many working as one, of powers combined rather than competing, of goals aligned instead of opposed.

It is, perhaps, the most powerful force in existence. More potent than any individual strength. More enduring than any solitary achievement. More capable of reshaping existence than any lone tyrant could ever manage.
But collaboration requires trust. And trust, in a reality where everyone seeks advantage, where betrayal can mean power and loyalty can mean limitation... trust is the rarest resource of all.
Yet when found, when nurtured, when wielded with intelligence and purpose...
Collaboration becomes the foundation of Civilization itself!
The Earliest Folds, an unknown location.
An obsidian Nest of Inevitabilities stretched across impossibilities, its structure pulsing with hunger.
Within this Nest, surrounded by Inevitabilities that pulsed with potential, THE Living Paradox had taken form.
Not his true form...that would be too revelatory, too honest, too vulnerable. Instead, he wore the shape of an Inevitability itself, a construct of contradictions made manifest, tentacles shining
brilliantly!
Into this impossible space, THE Weavers arrived.
One moment they weren't there, the next they had always been there, as if causality itself had been retroactively adjusted to accommodate their existence.

There were three of them, though calling them "three" was misleading. They were individuals and collective simultaneously, separate beings who shared consciousness, distinct entities who spoke as one.
When they spoke, their voices harmonized.
"Someone seems to have interfered with Anaximander."
The statement buzzed in the air.
THE Living Paradox turned his Inevitability-form toward THE Weavers, his expression showing mild curiosity mixed with amusement.
"Interfered how?" he asked.
THE Weavers' unified voice continued:
"Making it harder for us to gain his trust. Sowing seeds of doubt about our intentions. Suggesting that perhaps our guidance isn't entirely selfless."
They paused, and when they spoke again, frustration colored their harmonized tone.

"And because it is Anaximander, all weavings around him are cut off. We cannot track down the culprit. His existence refuses to be threaded into any pattern we create. We see threads approach him and simply... end. Cease. Stop being threads and become nothing." Their forms flickered.
"Should we worry about this? Could it be THE Creature beginning to catch on to our plans?"
THE Living Paradox smiled.

"No," he said with certainty that suggested absolute knowledge. "THE Creature only just confirmed I had never been chained. He knows nothing of Anaximander. Our containment of THE Creature remains absolute. He sees only what we allow him to see."
His smile widened.
"As for whether we should worry..."
He made a gesture that might have been a shrug if shrugging existed in the form he currently wore.
"Nah. If they were going to be anything major, they would do more than try to sow mistrust. They would act directly, intervene obviously,
make themselves known."
His tone became almost dismissive.
"It could just be an insect that came across Anaximander and said some profound things. Sometimes, even insects can be grand. Sometimes a random encounter sparks thoughts that change
trajectories."
He waved one approximation of a hand.
"Monitor it, certainly. But don't waste energy worrying about every minor deviation in the pattern. The grand weaving remains on course. The Way remains on course. Civilization...remains on course."
HUUUM!
THE Weavers stood silently for a moment, processing this
assessment. Their unified consciousness considered angles and implications with speed that would have made lesser minds fragment.
Finally, they spoke again.
"How goes the progress with THE Living Emotive?"
THE Living Paradox's expression shifted to something more satisfied.
"They are already by my side. Cooperation proceeds beautifully. THE Living Emotive has agreed to help forge our Sanctuary. Our higher levels of controlled Civilization."
"Soon, we will begin the real work."
He leaned forward slightly, and when he spoke again, his words
carried heavy weight!
"Having multiple of us working on all this... this is what is grand. This
collaboration is Civilization."
His smile became triumphant!

"THE Creature is alone. We have isolated him beautifully. He stands singular, powerful but solitary, maintaining his principles while we... He gestured broadly, encompassing not just THE Weavers but the grand plan they were all part of.
"We embark on the path of a glorious Civilization! Multiple powers working together, combining strengths, covering each other's weaknesses. THE Living Emotive, You three, Others joining as their
self-interest aligns with ours...."
His voice carried conviction!
"This is how existence should work. Not solitary tyrants holding onto
power through individual strength, but intelligent beings recognizing
that collaboration elevates everyone involved."
THE Weavers nodded in unison, their forms stabilizing as agreement settled over them.
"Collaboration," they echoed, their unified voice carrying approval.
THE Living Paradox knew with absolute certainty that came from eons of observation and planning, that collaboration was critical in the emergence of a glorious Civilization.
Individual power was impressive but limited.
Combined power, intelligently coordinated, became something that
could reshape existence itself.
THE Creature might be stronger individually. Might possess capabilities none of them could match alone. Might be the most
powerful single being in the Earliest Folds.
But he was alone.
And they were many, working together, weaving plans within plans,
supporting each other's ambitions while advancing their collective
goal.
In the end, THE Living Paradox was confident that collaboration
would prove superior to isolation.
The strongest thread eventually breaks.
But woven fabric endures.
And they...were weaving something magnificent!
Kael stood at the edge of their isolated domain, his hand raised before
him as he watched blue Mana swirl around his fingers like living water that had learned to dance.
The sensation was intoxicating!
No, intoxicating was too simple a word. This was transcendent. This
was the feeling of limitation being torn away, of potential that had been locked behind doors he didn't even know existed suddenly flooding through every particle of his being.
His Mana Locus pulsed within his chest like a second heart, rhythmic
and powerful, each beat sending waves of energy through pathways that had only just formed.
He could feel it growing, adapting, learning how to channel more with
each passing hour.
The Way of the Mana Architect!
That's what The Ancestor had called it. A method of existence that
didn't just cultivate power but constructed it, built it deliberately like crafting something with purpose and design rather than simply accumulating strength through time and effort.
Kael concentrated, and the Mana around his hand began to take
shape.
A Weave began to form as blue mana wrapped around him!
