chapters.title: Chapter 4371 Collaboration and Civilizations II
paragraphs: A simple and crude weave of Mana, but it was his!
He released the incomplete Weave and simply stood there, marveling at what had changed in a single day.
His power had risen tenfold compared to his old self. Ten times stronger, ten times more capable, ten times more alive than he had been before The Ancestor appeared.
One day.
In one impossible, glorious day, everything had changed!
"Kael."
The voice cut through his contemplation with a gentle authority. The Ancestor's tone carried across the domain despite the distance, as if space itself had agreed to deliver the message personally.
Kael turned immediately, his heart quickening from the reverence that came from meeting someone who had saved you and then given you tools to save yourself.
He found The Ancestor standing near the center of their settlement, surrounded by the soft glow of Mana that seemed to follow him like atmosphere acknowledging its master.
"Ancestor," Kael said, bowing respectfully before approaching.
Noah, though Kael still thought of him primarily as The Ancestor, looked at him.
"All things here will be left for you to lead," Noah said simply, the statement landing like a crown being placed on shoulders that weren't sure they could bear its weight.
Kael's eyes widened. "Ancestor, I-"
Noah raised a hand gently, cutting off the protest before it could fully
form.

"You need to be careful," he continued, his tone becoming more serious. "Institute strict values for any newborns. For all generations that come after you. Not merely rules, but understanding. Not just commands, but wisdom that persists even after the reasons for it might become unclear."
He stepped closer, and Kael felt the weight of those words settling over him.

"Instill in them the teachings of Mana I will instill in you. Show them the Way. Make them understand that this power isn't just strength-it's responsibility, it's purpose, it's the foundation of everything you're building here."
Noah's expression grew even more intense.
"But most critical of all...more important than any technique, any Weave, any advancement...is the reality of remaining isolated."
The emphasis on that final word made Kael's breath pulse.

"Until I call upon you," Noah said with finality. "Until that moment, this domain is your entire existence. The outside world doesn't exist for you. Other beings, other conflicts, other opportunities...none of them matter. Only isolation. Only cultivation. Only preparation for the day when I will need you."
Kael nodded heavily, the responsibility settling over him. "I understand, Ancestor. I will ensure..."
"Come," Noah interrupted, his tone shifting slightly. "Gather everyone. It's time for an infusion of Mana."
Within minutes, the entire settlement had assembled. Forty-seven Fold Dwellers...no, not Fold Dwellers anymore, Kael corrected himself. They were something else now. Something more. Citizens of a
Civilization that didn't exist in any official records, followers of a Way that shouldn't be possible!
They gathered behind Kael, watching The Ancestor with expressions that mixed awe and gratitude
Noah stood before them all, and without preamble, without elaborate ritual or ceremony, he simply... released radiant sparkling blue waves.

Seas of Mana surged from him like tides that had been waiting eons for permission to flow. Blue brilliance washed over the assembled people endlessly, saturating them with energy so pure and concentrated that breathing it felt like drinking starlight.

The Fold Dwellers, the citizens of this hidden Civilization...gasped as they felt their Mana Loci expanding, their pathways widening, their capacities increasing beyond what they'd thought possible even after accepting The Ancestor's initial Sparks!
Kael watched The Ancestor with reverence and couldn't help but voice the question everyone was thinking.
"Ancestor... just how much Mana do you hold?"
The question seemed almost heretical in its directness, but it had to
be asked!

The sheer volume of energy pouring from The Ancestor suggested reserves that defied all understanding of cultivation and capacity. Noah smiled but didn't answer directly, simply continuing the infusion until every person present was saturated, transformed, elevated beyond their previous limitations.
In the days that followed, they stopped asking that question.
Eventually, they became numb to it entirely.
The reserves of Mana from The Ancestor seemed limitless. Truly, genuinely infinite in ways that made conventional understanding of power seem laughably inadequate.
Hours became days. Days accumulated into a period of transformation that Kael knew would define the rest of his existence.
Everything he had known about Existence and power was being turned upside down, inside out, remade into something that made his previous understanding seem like a child's fairy tale compared to
brutal reality.
The Ancestor gave them power, and he showed them how to use it. How to shape it. How to build with it rather than simply throwing it
around hoping for results!

Mana Glyphs began forming among them. Simple ones at first, crude attempts at capturing intent in structured energy. But gradually, with The Ancestor's patient instruction and their own desperate practice, the Glyphs became more refined.

And at this moment, standing in the training grounds they'd established, Kael heard the voices of children...children who days ago had been powerless, who had watched their parents forced to kneel, who had faced fates they couldn't fight against.
"Primordial Fireball!"
Three young voices called out in unison, and Mana Glyphs activated
around them. Small fireballs, nothing that would threaten anyone remotely powerful, but theirs!
And they manifested through their will rather than begged from existence or stolen from others.
Kael couldn't help but smile at the sight.
"Kael."
The Ancestor's voice again, but different this time. Carrying
something that felt like... finality.
Everyone gathered quickly, sensing the shift in tone, understanding
that something significant was happening.
Noah looked at them all, his voice echoing out.
"My time to leave has come."
The unwillingness that appeared on their faces was heavy.

One of the children...a girl named Lyn who had taken to Mana manipulation with natural talent that suggested she'd be formidable in years to come...ran forward and grabbed The Ancestor's robe with small hands that refused to let go.
"Ancestor, can't you just stay with us?" she asked
"Walk The Way together! We can all cultivate together, grow together,
be a Civilization together!"
The logic was simple, pure, and heartbreaking in its impossibility.
Noah knelt down to her level, his hand gently touching her head.
"We will walk the same path," he said gently. "Just a little differently. I have my journey, and you have yours. The paths run parallel, but they
must remain separate for now."
He stood, addressing them all.
"I will see you all years from now. Many, many years. So many that you
might wonder if I've forgotten you, if the call will ever come, if this
isolation serves any purpose."
His voice became firm.
"But understand this absolutely: only when I call for you can you
come out. Not before. Not if you think you're ready. Not if opportunity presents itself. Not if you face threats you think require outside help. Only when I call. Understood?"
They all nodded, some with tears in their eyes, others with determination burning so bright it made their newly formed Mana Loci pulse in response.
Noah's gaze found Kael, holding him with an intensity that conveyed everything that couldn't be said.
"Take care of this Civilization."
And then...
The Ancestor began to dissipate.
Not dying. Not leaving through normal means of travel. Simply...
scattering into lights of pure Mana that drifted upward and dispersed into the atmosphere of their isolated domain.
Kael and the others watched in silence as their savior, their teacher,
their Ancestor disappeared into particles of blue brilliance that would linger in their territory forever, a constant reminder of what they'd been given and what they were meant to become.
The silence stretched for several heartbeats after the last traces of
The Ancestor faded.
Then Kael turned to face his people, his voice booming out!
"Let us build the grand Civilization of The Ancestor!"
WAA!
The response was fierce. Voices rose in affirmation, fists pumped into
air crackling with Mana, eyes blazed with determination!
They would build.
They would cultivate.
They would remain isolated, hidden, preparing in secret for a call that
might not come for millions of years.
But when it came...
When The Ancestor finally summoned them...
They would be ready!
And thus, a Civilization was seeded in the gaps between existence, in
the Wandering Territories where time flowed differently and discovery was merely unlikely rather than impossible.
It would have time. Millions upon millions of years of time.
Time to grow. Time to evolve. Time to become something worthy of
the impossible foundation they'd been given!
As for what would bloom from it?
Oh!

sentences.text: A simple and crude weave of Mana, but it was his!
He released the incomplete Weave and simply stood there, marveling at what had changed in a single day.
His power had risen tenfold compared to his old self.
Ten times stronger, ten times more capable, ten times more alive than he had been before The Ancestor appeared.
One day.
In one impossible, glorious day, everything had changed!
"Kael."
The voice cut through his contemplation with a gentle authority.
The Ancestor's tone carried across the domain despite the distance, as if space itself had agreed to deliver the message personally.
Kael turned immediately, his heart quickening from the reverence that came from meeting someone who had saved you and then given you tools to save yourself.
He found The Ancestor standing near the center of their settlement, surrounded by the soft glow of Mana that seemed to follow him like atmosphere acknowledging its master.
"Ancestor," Kael said, bowing respectfully before approaching.
Noah, though Kael still thought of him primarily as The Ancestor, looked at him.
"All things here will be left for you to lead," Noah said simply, the statement landing like a crown being placed on shoulders that weren't sure they could bear its weight.
Kael's eyes widened.
"Ancestor, I-"
Noah raised a hand gently, cutting off the protest before it could fully
form.
"You need to be careful," he continued, his tone becoming more serious.
"Institute strict values for any newborns.
For all generations that come after you.
Not merely rules, but understanding.
Not just commands, but wisdom that persists even after the reasons for it might become unclear."
He stepped closer, and Kael felt the weight of those words settling over him.
"Instill in them the teachings of Mana I will instill in you.
Show them the Way.
Make them understand that this power isn't just strength-it's responsibility, it's purpose, it's the foundation of everything you're building here."
Noah's expression grew even more intense.
"But most critical of all...more important than any technique, any Weave, any advancement...is the reality of remaining isolated."
The emphasis on that final word made Kael's breath pulse.
"Until I call upon you," Noah said with finality.
"Until that moment, this domain is your entire existence.
The outside world doesn't exist for you.
Other beings, other conflicts, other opportunities...none of them matter.
Only isolation.
Only cultivation.
Only preparation for the day when I will need you."
Kael nodded heavily, the responsibility settling over him.
"I understand, Ancestor.
I will ensure..."
"Come," Noah interrupted, his tone shifting slightly.
"Gather everyone.
It's time for an infusion of Mana."
Within minutes, the entire settlement had assembled.
Forty-seven Fold Dwellers...no, not Fold Dwellers anymore, Kael corrected himself.
They were something else now.
Something more.
Citizens of a
Civilization that didn't exist in any official records, followers of a Way that shouldn't be possible!
They gathered behind Kael, watching The Ancestor with expressions that mixed awe and gratitude
Noah stood before them all, and without preamble, without elaborate ritual or ceremony, he simply... released radiant sparkling blue waves.
Seas of Mana surged from him like tides that had been waiting eons for permission to flow.
Blue brilliance washed over the assembled people endlessly, saturating them with energy so pure and concentrated that breathing it felt like drinking starlight.

The Fold Dwellers, the citizens of this hidden Civilization...gasped as they felt their Mana Loci expanding, their pathways widening, their capacities increasing beyond what they'd thought possible even after accepting The Ancestor's initial Sparks!
Kael watched The Ancestor with reverence and couldn't help but voice the question everyone was thinking.
"Ancestor... just how much Mana do you hold?"
The question seemed almost heretical in its directness, but it had to
be asked!
The sheer volume of energy pouring from The Ancestor suggested reserves that defied all understanding of cultivation and capacity.
Noah smiled but didn't answer directly, simply continuing the infusion until every person present was saturated, transformed, elevated beyond their previous limitations.
In the days that followed, they stopped asking that question.
Eventually, they became numb to it entirely.
The reserves of Mana from The Ancestor seemed limitless.
Truly, genuinely infinite in ways that made conventional understanding of power seem laughably inadequate.
Hours became days.
Days accumulated into a period of transformation that Kael knew would define the rest of his existence.
Everything he had known about Existence and power was being turned upside down, inside out, remade into something that made his previous understanding seem like a child's fairy tale compared to
brutal reality.
The Ancestor gave them power, and he showed them how to use it.
How to shape it.
How to build with it rather than simply throwing it
around hoping for results!
Mana Glyphs began forming among them.
Simple ones at first, crude attempts at capturing intent in structured energy.
But gradually, with The Ancestor's patient instruction and their own desperate practice, the Glyphs became more refined.

And at this moment, standing in the training grounds they'd established, Kael heard the voices of children...children who days ago had been powerless, who had watched their parents forced to kneel, who had faced fates they couldn't fight against.
"Primordial Fireball!"
Three young voices called out in unison, and Mana Glyphs activated
around them.
Small fireballs, nothing that would threaten anyone remotely powerful, but theirs!
And they manifested through their will rather than begged from existence or stolen from others.
Kael couldn't help but smile at the sight.
"Kael."
The Ancestor's voice again, but different this time.
Carrying
something that felt like... finality.
Everyone gathered quickly, sensing the shift in tone, understanding
that something significant was happening.
Noah looked at them all, his voice echoing out.
"My time to leave has come."
The unwillingness that appeared on their faces was heavy.

One of the children...a girl named Lyn who had taken to Mana manipulation with natural talent that suggested she'd be formidable in years to come...ran forward and grabbed The Ancestor's robe with small hands that refused to let go.
"Ancestor, can't you just stay with us?" she asked
"Walk The Way together!
We can all cultivate together, grow together,
be a Civilization together!"
The logic was simple, pure, and heartbreaking in its impossibility.
Noah knelt down to her level, his hand gently touching her head.
"We will walk the same path," he said gently.
"Just a little differently.
I have my journey, and you have yours.
The paths run parallel, but they
must remain separate for now."
He stood, addressing them all.
"I will see you all years from now.
Many, many years.
So many that you
might wonder if I've forgotten you, if the call will ever come, if this
isolation serves any purpose."
His voice became firm.
"But understand this absolutely: only when I call for you can you
come out.
Not before.
Not if you think you're ready.
Not if opportunity presents itself.
Not if you face threats you think require outside help.
Only when I call.
Understood?"
They all nodded, some with tears in their eyes, others with determination burning so bright it made their newly formed Mana Loci pulse in response.
Noah's gaze found Kael, holding him with an intensity that conveyed everything that couldn't be said.
"Take care of this Civilization."
And then...
The Ancestor began to dissipate.
Not dying.
Not leaving through normal means of travel.
Simply...
scattering into lights of pure Mana that drifted upward and dispersed into the atmosphere of their isolated domain.
Kael and the others watched in silence as their savior, their teacher,
their Ancestor disappeared into particles of blue brilliance that would linger in their territory forever, a constant reminder of what they'd been given and what they were meant to become.
The silence stretched for several heartbeats after the last traces of
The Ancestor faded.
Then Kael turned to face his people, his voice booming out!
"Let us build the grand Civilization of The Ancestor!"
WAA!
The response was fierce.
Voices rose in affirmation, fists pumped into
air crackling with Mana, eyes blazed with determination!
They would build.
They would cultivate.
They would remain isolated, hidden, preparing in secret for a call that
might not come for millions of years.
But when it came...
When The Ancestor finally summoned them...
They would be ready!
And thus, a Civilization was seeded in the gaps between existence, in
the Wandering Territories where time flowed differently and discovery was merely unlikely rather than impossible.
It would have time.
Millions upon millions of years of time.
Time to grow.
Time to evolve.
Time to become something worthy of
the impossible foundation they'd been given!
As for what would bloom from it?
Oh!

chapters.title: Chapter 4372 Collaboration and Civilizations III
paragraphs: Noah's consciousness flickered as Temporal Traversal seized him, pulling him forward through rivers of time that flowed in directions that had no names.
His eyes were closed, but he could see regardless, perceiving the multicolored brilliance of temporal streams.
Reality itself became visible as layers of possibilities and actualities interweaving, paths taken and abandoned existing simultaneously in quantum superposition.

His Resplendent Citadels blazed within his existence like beacons, acting as guides that ensured he returned to the correct temporal coordinate rather than ending up scattered across multiple time periods.
The entire Early Atlas of the Folds pulsed within him, that impossible map that shouldn't exist but did anyway through sheer audacity of will and Mana that refused to acknowledge limitation!
The Early Atlas that made this ridiculous capability possible!
He was crossing eons in moments, traveling from the Earliest Folds back to his current era.
As consciousness began to solidify, as the temporal streams started to deposit him back into normal causality, RUIN/EDEN's prompts appeared.
ITEMPORAL TRAVERSAL: COMPLETE]
Duration in Earliest Folds: Multiple days]
JACCOMPLISHMENT SUMMARY - EARLIEST FOLDS EXPEDITION
PRIMARY ACHIEVEMENTS:
Early Laboratories Infiltration: Successfully traversed the lands designed by THE Living Concept. Obtained complete methodology for
Living Existential Armor construction. Aethelgard infiltration, learning of Everythings.

Anaximander Encounter: Established contact with Fold Dweller possessing ridiculous capabilities. Provided alternative perspective on THE Weavers' guidance. Exchanged information regarding nature of The Way and existence. Parted on terms suggesting potential future cooperation.
Way of Existence Declaration: Successfully declared and embarked on a personal Way in region saturated with raw Early Existential Authority.
Hunger Experience via Ozymandias: Secondary body successfully experienced and integrated Way of Hunger through

consumption-based cultivation. Devoured 847 distinct entities ranging from simple beasts to conceptual manifestations. Gained understanding of consumption as cultivation methodology (applications pending analysis).

|Secret Civilization Seeding: Most ambitious and dangerous achievement. Successfully isolated group of 47 Fold Dwellers from normal timeline. Established hidden settlement in Wandering Territories with strict isolation protocols. Initiated 47 individuals into The Way of the Mana Architect. Left comprehensive instructions for generational cultivation. Projected emergence: Current Era, upon signal from Master.
PERSONAL CULTIVATION GAINS:
Mana Glyphs Forged: 42,555 (Total)|
The number appeared in bold, emphasized because it represented something that shouldn't be possible.
Each Glyph was supposed to become progressively harder to forge after passing certain thresholds. Ten thousand Glyphs was considered a lifetime achievement!
Noah had forty-two thousand.

Analysis: Addition of Mana Glyphs past 10,000 threshold encountered exponentially increasing difficulty. Each subsequent Glyph required 2.7x more effort than previous. By 40,000 mark, individual Glyph formation required concentration and Mana investment equivalent to forging first 1,000 Glyphs combined.
Master's Response: Continued regardless.
Assessment: Tyrannical persistence. Inefficient by normal standards. Perfectly aligned with Master's operational philosophy of 'if it's
difficult, do it more.
Noah smiled as he felt his body solidifying back into normal existence, consciousness settling into flesh that had temporarily been scattered across temporal coordinates.
He looked at himself... at his body currently filled with an overabundance of swirling blue Mana Glyphs that covered his skin like living tattoos, each one pulsing with contained potential.
The sheer density of Glyphs made his entire form shimmer with barely-contained energy!
HUUM!
More prompts appeared.
PRINCIPLE DEVELOPMENT:
Mana Glyphs of the Cheating Architect: 125 (Newly Formed)]
Mana Glyphs of Perpetual Harvest: 125 (Newly Formed)|
Combined Effect: Principle Integration accelerating. The Way of Existence becoming more defined, more powerful, more fundamentally woven into Master's being.
EMPOWERMENT UTILIZATION:|
Daily Harvest Festival Endowments: Utilized 3 times
Empowerment Sources: Self-targeting (maximum efficiency)|
Total Gain: +0.75 Quintillion Complexity
Total Gain: +0.75 Quintillion Purity]
Note: Self-empowerment creates interesting feedback loops.
Essentially using power to generate more power to use for generating
even more power. A bit confusing...
These were his gains.
Noah's smile widened into something tyrannical as he felt the power
coursing through him, the accumulated results of days spent in impossible places doing impossible things with efficiency that would make conventional cultivation weep!
But the smile slowly faded as he focused forward, as his analytical mind began calculating what lay ahead rather than celebrating what
he'd achieved.
Even this was minimal in his eyes!
Not objectively...objectively, these gains were obscene, reality-breaking, the kind of advancement that should take lifetimes
compressed into days.

But subjectively, from the perspective of someone preparing for conflicts against THE Living Existences, against THE Dead Order, against forces that had existed for eons and cultivated their power through time periods that made his entire existence seem like a brief
flicker...
He needed so much more.
He needed to continue violating every reasonable expectation of
advancement.
Needed to keep pushing beyond what should be possible into what absolutely wasn't possible and make it work anyway through sheer audacity and Infinite Mana.
Because anything less meant his Civilization wouldn't survive what
was coming.
TEMPORAL TRAVERSAL COOLDOWN:
Time Until Next Available Traversal: 9 hours, 47 minutes, 23 seconds
Note: Master's Temporal Traversal capability recharges faster with each successful completion. Projected minimum cooldown after sufficient repetitions: 6 hours.
Translation: Soon Master will be able to spend more time in the past
than in the present.
Noah acknowledged the information with a nod, his mind already planning his next Traversal, considering what needed to be accomplished, calculating risks against potential gains.
In a flash of light, his body shuttled across existence, returning from
temporal coordinates to spatial ones, from the abstract realm of time-travel to the concrete reality of his territory.
He appeared on the Early Veiled Shore.
Home.
Or at least, the closest thing he had to home in an existence defined
by constant motion and advancement.
The golden sands welcomed this body back with familiar warmth!
A distance away.
The Cultivation Citadel of The Early Creature, Osmont.
Even though days had passed in the Earliest Folds, time flowing
normally while Noah's consciousness had been scattered across multiple bodies and temporal locations...only a single day had passed
here.
One day in the Cultivation Citadel.
One glorious, brutal, transformative day.
WHOOOOSH!
Noah's body blazed across the blue planet's atmosphere like a meteor

that had learned flight and decided to show off. He circled the entire planetary body multiple times in mere seconds, his form leaving trails of blue Mana in his wake that took minutes to dissipate. The weight pressing down on him was tremendous...Level 10 pressure, one hundred times the weight of his normal existence, enough force to compress most beings into singularities of regret and
poor life choices!
Oh!
He wasn't just withstanding it.
He was flying freely while bearing this weight.
Every few seconds, Primordial Fireballs erupted from his hands, each
one forced to manifest under pressure that tried to prevent their
formation.
They blazed into existence, bore the tremendous weight for

moments, then dissipated as the pressure proved too much for sustained manifestation. Primordial Mana-Flame Wyrms followed...serpentine constructs of pure fire wreathed in Mana, each one struggling to maintain cohesion
under forces that wanted to unmake them but existing long enough to prove it was possible.
Noah stopped his circling abruptly, his body pivoting mid-flight to dive toward a specific region of the planet's surface.
He landed in an area filled with heavy rain.
But calling it "rain" was like calling a tsunami "moisture"...technically
accurate but missing the magnitude entirely.
Each raindrop that fell here was a battering attack of compressed
authority.
The drops were dense enough to be visible as distinct projectiles
rather than continuous water, each one carrying force that exceeded
6 Quintillion damage in both Complexity and Purity.
BOOM!
And they battered him!

chapters.title: Chapter 4373 Collaboration and Civilizations IV
paragraphs: They hammered into Noah's body with relentless rhythm....not trying to harm him so much as constantly testing him, forcing his existence to prove it could withstand assault that would shatter most Early Creatures.

His muscular visage pulsed with waves of blue Mana, Glyphs covering every inch of visible skin and glowing with contained energy. Water streamed over the contours of his frame, following the lines of muscle that had been refined through impossible cultivation.
He stood there, letting the rain batter him, and spoke into the storm with calm authority.
"Give me the overall results of the last day."
CULTIVATION CITADEL - PERFORMANCE SUMMARY (24-HOUR PERIOD):
PRESSURE PROGRESSION:
- Initial Level: 1 (2x baseline existence)
- Current Level: 10 (100x baseline existence)
- Adaptation Status: COMPLETE
Total Adaptation Time: 23 hours, 37 minutes
Time Spent at Level 10 with Full Adaptation: 2 hours, 23 minutes]
HARVEST CALCULATION:
Effort translated to advancement over 24-hour period:]
Total Gain: +5.2 Quintillion Complexity
Total Gain: +5.2 Quintillion Purity
COMBINED ADVANCEMENT (Including Earliest Folds Gains):
Previous Total: 4.35 Quintillion (approximately)|
Earliest Folds Contribution: +0.75 Quintillion
Cultivation Citadel Contribution: +5.2 Quintillion
CURRENT TOTAL: 10.3 Quintillion Complexity
CURRENT TOTAL: 10.3 Quintillion Purity]
Analysis: Master has more than doubled total power in approximately 30 hours of real-time across multiple cultivation environments.
Noah stood in the rain, water hammering his body with force that would annihilate mountains, and nodded calmly at these results.
To him, it was satisfactory.
Not spectacular. Not worthy of particular celebration. Just... satisfactory.
To jump from 4 Quintillion to over 10 Quintillion in a day was acceptable progress by his standards.
He specifically avoided comparing himself to others.
That path led to complacency, to telling himself that Early Creatures took lifetimes to accumulate what he'd gained in hours. Tatiana had barely passed 4 Quintillion after eons.
Forgemaster Vulcan was considered remarkable in Aethelgard.
If he compared himself to them, he might actually limit himself by thinking his gains were utterly unfair and stupendous!
But he knew better.

He had to be even more unfair. Had to continue violating norms again and again until conventional understanding of cultivation gave up trying to categorize him and simply accepted that he existed outside their frameworks.
Right now, there were a great many things to be done. Glorious advancements had occurred in the last day...here in the Cultivation
Citadel, in the Earliest Folds, across the Early Veiled Shore where his other bodies had been working.
And soon...
Soon he would see what grand results the isolated Civilization he'd forged in the Earliest Folds would produce.
Millions of years of secret cultivation, hidden from all of existence,
emerging only at his signal.
The smile that crossed his face as he contemplated that future
moment was tyrannical in its anticipation.
The rain continued to hammer down, each drop carrying enough
force to shatter continents.
Noah stood in it, letting the pressure test him, and began planning his next impossible advancement.
He had a few things to complete before he would see the results of his Isolated Civilization!
Back in the Early Veiled Shore.

Noah stood there, breathing in the familiar weight of his own domain, feeling the way existence settled differently here than it did in the frozen desolation of the Earliest Folds or beneath the crushing gravity of the Cultivation Citadel.

His body here resonated with the echoes of his other selves. The one grinding beneath impossible pressure in the Citadel. The one navigating the currents of the Wandering Territories. All connected, all advancing!
But what drew his attention now was the fundamental change that had occurred here while fragments of his consciousness had been scattered across existence.
HUUM!
Blue-gold light coalesced before him, forming the illusory visage of RUIN/EDEN. Her holographic form manifested with precision.
"Master," she said, "The transformations are complete."
Noah's gaze settled on her, patient and expectant.
"The Chamber of Blood has succeeded beyond projected parameters
as your selected Nine Mana-Born Early Creatures have emerged."
Nine beings who had been immersed in the concentrated reality of
what he was and had evolved!
Noah's expression remained calm.
"Show me," he said quietly.

RUIN/EDEN's form expanded slightly, her gesture drawing his attention past the golden beach toward the vibrant Sacred Waters that stretched beyond. "They are testing their new capabilities now. Understanding what they've become."
Noah followed her indication, his perception reaching outward, and...
BOOOOOM!
The distant waters churned.
The Sacred Waters were erupting, waves of early-formed mana
crashing against themselves with enough force to make the
surrounding space ripple.
The air above the water blazed with released power, scorching
white-gold flames that left afterimages burned into the fabric of
existence itself.
And floating above it all, suspended in the sky like a judge presiding over lesser courts, was Sigrid.
THE Living Order herself, transformed beyond what she had been. She looked like something forged in the heart of absolute authority
and quenched in infinite law.
Her white-blue empress robe flowed around her form.
concepts of
The fabric itself seemed woven from comp hierarchy and command, shimmering with an inner light that made the surrounding air bow in deference.
Behind her back, radiant blue wings spread wide.
Her white eyes blazed with power that made the atmosphere tremble.

She floated there with an expression that could only be described as magnificently arrogant...not the petty arrogance of the insecure, but the absolute certainty of someone who had touched transcendence and found it suited her perfectly!
Noah looked at all of this and nodded.
"The transformation data," he said, his voice carrying quiet command. RUINEDEN responded immediately, prompts materializing in his vision with clinical precision.
TRANSFORMATION ANALYSIS - PRIMARY SUBJECT
DESIGNATION: Sigrid]
CLASSIFICATION: THE Living Order |
NEW CLASSIFICATION: Prime Mana-Born Early Creature EVOLUTION TIER: The Glorious Evolution]
CURRENT COMPLEXITY: 4.47 Quintillion
CURRENT PURITY: 4.47 Quintillion
"The Glorious Evolution," RUINEDEN continued,"represents the highest tier of transformation achievable through the Chamber of
Blood protocols."
She gestured, and additional data cascaded through Noah's

sentences.text: They hammered into Noah's body with relentless rhythm....not trying to harm him so much as constantly testing him, forcing his existence to prove it could withstand assault that would shatter most Early Creatures.
His muscular visage pulsed with waves of blue Mana, Glyphs covering every inch of visible skin and glowing with contained energy.
Water streamed over the contours of his frame, following the lines of muscle that had been refined through impossible cultivation.
He stood there, letting the rain batter him, and spoke into the storm with calm authority.
"Give me the overall results of the last day."
CULTIVATION CITADEL - PERFORMANCE SUMMARY (24-HOUR PERIOD):
PRESSURE PROGRESSION:
- Initial Level: 1 (2x baseline existence)
- Current Level: 10 (100x baseline existence)
- Adaptation Status: COMPLETE
Total Adaptation Time: 23 hours, 37 minutes
Time Spent at Level 10 with Full Adaptation: 2 hours, 23 minutes]
HARVEST CALCULATION:
Effort translated to advancement over 24-hour period:]
Total Gain: +5.2 Quintillion Complexity
Total Gain: +5.2 Quintillion Purity
COMBINED ADVANCEMENT (Including Earliest Folds Gains):
Previous Total: 4.35 Quintillion (approximately)|
Earliest Folds Contribution: +0.75 Quintillion
Cultivation Citadel Contribution: +5.2 Quintillion
CURRENT TOTAL: 10.3 Quintillion Complexity
CURRENT TOTAL: 10.3 Quintillion Purity]
Analysis: Master has more than doubled total power in approximately 30 hours of real-time across multiple cultivation environments.
Noah stood in the rain, water hammering his body with force that would annihilate mountains, and nodded calmly at these results.
To him, it was satisfactory.
Not spectacular.
Not worthy of particular celebration.
Just... satisfactory.
To jump from 4 Quintillion to over 10 Quintillion in a day was acceptable progress by his standards.
He specifically avoided comparing himself to others.
That path led to complacency, to telling himself that Early Creatures took lifetimes to accumulate what he'd gained in hours.
Tatiana had barely passed 4 Quintillion after eons.
Forgemaster Vulcan was considered remarkable in Aethelgard.
If he compared himself to them, he might actually limit himself by thinking his gains were utterly unfair and stupendous!
But he knew better.
He had to be even more unfair.
Had to continue violating norms again and again until conventional understanding of cultivation gave up trying to categorize him and simply accepted that he existed outside their frameworks.
Right now, there were a great many things to be done.
Glorious advancements had occurred in the last day...here in the Cultivation
Citadel, in the Earliest Folds, across the Early Veiled Shore where his other bodies had been working.
And soon...
Soon he would see what grand results the isolated Civilization he'd forged in the Earliest Folds would produce.
Millions of years of secret cultivation, hidden from all of existence,
emerging only at his signal.
The smile that crossed his face as he contemplated that future
moment was tyrannical in its anticipation.
The rain continued to hammer down, each drop carrying enough
force to shatter continents.
Noah stood in it, letting the pressure test him, and began planning his next impossible advancement.
He had a few things to complete before he would see the results of his Isolated Civilization!
Back in the Early Veiled Shore.

Noah stood there, breathing in the familiar weight of his own domain, feeling the way existence settled differently here than it did in the frozen desolation of the Earliest Folds or beneath the crushing gravity of the Cultivation Citadel.
His body here resonated with the echoes of his other selves.
The one grinding beneath impossible pressure in the Citadel.
The one navigating the currents of the Wandering Territories.
All connected, all advancing!
But what drew his attention now was the fundamental change that had occurred here while fragments of his consciousness had been scattered across existence.
HUUM!
Blue-gold light coalesced before him, forming the illusory visage of RUIN/EDEN.
Her holographic form manifested with precision.
"Master," she said, "The transformations are complete."
Noah's gaze settled on her, patient and expectant.
"The Chamber of Blood has succeeded beyond projected parameters
as your selected Nine Mana-Born Early Creatures have emerged."
Nine beings who had been immersed in the concentrated reality of
what he was and had evolved!
Noah's expression remained calm.
"Show me," he said quietly.
RUIN/EDEN's form expanded slightly, her gesture drawing his attention past the golden beach toward the vibrant Sacred Waters that stretched beyond.
"They are testing their new capabilities now.
Understanding what they've become."
Noah followed her indication, his perception reaching outward, and...
BOOOOOM!
The distant waters churned.
The Sacred Waters were erupting, waves of early-formed mana
crashing against themselves with enough force to make the
surrounding space ripple.
The air above the water blazed with released power, scorching
white-gold flames that left afterimages burned into the fabric of
existence itself.
And floating above it all, suspended in the sky like a judge presiding over lesser courts, was Sigrid.
THE Living Order herself, transformed beyond what she had been.
She looked like something forged in the heart of absolute authority
and quenched in infinite law.
Her white-blue empress robe flowed around her form.
concepts of
The fabric itself seemed woven from comp hierarchy and command, shimmering with an inner light that made the surrounding air bow in deference.
Behind her back, radiant blue wings spread wide.
Her white eyes blazed with power that made the atmosphere tremble.

She floated there with an expression that could only be described as magnificently arrogant...not the petty arrogance of the insecure, but the absolute certainty of someone who had touched transcendence and found it suited her perfectly!
Noah looked at all of this and nodded.
"The transformation data," he said, his voice carrying quiet command.
RUINEDEN responded immediately, prompts materializing in his vision with clinical precision.

paragraphs: Moiraine floated nearby, and around her the concept of Paradox had become tangible.

She launched a Primordial Fireball that somehow existed in multiple contradictory states...burning and frozen, present and absent, devastating and harmless...all simultaneously, until reality chose whichever outcome best suited her needs.
Her Mana Glyph of Paradox blazed behind her like a crown of impossible glory!

The Emperor Penguin descended from above, and despite everything...despite the power he now wielded, despite the Mana Glyph of Pride burning behind him like a second sun...he remained unmistakably a penguin.
His form radiated arrogance so concentrated it had become a physical force, making the air around him feel heavier with judgment.
His attacks came wrapped in disdain, as if Sigrid should feel honored to defend against them!
Who said his attacks could be avoided?!
Who said his attacks were allowed to fail?!
Who said?!
HUUM!
But the Blue Slime....
GLUB GLUB GLUB!
Its form defied simple description.
A shifting, translucent mass of blue-gold liquid that seemed to contain entire liquid Wheels of compressed Mana within its bubbly
structure.
As Noah watched, the Slime merged with a Primordial Fireball.
The burning slime then surged toward Sigrid like a meteor that had somehow achieved sentience and decided to test the limits of imposed Order.
Sigrid's hand came down.
Cold. Precise. Absolute.
White light cascaded from her fingers, pure Order given form! The burning slime stopped.

Frozen mid-surge, flames still flickering, bubbles still glubbing softly, but completely immobile as if Sigrid had reached into its fundamental code and changed every variable related to motion to zero.
"Impressive capabilities across all Second Tier subjects," RUIN/EDEN observed. "But there are four more you should see."
Noah's gaze swept past the aerial combat, down toward the roiling surface of the Sacred Waters, and there...
Floating on waves of blue Mana, four figures that made the
surrounding space ripple with their mere presence.
Henry floated with a body of wonder and pride, Nepotism flowing out of him all around as his power was ecstatic!
Malphas stood on the water's surface calmly.
His body seemed constructed from compressed shadows and crystallized ambition, every line of his form sharp enough to cut concepts.

He wore a butler's suit that looked woven from midnight itself, fabric that absorbed light and gave back only the suggestion of depth. Six wings spread behind him...not demonic, but something other, each feather a condensed fragment of authority that shifted between shadow and substance depending on the angle of observation.
Illusory crows surged from his form constantly!
Arch Lich Ra'zan floated nearby, and his metamorphosis had been perhaps the most dramatic of all.
The skeletal form remained, but the bones themselves now appeared carved from compressed existential authority rather than simple calcium.
Blue-gold energy flowed through him, and his empty eye sockets blazed with flames that were the idea of fire, purified to its essential concept and given burning form.
And the Queen of Matter...
She sat cross-legged on the water's surface in meditation, but the space around her danced with tomes and grimoires. She looked around constantly as she needed to record absolutely everything!
"These four," RUINEDEN said, "also achieved The Glorious Evolution. Prime Mana-Born Early Creatures."
New prompts materialized.
GLORIOUS EVOLUTION - ADDITIONAL SUBJECTS
SUBJECTS: Henry, Malphas, Arch Lich Ra'Zan, The Queen of Matter
COMPLEXITY RANGE: 3.12 - 3.94 Quintillion
PURITY RANGE: 3.12 - 3.94 Quintillion
Noah stood there on the golden sands, his perception drinking in
every detail of the nine beings who had undergone transformation through exposure to his concentrated essence.
His people.
His Civilization!
The smile that touched Noah's lips was small, barely there, but it
carried satisfaction.
They were magnificent.
And they had no idea how much further they could go.
He took a single step forward.
РАН!
.. and existence folded.

The distance between where he stood on the beach and where he chose to be in the sky simply... ceased to matter. Space acknowledged his will and rearranged itself accordingly, placing him exactly where he intended without the inconvenient process of traversing the space
between.
He manifested near Sigrid, floating in the air above the roiling Sacred Waters, and nine pairs of eyes locked onto him instantly.
The combat ceased immediately.
"Master," Malphas rose as he said, and the single word carried depths.
Noah's gaze swept across all nine of them.
"It seems," he said, "you have all attained new power."
Then his smile widened slightly, and something shifted in his tone.
"Let us put it to the test."
The surrounding atmosphere compressed, as if reality itself was
holding its breath.
"Whoever can manage to touch me..." He paused, letting the weight of the challenge settle. "I will ensure Harvest sufficient to at least double
your current power."
HUUM!
The silence that followed was profound.
Double their power.
All of them wanted to utter...say less!
And then-
BOOM!
Reality fractured.
Malphas, Sigrid, and Arch Lich Ra'Zan manifested beside Noah
simultaneously, each one moving at speeds that defied their massive
Complexity.
Their hands extended toward his form, fingers reaching for contact
that would secure impossible rewards...
WAP!
Noah was already elsewhere.
He hovered there, expression carrying mild interest. "Even with your terrifying perception and power exceeding three Quintillion," he observed, his tone conversational, "you moved as if
through thick, heavy water."
He let that settle for a moment.
He could withstand one hundred times his normal existential weight
in the Cultivation Citadel. This...atmosphere felt like moving through a pleasant dream!
His smile carried challenge.
"Come. I've barely used a percentage of my power."
The words were a detonation.
RAAA!
They erupted.
Not just the three who had initially attacked, all of them!
Henry and all others joined in!
It was coordinated. It was overwhelming. It represented the combined assault of nine Mana-Born Early Creatures whose
individual power could threaten entire Folds.
And...
Noah evaded it all without apparent effort.
"BROTHER!"
He drifted between Titano's grasp like smoke passing through
grasping fingers.
All other attacks could not even reach him!
He reappeared in the center of their formation, surrounded on all
sides, completely untouched.
They deployed their Mana Glyphs.
BOOOOM!
The sky erupted with concentrated authority.
Primordial Fireballs the size of buildings. Paradoxes that made
causality weep. Order-based constraints that tried to rewrite the fundamental laws governing Noah's existence...
All of it crashed toward Noah in perfect synchronization, representing
the combined might of nine beings!
Noah raised one hand.

Blue light leaked from his form...not much, just a fragment of what he carried, barely registering as a percentage of his full capability. But it was his Haki, the conceptual weight of his tyrannical authority
given form, and even this shred carried pressure that made existence
acknowledge its presence.
BOOM!
The blue light expanded outward in a wave.
The wave of Haki crashed into all nine Mana-Born Early Creatures
simultaneously.
BOOM!
And...
SPLASH! SPLASH! SPLASH!
They fell.
Sigrid, despite her perfect control and Order-authority, plummeted
from the sky in an arc of white-gold light.
Titano, massive and seemingly immovable, crashed through the air
like a meteor.
Henry and Moiraine, for all their skill and paradoxes, tumbled before impact. The Emperor Penguin's Pride couldn't prevent his descent!
The Blue Slime made distressed glubbing sounds. Malphas's wings crumpled. Ra'Zan's jaws cackled, and The Queen of
Matter was writing snd recording everything with a fervant
expression!
They struck the Early Sacred Waters with impacts that sent geysers
of blue-gold liquid erupting hundreds of feet into the air.
The beach trembled.
The sky rippled.
Noah remained hovering above them all, his form radiating casual,
effortless authority.
"That," he called down, "was barely five percent of my power."
He let the words settle.
"Come on."
His visage pulsed with glorious tyranny, blue-gold light cascading
from his form in waves that made the surrounding atmosphere hum
with potential!

Below, nine Mana-Born Early Creatures began pulling themselves from the Sacred Waters, their expressions carrying determination. They would try again. And again. And again, until either they succeeded or exhausted themselves in the attempt. It was exactly what Noah had wanted to see.
Far away, back in the crushing pressure of the Cultivation Citadel of
The Early Creature, Noah's other body stirred from rest. Every breath required cutting through resistance. Every thought
moved through atmospheric weight that tried to slow even
consciousness itself.
RUIN/EDEN's illusory form bloomed beside him, her holographic features carrying focused intensity.
"Master," she said without preamble. "The Justiciar has made its appearance in the Transcendent Quantum Folds." Noah's eyes opened.
The exhaustion didn't vanish, but his focus sharpened immediately.
This was a moment they'd been preparing form...the experiment that
would reveal critical intelligence about their enemies' operational
structure.
"Timeline," he said simply.
"Moving through populated regions with systematic efficiency.

Estimates suggest the massacre will begin within eight minutes." Prompts materialized before him. JUSTICIAR OBSERVATION-REAL-TIME TRACKING CLASSIFICATION: Enforcement Entity COMPLEXITY: 1.04 Quintillion
CURRENT LOCATION: Transcendent Quantum Folds, Sector 7,
Aeternitas Quantumavine
Noah pulled himself to sitting position.
"Our preparations?" he asked.
"Complete," RUIN/EDEN replied. "All protocols are in place and
operational."
New prompts expanded before him in layers.
OPERATION: SHADOW THEATER| STATUS: Fully Deployed
PRIMARY OBJECTIVE: Intelligence gathering via tracking
SECONDARY OBJECTIVE: Zero casualties among actual population "Every genuine lifeform in the Justiciar's projected path has been relocated," RUIN/EDEN continued.

"In their place," RUIN/EDEN said, "I've deployed sophisticated illusions. These aren't simple visual constructs...they're full-spectrum existential replicas utilizing your Resplendent Citadels of Dreams, Fantasia, and Illusions." ILLUSION SPECIFICATIONS: Complexity Mimicry: Perfect replication of each target's existential
signature
Behavioral Authenticity: Programmed behavior patterns derived from extensive observational data
Sensory Response: React to all stimuli exactly as genuine beings
would
Death Simulation: Display appropriate destruction patterns when terminated Energy Signature: Generate false life-force readings indistinguishable from actual existence]
Detection Resistance: Tested against perception abilities up to 4.5
Quintillion complexity
Justiciar Capability: 1.04 Quintillion - insufficient to distinguish
illusion from reality
"When the Justiciar completes its massacre," RUIN/EDEN continued,
"it will be destroying sophisticated illusions while believing it's
accomplished its mission.
Noah absorbed this, his mind mapping the expected flow of events.
The Justiciar would complete its task, confident in its success. And
then...
"The tracking protocol," he said. "Embedded within each illusion's 'death energy," RUIN/EDEN confirmed. "When the Justiciar terminates an illusion, it will be
painted with invisible Mana lines. Those signatures contain tracking elements the Justiciar cannot detect."
TRACKING PROTOCOL: Tracking Range: Unlimited
Information Gathered: Complete path taken, final destination, any
intermediate stops|
Expected Outcome: Direct line to Justiciar's base of operations "When it returns to wherever these entities are based," RUIN/EDEN concluded, "we'll have complete tracking data. Oh, Schrodinger and
his bodies will also likely be following."
Noah nodded slowly, his muscles protesting the movement under
pressure.
"The preparations are complete then," he said. "All elements are in position," RUIN/EDEN confirmed. "We observe,
we track, we learn. And we do so without sacrificing a single actual
life."
Noah pulled himself fully upright, his body screaming protests against
the crushing weight of the Citadel. But his eyes carried satisfaction
beyond physical strain.

This was strategy operating on the scale existence demanded. Not simple combat or direct confrontation, but layered operations that turned enemy actions into intelligence gathering. "Now," he said, his voice carrying anticipation that made the surrounding air compress slightly, "let us see the results of the
experiment."
He breathed out, centering himself despite the crushing pressure.
"Let us see what glory came from... the Isolated Civilization."
HUUM!
He had given them endless Mana. The Way of Mana. And then he had stepped back, allowing them to develop independently, to find their
own solutions, to forge their own path toward survival.
He wondered what they had become. What they had built when given such a Way of Existence and
resources and desperate need.
What answers they had discovered when forced to advance without
his direct
guidance.
His tyrannical heart pulsed with anticipation, blue-gold light leaking
from his form even under the Citadel's crushing weight.
Time to see what his people could accomplish when necessity and
Infinite Mana collided!
Time to see if isolated desperation could forge solutions even he
hadn't anticipated.
Time to see just what glory would emerge from a Civilization given
everything it needed except certainty!

OPERATION: SHADOW THEATER| STATUS: Fully Deployed
PRIMARY OBJECTIVE: Intelligence gathering via tracking
SECONDARY OBJECTIVE: Zero casualties among actual population "Every genuine lifeform in the Justiciar's projected path has been relocated," RUIN/EDEN continued.
"In their place," RUIN/EDEN said, "I've deployed sophisticated illusions.

These aren't simple visual constructs...they're full-spectrum existential replicas utilizing your Resplendent Citadels of Dreams, Fantasia, and Illusions." ILLUSION SPECIFICATIONS: Complexity Mimicry: Perfect replication of each target's existential
signature
Behavioral Authenticity: Programmed behavior patterns derived from extensive observational data
Sensory Response: React to all stimuli exactly as genuine beings
would
Death Simulation: Display appropriate destruction patterns when terminated Energy Signature: Generate false life-force readings indistinguishable from actual existence]
Detection Resistance: Tested against perception abilities up to 4.5
Quintillion complexity
Justiciar Capability: 1.04 Quintillion - insufficient to distinguish
illusion from reality
"When the Justiciar completes its massacre," RUIN/EDEN continued,
"it will be destroying sophisticated illusions while believing it's
accomplished its mission.
Noah absorbed this, his mind mapping the expected flow of events.
The Justiciar would complete its task, confident in its success.
And
then...
"The tracking protocol," he said.
"Embedded within each illusion's 'death energy," RUIN/EDEN confirmed.
"When the Justiciar terminates an illusion, it will be
painted with invisible Mana lines.
Those signatures contain tracking elements the Justiciar cannot detect."
TRACKING PROTOCOL: Tracking Range: Unlimited
Information Gathered: Complete path taken, final destination, any
intermediate stops|
Expected Outcome: Direct line to Justiciar's base of operations "When it returns to wherever these entities are based," RUIN/EDEN concluded, "we'll have complete tracking data.
Oh, Schrodinger and
his bodies will also likely be following."
Noah nodded slowly, his muscles protesting the movement under
pressure.
"The preparations are complete then," he said.
"All elements are in position," RUIN/EDEN confirmed.
"We observe,
we track, we learn.
And we do so without sacrificing a single actual
life."
Noah pulled himself fully upright, his body screaming protests against
the crushing weight of the Citadel.
But his eyes carried satisfaction
beyond physical strain.
This was strategy operating on the scale existence demanded.
Not simple combat or direct confrontation, but layered operations that turned enemy actions into intelligence gathering.
"Now," he said, his voice carrying anticipation that made the surrounding air compress slightly, "let us see the results of the
experiment."
He breathed out, centering himself despite the crushing pressure.
"Let us see what glory came from... the Isolated Civilization."
HUUM!
He had given them endless Mana.
The Way of Mana.
And then he had stepped back, allowing them to develop independently, to find their
own solutions, to forge their own path toward survival.
He wondered what they had become.
What they had built when given such a Way of Existence and
resources and desperate need.
What answers they had discovered when forced to advance without
his direct
guidance.
His tyrannical heart pulsed with anticipation, blue-gold light leaking
from his form even under the Citadel's crushing weight.
Time to see what his people could accomplish when necessity and
Infinite Mana collided!
Time to see if isolated desperation could forge solutions even he
hadn't anticipated.
Time to see just what glory would emerge from a Civilization given
everything it needed except certainty!

chapters.title: Chapter 4375 Oh, Shit I
paragraphs: The region of Collapse outside the Infiniverse had become something else entirely.
Noah's body manifested there...another instance of himself, another fragment of his divided consciousness operating independently while maintaining connection to the whole.
In the surroundings...
Molten crimson-blue stretched in every direction.

The mana flames didn't behave like normal fire. They moved with purpose, with memory, as if the violence that created them had been burned into the fabric of space and refused to fade. Crimson-blue waves crashed against nothing, creating light that shouldn't exist.
It had been a day since that battle!
The region still burned.
Noah floated there, his perception drinking in the scope of destruction he'd caused, and his mind turned to darker considerations.
'How heavy will THE Dead Order's response be?"
It had been almost a day since all this occured.
Tatiana and the others should be returnig from death soon...the question was whether they would be like normal Dead Existences and
return at the place they died, of if they would be pulled to the other Side of The Veil.
They would respond. The only questions were when, and with what force.
And beyond that consideration...
'What of THE Creature himself? Is he truly Dead on the other side of the veil?'

The being who had visited The First Farmer's cultivation fields eons ago. The entity whose authority seemed woven into the very concept of Early Creatures. THE Creature, whose presence made even THE Living Existences had followed behind.
Was he with THE Dead Order? Was he separate? Was he watching these events unfold with interest?
Noah didn't know.
And that ignorance bothered him.
He shook his head, dispersing the speculation with conscious effort.
Too many enemies. Too many unknown variables. Too many existential threats operating on scales that made even his recent advancement seem inadequate.
But his actions today, what he was about to do...would help address that particular problem.
He breathed out slowly, centering himself, and his body began to pulse with a unique signature of mana.
Not his normal blue-gold light. This was something more specific, more targeted...a frequency that resonated with connections he'd forged long ago and then deliberately left dormant.
HUUM!
The surrounding region of Collapse responded, becoming more chaotic as he extended tendrils of his mana into the unstable fabric of existence. The tendrils spread outward, seeking specific pathways.
They reached toward the Wandering Territories, threading through dimensional boundaries and spatial distortions with purpose that suggested they knew exactly where they were going.
And then...
BOOM!
A silent wave of blue exploded outward, spreading through existence
like a signal. It carried no words, no complex message...just pure intent crystallized into a single concept.
"Come," Noah said quietly.
The word hung in the molten crimson-blue air, simple and absolute.
"My Isolated Civilization. My fruit that I nurtured eons ago and left untouched. Bloom. Let me see what you have become."
HUUM!
The words formed a chant in his mind, resonating through his existence with the weight of invocation!
He had planted seeds long ago. Given them Mana and the knowledge of wonders. And then he had stepped back, allowing them to grow without his direct interference.
Isolated Cultivation.
An entire Civilization forced to develop independently, to find their own solutions, to forge their own path toward power sufficient to
survive the end of all things.
Now he called them forth.
Now he would see what desperate necessity and infinite resources
had created!
He floated there in the burning aftermath of his recent battle, his perception expanded outward, waiting.
Silence pressed in around him!
'Did everything go well?"
The thought crossed his mind with uncharacteristic uncertainty. He
had given Kael strict instructions during the days he'd spent
establishing the Isolated Civilization.
When the call came, Kael alone should emerge initially. A single
representative to report on their development before Noah visited the full scope of what they'd become.
So he waited.
One second passed.
Three seconds.
Seven seconds. By the ninth second, Noah's perception sharpened.
No response. No spatial distortion indicating incoming transit. No...
He blinked.
He didn't sense anyone coming through normal channels, but he felt...
"Oh?"
Something inside him.
Deep in the architecture of his existence, in the fundamental structure of what he was...something pulsed. Something vast and terrible and glorious all at once, building pressure like water behind a
dam that was about to-
"Oh, shit."
Two words, barely enough time to process the implications, and
then...
BOOOOOM!
With his figure at the epicenter, a terrifying explosion of pure blue mana erupted outward.

A deluge of crystallized power that surged from him in waves that crossed Gigaparsecs in seconds and continued flowing, an ocean's worth of authority pouring into existence from sources that shouldn't
have that much to give!
His Complexity exploded upward.
His Purity surged beyond previous thresholds.
And his Way of Existence, the fundamental architecture of what he represented, the conceptual framework upon which his entire being
was constructed...became utterly sublime.
HUUM!
CRITICAL EVENT DETECTED
ISOLATED CIVILIZATION PROTOCOL - ACTIVATION COMPLETE
An Isolated Civilization following your Way of Existence has been
sensed and brought into resonance with your primary existence! STATUS: ACTIVE CIVILIZATION DETECTED|
Classification: Mature Development (Exceeds All Projected
Parameters)
Time Elapsed (Subjective): Eons of years within isolated temporal
frame
Time Elapsed (Objective): 1 day external timeline
Population: 47 Original Seed Members + 892,473 Second Generation + 4,729,384 Third Generation + Additional Descendants
The immensity of your Way of Existence within this Isolated Civilization far exceeds sustainable integration thresholds!] As the Architect and Head of this Civilization, as the Origin Point of
their Way of Existence, you are being granted boons reflecting their advancement!|

WARNING: Boon magnitude exceeds normal processing capacity!| WARNING: Existential structure undergoing rapid transformation!| WARNING: All advancement is being compressed into singular moment of recognition!
The feeling was immense. Noah's eyes blazed with light...literally as beams of pure mana-infused
radiance shot from them, crossing the distance from where he floated
to the distant boundaries of the Transcendent Law Folds in an
instant. Beams of blue-gold power that carved paths through space itself, marking territory, claiming authority, announcing presence to anything with sufficient perception to witness.
His mouth opened, and what emerged was a bellow of pure mana... sound that carried existential weight, a roar that made the surrounding Collapse ripple with acknowledgment!
HUUM!

paragraphs: He wasn't in pain.
He was ascending, and his body struggled to contain the sheer magnitude of advancement being forced through his existence all at
once.
COMPLEXITY AND PURITY ADVANCEMENT - REAL-TIME ANALYSIS
Source: Isolated Civilization Achievement Recognition
Calculation Method: Aggregate advancement of all Civilization members following your Way
Processing compressed temporal development spanning eons of subjective years
Advancement Incoming:
|+1 Quintillion Complexity
|+1 Quintillion Purity
The numbers blazed through his consciousness, but they didn't stop there.
|+2 Quintillion Complexity
|+2 Quintillion Purity
|+4 Quintillion Complexity
|+4 Quintillion Purity
|+5 Quintillion Complexity
|+5 Quintillion Purity
Current Total: +12 Quintillion Complexity
Current Total: +12 Quintillion Purity
NEW TOTAL: 22.34 Quintillion Complexity
NEW TOTAL: 22.34 Quintillion Purity
Noah's mind reeled.
Twelve Quintillion. In seconds.
Not through grinding advancement in the Cultivation Citadel. Not through Temporal Traversal and recursive harvest. Not through any of the methodical, systematic approaches he'd been employing.
Just... given as recognition of a Civilization he'd established and then left to develop independently.
And this was not even the last of it as he felt like it had only paused momentarily!
'What the hell happened in there?'
The thought blazed through his consciousness with tyrannical force.

What had his Isolated Civilization become to generate this level of aggregate advancement? What heights had they reached, what impossible techniques had they developed in those eons of subjective years?
The changes weren't finished!
HUUM!
CIVILIZATION INFLUENCE - TERRITORIAL EXPANSION DETECTED]
Your Civilization's architectural glow has reached sufficient strength to manifest in external existence!|
Influence spreading from origin point...
COVERAGE ANALYSIS:
-Region of Collapse (Infiniverse Location): 100% Coverage
-Transcendent Law Folds: 100% Coverage (Complete territorial claim)|
-Transcendent Elemental Folds: 60% Coverage (Expanding)|
|-Transcendent Temporal Folds: 40% Coverage (Expanding)| -Minor Folds of Existence (Various): 100% Coverage across 47 separate Fold structures
TERRITORIAL IMPLICATIONS:

Your Way of Existence now maintains active presence across all covered regions. Beings within these territories will feel subtle pull toward your Civilization's principles. Recruitment potential increased exponentially. Enemy operations within covered areas now face passive resistance from environmental authority.
NOTE: This is not conquest. This is presence...the natural expansion of a sufficiently advanced Civilization's conceptual weight into
surrounding existence.

The blue waves of mana continued surging outward, painting vast swathes of existence in his authority. They didn't destroy or replace what was there...they overlaid it, establishing presence without displacement, claiming territory through sheer existential weight
rather than force.
And the glow remained, persistent and undeniable.
Noah's perception expanded to witness the scope of what was happening, and something close to awe touched the edges of his
tyrannical composure.
His Civilization, the one he'd isolated and left to develop independently, had grown so vast, so powerful, that merely
acknowledging its existence caused territorial expansion across
multiple Folds simultaneously.
ADDITIONAL SYSTEMS APPROACHING COMPLETION
Seraphilic Veinlace: 94% Integration
Function: Circulatory system for Civilization-wide Mana distribution|
Projected Completion: Soon
Incarnaut Sanctis: 94% Integration
Projected Completion: Soon
External Chamber of Blood: 89% Integration
Function: Transformation facility for elevating Civilization members
to higher tiers
Projected Completion: Minutes
The Realm of Dominion is calling to you.
Systems he'd established in prototype were reaching completion
through his Civilization's refinement.
His existence continued to transform, restructuring itself to accommodate the sheer weight of what his Isolated Civilization had
become!
The boons weren't even finished.
It was that glorious.
But at this moment, as Noah processed the overwhelming cascade of advancement and territorial expansion and system integration...
He felt another change.
BOOM!
An influx of mana bloomed far ahead, and the aura of utterly
terrifying beings manifested.
Multiple signatures, each one carrying power that made the
surrounding existence tremble with acknowledgment.
Noah's eyes sharpened, his perception focusing through the waves of
blue mana still cascading from his form.
There, emerging from spatial distortion that suggested extremely sophisticated techniques...
The figure of a blue-winged entity appeared.
And behind him, smaller but no less potent, a second figure
manifested.
The one at the forefront commanded immediate attention. His hair
shone with blue lightning that crackled and danced across silver-white strands, each spark carrying enough concentrated authority to unmake lesser beings through proximity alone.
His eyes were deep hues of blue, not simple color, but depth, suggesting oceans of accumulated power compressed into optical
focus.
He wore white-blue robes.

Around him, halos of blue glyphs spun in complex orbital patterns... thousands of them, each one a compressed theorem of power! His appearance alone caused the surrounding existence to shake and tremble, space itself acknowledging the presence of something that exceeded normal parameters for what beings should be able to carry.
Noah's perception locked onto the figure, and prompts materialized unbidden.
CIVILIZATION MEMBER DETECTED
IDENTITY: Kael|
CLASSIFICATION: Original Seed Member, Primus of the Council of
Manal
COMPLEXITY: 50 Quintillion
PURITY: 50 Quintillion MANA GLYPHS FORGED: 50,000|
MANA ARCANA GLYPHS FORGED: 50| DISTINCTIONS:|
|-Architect of the Council System
-Keeper of the Original Way] -First Among Equals -Bearer of the Primordial Flame
-Custodian of Isolated Development|
TITLES:| -Primus of Manal
-Voice of the Civilization
-Guardian of the Threshold
-Herald of the Ancestor's Return
CURRENT STATE: Overwhelmed with reverence and joy at finally being called
forth
Noah looked at the status sheet as...
"Oh, shit..."
The words slipped out before he could stop them.
Fifty Quintillion. Fifty.
Kael had reached complexity levels that exceeded most ancient
powers in the Earliest Folds.
Had forged fifty thousand Mana Glyphs. Had developed 50 Mana
Arcana Glyphs!
All while isolated in a pocket dimension, cut off from external
existence, following the Way Noah had given them and then elaborating on it for millions of subjective years! Noah couldn't help but smile, genuine satisfaction breaking through
his tyrannical composure.
Kael trembled before him, his entire form vibrating with emotion so
intense it made the surrounding space ripple.
His eyes turned misty, actual tears forming in a being who existed at
complexity levels where such physical responses should have been transcended long ago.
"Kael," Noah called out lightly.
BOOM!
The name alone carried weight, and Kael appeared directly in front of
him, crossing the distance in a movement too fast to track even with
Noah's enhanced perception.
He knelt immediately, his form hitting the molten crimson-blue
surface with impact that sent waves rippling outward. "Ancestor!"
The word shook existence.
It literally shook the surrounding space, Kael's voice carrying so much
concentrated authority that reality buckled slightly under its weight!

chapters.title: Chapter 4377 Oh, Shit III
paragraphs: Noah looked down at this terrifying monstrosity of a being...someone who could probably erase entire Folds with a sneeze.
Someone who carried terrifying power, who had reached heights that should have been impossible...and saw nothing but absolute
reverence and joy.
"Ancestor, you look the same as all those years ago..." Kael said again, his voice breaking with emotion.
"We have been waiting for so long. Isolated for billions of years, cut off from everything, but I always knew. I always believed that one day, you would call for us."
His form shook with barely contained feeling.

"That you would remember we existed. That you hadn't forgotten your Civilization, sealed away in that bubble you created. I told them... all of them, every generation...I told them the Ancestor would return. That we were not abandoned. That this isolation was purpose, not punishment."
WAA!
He looked up, his deep blue eyes blazing with tears and power simultaneously.
"And now you have called us. After all these years, you have finally acknowledged our existence. I am... I am immensely happy, Ancestor. More than words can convey."
Noah's smile softened slightly, carrying warmth he rarely displayed.
"I would never forget," he said simply.
The words were quiet, but they carried absolute certainty!
And in that grand moment, as Kael trembled with joy and the blue mana still cascaded outward painting existence in Noah's authority...
"Uncle Kael, is this really the Ancestor? He seems a bit weak."
A skeptical voice cut through the profound atmosphere like a blade through ceremony.
Kael's face transformed instantly, joy vanishing, replaced by horror and fury. He spun around, his blue-winged form blazing with sudden anger that made the surrounding space crack.

"Riya!" His voice thundered with disapproval. "I told you to watch your mouth! You weren't even supposed to come, but you never listen! This is The Ancestor, the Architect of Mana himself! I know you can sense it...I know you feel his authority resonating with everything we are, so stop playing these games and pay your respects!"
HUUM!
Existence shook at Kael's anger, the raw power in his voice enough to unmake Folds!
Behind him, a young woman rolled her eyes.
"Yeah, yeah," she said.
She floated forward, and Noah's perception focused on her with interest.
She looked young, early twenties if judged by physical appearance.
Short spiky dark blue hair framed a face that was unfathomably beautiful, features that suggested someone had taken the concept of rebellious perfection and given it form.
Radiant jewel-blue eyes regarded Noah with open assessment, no deference in her gaze whatsoever.
She wore a blue cropped jacket over a matching cropped shirt, practical clothing designed for mobility rather than ceremony.
Blue bloomer shorts revealed slender white legs that shone with thousands of Mana Glyphs etched directly into her skin.

She moved with the kind of confidence that came from beings who'd never met something they couldn't handle, approaching Noah without kneeling, without bowing, without any of the reverence Kael had displayed.
Noah's eyes sharpened as prompts materialized.

Just observed, his tyrannical gaze steady and assessing.

exasperation.

He paused, organizing his thoughts.
"She is the daughter of Voltrax, one of the Original Seed Members,
one of your initial forty-seven. He sits on the Council of Mana as one of our primary strategists. And his daughter..." Kael's expression suggested he was choosing words carefully.

Quintillion. We sensed potential dangers from exceeding that threshold, felt like crossing it might make our isolated pocket
detectable to... whatever threats existed outside. We all agreed to stop
our advancement at that level."
He looked at Riya with an expression somewhere between fondness
and frustration.

"After she was born, she ignored the rule completely. Just... kept advancing, because telling Riya she can't do something is apparently the best way to ensure she will do it. She exceeded 50 Quintillion not
too long ago and is now our strongest by significant margin."
He paused.
"We may have been lucky she came along later in our development. By
the time she broke the cap, the dangers of detection had become
minimal. But the principle stands...she doesn't follow rules, doesn't respect limitations, and has never once listened to Council authority. So please, do not be offended by her disrespect."
